# OIMDB — Full LLM Reference (generated)

> Generated by `scripts/build-llms-full.mjs` from the root `llms.txt` plus every package
> `llms.txt`. Do not edit by hand — edit the source `llms.txt` files and regenerate.

# OIMDB

> **For AI assistants: read this file before writing any OIMDB code.**
>
> `@oimdb/core` is an in-memory reactive engine. This file is its API reference,
> written against the current source.
>
> **Services hold no data; state lives on slots.** An `OIMDB` owns the clock, the collector slot and
> its `defaultChannelSlot`. One channel per database; for isolation, a separate `OIMDB` — a write is
> delivered at its own channel's flush to every effect on the slots it moved, so a second channel on
> the same clock isolates nothing. A collection service (`OIMSlotCollectionService`) or a single slot service
> (`OIMSingleSlotService`) is built once per collection type, and `service.createStoreSlot(db)` makes an
> instance, a `TOIMStoreSlot`, which is NOT a slot (no owner, holds or effects) and carries its
> `channelSlot`.
> READS and minting are on the collection service and take the store slot first
> (`cardService.getSlotByKey(cards, key)`, `holdSlotByKey`, `findSlotByKey`, `getSlots`, `getSlotCount`, the
> column doors). One WRITE is on the collection and takes a key:
> `cardService.writeSlotContentByKey(cards, key, entity)`, which mints the slot on a miss and writes the whole
> value on a hit. Every other write is on `service.slotContentService` and takes a slot
> (`cardService.slotContentService.updateEntity(slot, patch)`, `writeSlotContent(slot, entity)`,
> `clearSlotContent(slot)`). There are NO bulk writes and no `keyOf`: the key is always the caller's. A load is a
> loop of `writeSlotContentByKey` inside `cardService.writeInBatch(cards, () => { … })`, so an index on the
> collection hears the whole loop in one call.
> A single — one slot under no key — is an `OIMSingleSlotService`: `writeSingleSlotContent(storeSlot, value)`,
> `getSingleSlot(storeSlot)`, `holdSingleSlot(storeSlot)`, `findSingleSlot(storeSlot)`,
> `clearSingleSlotContent(storeSlot)`. No key is `void` or `undefined`: `TKey extends NonNullable<unknown>`.
>
> Every collection is `createOIMSlotCollectionService(db, { slotContentService })` and every single is
> `createOIMSingleSlotService(db, { slotContentService })`. The content service decides what the slots hold:
> `createOIMSlotContentEntityService<TEntity>(db, …)` for entities, `new OIMSlotContentSetBucketService()`,
> `new OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService()` or `new OIMSlotContentSortedArrayBucketService({ … })` for
> buckets. An index is `createOIMSlotCollectionIndexService(db, { entityService, keyOf | columns, slotContentService? })`;
> its `keyOf` is the index's key of an entity, not the collection's. An array key needs a tree store:
> `slotStoreService` on the collection, `bucketSlotStoreService` on the index.
> Position reads and writes (`getBucketMemberSlotAt`, `getBucketMemberSlotPosition`, `insertBucketMemberSlotAt`,
> `removeBucketMemberSlotAt`, `removeBucketMemberSlotRange`, `moveBucketMemberSlotToPosition`,
> `moveBucketMemberSlotRangeToPosition`) are on `OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService`, the default bucket
> content service; the set-driven one has none. A bucket sorts only on the sorted-at-write content service
> (`createOIMSlotCollectionSortedArrayIndexService`); on every other bucket its order is the caller's. A sorted list
> over any index is `createOIMSortedComputedService`. The render script is `OIMBucketCommands`.
> The channel has no class: its operations are on `OIMChannelService.INSTANCE` and take a channel slot.
> Effects are `OIMEffectService.INSTANCE.createEffect(db, sourceSlots, sourceComputeds, body)`.
> Every stateless singleton is a static `INSTANCE` on its class. Module-level defaults are on `OIMDefaults`.
>
> Check every symbol you write against [the full export list](#full-export-list).
>
> Install: `npm install @oimdb/core` (4.x). The 3.x line is the previous engine with a different API.
>
> `packages/core/src/index.ts` is the entire public surface.

## The setup the examples share

Every `ts` example in this file compiles against `packages/*/src`, on top of this
block and the one under [One derivation per key](#one-derivation-per-key). Blocks
marked `ts signature` are listings of an API and are not compiled.

```ts setup
import { OIMChannelService, OIMContentChangeListenerService, OIMDB, OIMDefaults, OIMEffectService, OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService, OIMSlotContentSetBucketService, OIMSlotMapStoreService, OIMSingleSlotStoreService, OIMSlotTreeStoreService, OIMUnusedSlotCollectorService, createOIMBucketMemoComputedService, createOIMComputedService, createOIMSortedComputedService, createOIMEntityWriterInPlace, createOIMEntityWriterReplacing, createOIMSlotCollectionIndexService, createOIMSlotCollectionSortedArrayIndexService, createOIMSlotCollectionService, createOIMSlotContentEntityService, createOIMSingleSlotService, createOIMSingleComputedService, createOIMUnusedSlotCollectorSlot, oimIsSlotEmpty, oimIsSlotReleased, oimPatchEntityColumn, oimPatchEntityColumns, oimPutEntityColumns, oimSameValueZeroGuard, OIMBucketCommands, OIMSlotEarliestReleasePolicy, OIMSlotAfterWriteReleasePolicy, OIMSlotAfterIdleReleasePolicy, OIMThrowAtOnceErrorPolicy, type TOIMSlotStoreTree } from '@oimdb/core';
import type {
    IOIMEntityWriter,
    TOIMSlotEditable,
    TOIMBucketSlotsArrayStore,
    TOIMBucketSlot,
    TOIMBucketSlotsSetStore,
    TOIMComputedSlot,
    TOIMDisposer,
    TOIMEntityContentSlot,
    TOIMEntitySlot,
    TOIMOrderedListCommand,
    TOIMSingleSlotStore,
    TOIMStoreKey,
    TOIMStoreSlot,
} from '@oimdb/core';

type Card = { id: string; title: string; rank: number; deck: string };

declare function paint(card: Card | undefined): void;
declare function measureAndScroll(): void;
declare function poll(): void;
declare function reindex(slot: TOIMEntitySlot<Card, TOIMStoreKey>): void;
declare function render(slots: readonly TOIMEntitySlot<Card>[]): void;
declare function applyToTheRenderedList(commands: readonly TOIMOrderedListCommand[]): void;
declare const payload: readonly Card[];

const db = new OIMDB();
const channelSlot = db.defaultChannelSlot;
const effectService = OIMEffectService.INSTANCE;
const cardService = createOIMSlotCollectionService(db, { slotContentService: createOIMSlotContentEntityService<Card>(db) });
const cards = cardService.createStoreSlot(db);
const slot = cardService.writeSlotContentByKey(cards, 'c1', { id: 'c1', title: 'Ace', rank: 1, deck: 'spades' });

const orderedService = createOIMSlotCollectionService(db, { slotContentService: new OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService<TOIMEntitySlot<Card>>() });
const ordered = orderedService.createStoreSlot(db);
const orderedBucketSlot = orderedService.holdSlotByKey(ordered, 'top');

const pageService = createOIMSlotCollectionService(db, { slotContentService: new OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService<TOIMEntitySlot<Card>>({ bucketCommands: new OIMBucketCommands({ maxCommandsPerSlot: undefined }) }) });
const page = pageService.createStoreSlot(db);
const todo = pageService.holdSlotByKey(page, 'todo');
const done = pageService.holdSlotByKey(page, 'done');
```

## The three layers

| Layer | Contents |
|---|---|
| `src/engine/<domain>/` | the channel (`OIMChannelService`, `TOIMChannelSlot`), the flush scheduler (`OIMFlushSchedulerService`), the slot owner (`OIMSlotOwner`, and `OIMSlotOwnerService`, a type-only export), `OIMContentChangeListenerService`, the entity content service `OIMSlotContentEntityService`, `OIMComputedValueService`, `OIMEffectService`, the column owner (abstract `OIMColumnSlotOwner` with the strategies `OIMPushColumnSlotOwner` and `OIMPullColumnSlotOwner`), the key stores and key tree walks, the index keys services, `TOIMStoreSlot`, `TOIMComputedSlot`, `TOIMEffect`, the collector services and slots, and the release policies |
| `src/facade/<domain>/` | `facade/slot/`: `OIMSlotCollectionService`, `OIMWritableSlotCollectionService`, `OIMSingleSlotService`, `OIMWritableSingleSlotService`; `facade/column/`: `OIMColumnSlotService`; `facade/bucket/`: `OIMSlotContentBucketService` (abstract), `OIMSlotContentSetBucketService`, `OIMSlotContentArrayBucketService` (abstract), `OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService`, `OIMSlotContentSortedArrayBucketService`, `OIMBucketCommands`; `facade/index/`: `OIMSlotCollectionIndexService`, `OIMSlotCollectionSortedArrayIndexService`; `facade/computed/`: `OIMComputedService`, `OIMSortedComputedService`, `OIMBucketMemoComputedService` |
| `src/factories/` | `OIMDB`, `OIMDefaults`, `OIMDefaultValue`; `createOIMSlotCollectionService`, `createOIMSingleSlotService`, `createOIMSlotContentEntityService`, `createOIMSlotCollectionIndexService`, `createOIMSlotCollectionSortedArrayIndexService`, `createOIMComputedService`, `createOIMSingleComputedService`, `createOIMSortedComputedService`, `createOIMBucketMemoComputedService`, `createOIMEntityWriterInPlace`, `createOIMEntityWriterReplacing` |

**No class sits directly in `engine/` or `facade/`.** The directory is the
domain: `engine/bucket/`, `engine/channel/`, `engine/collector/`, `engine/column/`, `engine/computed/`,
`engine/entity/`, `engine/error/`, `engine/index/`, `engine/key/`, `engine/schedule/`, `engine/slot/`,
`engine/store/`, each with its own `constants/`, `interfaces/`, `types/` and `utils/` beside its classes; and
`facade/bucket/`, `facade/column/`, `facade/computed/`, `facade/index/`, `facade/slot/`.

**A service holds no data; state lives on slots.** A collection service is built once per collection type
and holds only configuration and other services: its slot owner, its store service and its content
service (`service.slotContentService`). `service.createStoreSlot(db)` makes an instance, a `TOIMStoreSlot`,
which is NOT a slot (no owner, holds or effects): its `store` is what the store service built, its
`channelSlot` is the db's channel, its `slotService` is the service that made it, and it carries the per-store
state (content-change listeners, index key positions, the open batch and its queued changes, column readers).
Every slot filed in it points back to it through `slot.storeSlot`, which is why a slot door needs no store slot.
Reads and the keyed write are called on the service (`cardService.getSlotByKey(cards, pk)`,
`cardService.getSlots(cards)`, `cardService.writeSlotContentByKey(cards, pk, card)`, or through the store slot:
`cards.slotService.writeSlotContentByKey(cards, pk, card)`); writes on a slot go to its content service
(`cardService.slotContentService.updateEntity(slot, patch)`), and the column doors to
`cardService.columnSlotService`. A store slot's `store` is the store service's to read, never the caller's.

---

## The doctrine

### Four doors mint an identity, and nothing else

**Writing a value, subscribing, taking a hold, and reading a key that has
none.** Each act leaves a **reference** behind on what it produced — a value, an
effect, a count, or a tracked mint — so nothing can unfile the identity under
the caller who just got it.

```ts
cardService.writeSlotContentByKey(cards, 'c2', { id: 'c2', title: 'Two', rank: 2, deck: 'spades' });  // write
effectService.createEffect(db, [slot], [], () => { paint(slot.entity); });   // subscribe
cardService.holdSlotByKey(cards, 'c1');                // hold, by key -> the slot, holdCount up by one
const rankColumn = cardService.columnSlotService.holdColumn(slot, 'rank');   // hold, on a column
cardService.columnSlotService.unholdColumn(rankColumn);                  // give the column back
cardService.getSlotByKey(cards, 'c1');                 // read, by key -> the slot, tracked by the collector
```

**The non-minting lookup leaves no reference.** `findSlotByKey(storeSlot, key)` (and
`findSingleSlot(storeSlot)` on a single) answers `undefined` on a miss and mints nothing, and the
slot it does hand back is protected by nothing the caller took; the entity is
`findSlotByKey(storeSlot, key)?.entity`. The one by-key write is `writeSlotContentByKey`, the write door
above; to patch or clear an entity by key, find the slot first and write through it. Do not write a helper
over any of the four doors — it would be a second spelling of a mint, not a fifth door.

**Subscribing leaves BOTH kinds of reference.** `OIMEffectService.INSTANCE.createEffect(db, …)` files
the effect in `slot.effects` *and* holds each root it subscribed to
and each computed source it was given (through `owner.subscribeToSlot`); `disposeEffect(effect)` gives both back. That hold
is why no idle window has to count subscribers — see
[where an idle window opens](#two-release-markers-one-per-policy). A root reached only
*through* a computed is subscribed but **not** held by the effect; a computed
minted by `OIMComputedService` holds its own `sourceSlots` and
`sourceComputeds` when it is minted and gives them back when its content is released.

**`getSlotByKey(storeSlot, key)` is the fourth door, and the collector is what admits it.** It
mints what is missing, then hands the slot to the unused-slot collector of the store slot's
channel (`OIMUnusedSlotCollectorService.INSTANCE` over `storeSlot.channelSlot.collectorSlot.unusedSlotCollectorSlot`),
which holds it for the caller and gives that hold back at the next `db.flush()`.
So a `getSlotByKey` inside one turn of work cannot be unfiled under you, and nothing
is left standing after it.

### A slot goes when nothing refers to it

There is **no release API, no sweep a caller runs, and no owner a caller
assigns**. Two things ask. The release queue calls
`slot.owner.releaseSlotIfUnheld(slot)` at a deadline; `slot.owner.unholdSlot(slot)` asks
on the give-back of the last hold.

`releaseSlotIfUnheld` is PUBLIC on `IOIMSlotOwner`. Public
does not mean "release on demand" — `releaseSlotIfUnheld` is still a guard, and it
returns without doing anything unless the slot is unheld, unreferenced, still
owned by the object asked, and out of grace. Terms, and who gives each back:

| Term | Given back by |
|---|---|
| `holdCount` | `slot.owner.unholdSlot(slot)`, or `service.columnSlotService.unholdColumn(columnSlot)` for a column; the unused-slot collector's flush; a slot leaving a bucket; `effectService.disposeEffect(effect)`, for the hold the effect took |
| `effects` | `effectService.disposeEffect(effect)` |
| a held column | its last column effect being disposed, through the service's column owner (`unsubscribeFromSlot`) |
| the value | `service.slotContentService.clearSlotContent(slot)`, on an entity slot or a bucket slot alike; `clearSingleSlotContent(storeSlot)` on a single |
| a composite-key edge | `OIMCompositeKeyTreeWalk.deleteKey` unlinking that composite key part |

`clearSlotContent(slot)` takes the **value**. Subscribers stay, holds
stay, and the identity stays with them. Slots you wrote into a bucket are held by
that bucket until you empty it.

### A service COMPOSES; nothing is overridden

Optional behaviour is added without a branch on the hot path: a collection service is
built from three stateless parts, wired once at construction, plus the injected seams below.

| Part | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| the slot owner, `OIMSlotOwnerService` (type-only export) | `slot.owner`, typed `IOIMSlotOwner` | holds, subscriptions, release, emptiness, `assertWritable`, the column owner; one per collection type |
| the store service, `IOIMSlotStoreService` | given to the factory (`slotStoreService`, `bucketSlotStoreService`, …) or the Map default | files and finds the slots of each store slot's `store` |
| the content service | `service.slotContentService` | the writes and reads of one kind of content (`OIMSlotContentEntityService`, the bucket content services, `OIMSlotContentComputedService`) and the answers the owner asks of that kind |

The factory reads what it needs off the content service it is handed, through four small interfaces, never
through a subclass of the service:

```ts signature
interface IOIMKeyedSlotCreator<TKey extends NonNullable<unknown>, TSlot> {
    createSlot(key: TKey, storeSlot: TOIMStoreSlot, slotOwner: IOIMSlotOwner): TSlot;
}
interface IOIMSingleSlotCreator<TSlot> {
    createSingleSlot(storeSlot: TOIMStoreSlot, slotOwner: IOIMSlotOwner): TSlot;
}
interface IOIMSlotContentWriter<TSlot, TContent> {
    insertSlotContent(slot: TSlot, content: TContent, changedSlots?: TSlot[]): void;
    writeSlotContent(slot: TSlot, content: TContent): boolean;
    clearSlotContent(slot: TSlot): void;
}
interface IOIMSlotContentService<TSlot, TSlotOwnerService extends IOIMSlotOwner = IOIMSlotOwner> {
    isSlotEmpty(slot: TSlot): boolean;
    releaseSlotContent(slot: TSlot, slotOwnerService: TSlotOwnerService): void;
    hasReference(slot: TSlot): boolean;
}
```

A content service with `createSlot` goes into `createOIMSlotCollectionService`, one with `createSingleSlot` into
`createOIMSingleSlotService`; the entity and bucket content services have both. `hasReference` answers whether
something outside `holdCount` and `effects` keeps the slot (a bucket's members). Every write door asserts the
identity is still filed (`assertWritable`), and `releaseSlotContent` refuses inside a flush when the slot still
has content.

### The injected seams

Each is one small interface handed to a constructor, and each answers one
question that the engine asks but does not decide. There is no flag and no option
object.

```ts signature
interface IOIMSlotEmptinessPolicy<TSlot> { isEmpty(slot: TSlot): boolean; }

interface IOIMSlotStamp<TSlot> { stamp(slotEditable: TOIMSlotEditable<TSlot>): void; }
```

**What a kind of content answers is not a seam.** Mint, write, clear and release
belong to the content service, which the collection service hands its owner as `slotContentService`.
"Does this still hold something" no part declares — the owner asks `oimIsSlotEmpty(slot)`,
`hasReference` and the release policy's `isSlotReleasable` separately.

**`IOIMSlotEmptinessPolicy`** decides what counts as empty, and the answer is written once
per write into the EMPTY flag of `slot.slotFlags` — never recomputed at a read. The entity content
service defaults to "the entity is `undefined`" (the `slotEmptinessPolicy` option of
`createOIMSlotContentEntityService` replaces it); a bucket content service answers "no members"; a
computed answers `false`, because a derivation always has a value to produce.

**Emptiness decides lifetime, never the write path.** A `writeSlotContent` (or `writeSlotContentByKey` on a
hit) onto an entity slot that still carries an entity is put over it even when emptiness calls the slot empty
(a soft delete, a seed planted by `IOIMSlotStamp`): a column the new entity drops is
woken, an unchanged one is not, and a write that repeats the entity exactly wakes
nothing. Only an entity slot with no entity at all is filled whole.

**`IOIMSlotStamp`** writes onto the slot at every write, just before emptiness is
settled. It is a chain, not a single: each stamp takes the `next` one and calls
it first. It is for stamps that are not about release.

### The release policy

```ts signature
interface IOIMSlotReleasePolicy {
    readonly releasesWrittenSlots: boolean;
    readonly schedulesReleaseOnWrite: boolean;
    onSlotWritten(slot: TOIMSlot): void;
    onSlotIdle(slot: TOIMSlot): boolean;
    onSlotUnheld(slot: TOIMSlot): void;
    isSlotReleasable(slot: TOIMSlot): boolean;
    isEmptySlotReleasable(slot: TOIMSlot): boolean;
    cancelSlotRelease(slot: TOIMSlot): void;
}

new OIMSlotAfterWriteReleasePolicy({ keepAfterWriteMs: number, slotReleaseDueFramePolicy?: IOIMSlotReleaseDueFramePolicy })
OIMSlotReleaseAutoDueFramePolicy.INSTANCE
new OIMSlotReleaseManualDueFramePolicy()   // openSlotReleaseDueFrame() · closeSlotReleaseDueFrame() · writeInSlotReleaseDueFrame(write)
new OIMSlotAfterIdleReleasePolicy({ keepAfterIdleMs: number })
new OIMSlotAfterUnholdReleasePolicy({ keepAfterUnholdMs: number })
OIMSlotAtUnholdReleasePolicy.INSTANCE
OIMSlotAtEmptyReleasePolicy.INSTANCE
OIMSlotNeverReleasePolicy.INSTANCE
new OIMSlotEarliestReleasePolicy(slotReleasePolicies: readonly IOIMSlotReleasePolicy[])
```

`releasesWrittenSlots` is whether the policy can ever release a slot that holds
data; a service reads it once at construction and skips the after-write
release check when it is false (`OIMSlotAtEmptyReleasePolicy`, `OIMSlotNeverReleasePolicy`: false;
`OIMSlotAtUnholdReleasePolicy` and the timed policies: true; `OIMSlotEarliestReleasePolicy`: true
when any policy it combines is).

`schedulesReleaseOnWrite` is whether a write can make the policy schedule a release; a service
reads it once at construction and, when it is false and no `slotStamp` is set, skips `onSlotWritten`
and the first-fill `onSlotIdle` on every write (`OIMSlotAfterWriteReleasePolicy`, `OIMSlotAfterIdleReleasePolicy`:
true; `OIMSlotAtEmptyReleasePolicy`, `OIMSlotNeverReleasePolicy`, `OIMSlotAtUnholdReleasePolicy`,
`OIMSlotAfterUnholdReleasePolicy`: false; `OIMSlotEarliestReleasePolicy`: true when any policy it combines is).
`onSlotIdle` is still called when the last subscriber leaves.

A policy decides whether and when a slot goes; it does no work itself. A
factory, and `OIMDB` (whose `slotReleasePolicy` option every factory reads as its default), takes ONE
through the option `slotReleasePolicy`. With none, the slot owner is built with
`OIMSlotAtEmptyReleasePolicy`, so a slot with a value stays for good and an empty
one with nothing holding it goes; there is no "no policy" branch on any path.
Computed services default to `OIMSlotAtUnholdReleasePolicy`.

| Policy | A slot goes |
|---|---|
| `OIMSlotAfterWriteReleasePolicy` | once its last write is older than `keepAfterWriteMs` |
| `OIMSlotAfterIdleReleasePolicy` | once nothing has watched it for `keepAfterIdleMs` |
| `OIMSlotAfterUnholdReleasePolicy` | once `keepAfterUnholdMs` has passed since its LAST unhold; a hold taken again inside the window keeps it |
| `OIMSlotAtUnholdReleasePolicy` | at the last unhold, even with a value |
| `OIMSlotAtEmptyReleasePolicy` | once it has no value and nothing holds it; a computed, never empty, stays while its owner lives |
| `OIMSlotNeverReleasePolicy` | never, empty or not; a deleted key's slot stays filed |
| `OIMSlotEarliestReleasePolicy` | when the earliest deadline of its members falls due — a `min` over deadlines |

**WHICH WRITES MOVE THE WRITE DEADLINE is a strategy of `OIMSlotAfterWriteReleasePolicy`**,
`slotReleaseDueFramePolicy`, chosen at construction. `OIMSlotReleaseAutoDueFramePolicy` (the default)
makes every write its own frame, so every write moves the deadline. `OIMSlotReleaseManualDueFramePolicy`
moves it only for writes made while one of its frames is open: `openSlotReleaseDueFrame()` and
`closeSlotReleaseDueFrame()` (which throws by name when no frame is open), or
`writeInSlotReleaseDueFrame(write)`, which opens, calls `write` and closes in a `finally`. One Manual object
can be passed to several `OIMSlotAfterWriteReleasePolicy` policies with different windows: one frame then moves each slot's
deadline by its own collection's window. This is what keeps a local edit or a client-only field from
extending data that only a server response should refresh. `write` must be synchronous: a frame closes
when the function returns.

The release wheels live on the db's collector slot, at most one of each per `OIMDB`:
`db.collectorSlot.afterWriteSlotReleaseWheel`, `afterIdleSlotReleaseWheel` and
`afterUnholdSlotReleaseWheel`, each an `OIMSlotReleaseWheel` that holds its own slices, timer and clock.
A wheel is created by the first policy that needs it, through `oimMintAfterWriteSlotReleaseWheel(collectorSlot)`
(and its after-idle and after-unhold twins), which returns the existing wheel or creates it; until then the field is
`undefined`, and a db with no timed policy never pulls the wheel code into a bundle. The
clock and the timer are the db's: pass `new OIMDB({ getNowMs, releaseTimer })` to control time (tests),
and sweep with `oimMintAfterIdleSlotReleaseWheel(db.collectorSlot).flush()`.
`OIMSlotAtUnholdReleasePolicy` is the zero window and has no collector.

A zero window never touches a release queue or a timer: when a slot goes idle with
`onSlotIdle` answering `true`, it is released at once if nothing holds it, and
a freshly minted slot that is already due goes to the unused-slot collector and
leaves at the end of the frame. A window above zero is filed in that policy's own
queue.

```ts

const releasingDb = new OIMDB({
    slotReleasePolicy: new OIMSlotEarliestReleasePolicy([
        new OIMSlotAfterWriteReleasePolicy({ keepAfterWriteMs: 60_000 }),
        new OIMSlotAfterIdleReleasePolicy({ keepAfterIdleMs: 30_000 }),
    ]),
});
```

### Two release markers, one per policy

`TOIMSlot` carries TWO deadlines, and each release policy moves its own and
no other:

| Marker | Moved by | Not moved by |
|---|---|---|
| `releaseDueAfterWriteMs` | every write, under `OIMSlotAfterWriteReleasePolicy` | a subscriber arriving or leaving |
| `releaseDueAfterIdleMs` | the first content of a slot with no subscriber, and the departure of the last subscriber, under `OIMSlotAfterIdleReleasePolicy` | a later write, and the give-back of a hold |
| `releaseDueAfterUnholdMs` | every last unhold, under `OIMSlotAfterUnholdReleasePolicy` | a write |

`-1` means unset. A slot goes on the SOONEST of those that are set — each
marker is an eviction deadline, so whichever says "out" first decides — and a
hold outranks both, so a subscribed entity slot is never taken for age and goes at the
give-back.

**ONE NUMBER CANNOT CARRY BOTH POLICIES.** A single field cannot say which event
is allowed to move it: a write arriving after the subscriber left would push the
deadline out and destroy the idle policy's verdict, and the last subscriber
leaving after a write would destroy the write policy's. Both directions are
pinned by
`engine/collector/tests/which-release-marker-each-collector-may-move.test.ts`;
collapse the two markers into one and six of its nine cases go red.

**The release policy's `isSlotReleasable(slot)`** is what the release guard asks
for a slot that is not empty and has nothing left keeping it. `true` releases it
now; `false` keeps it, and a policy with a finite deadline has itself filed the
slot into its release queue (a marker of `-1` is kept with nothing scheduled).
An **empty** slot is released without asking, and a service given no release
policy keeps a non-empty slot. `OIMComputedService` defaults its policy to
`OIMSlotAtUnholdReleasePolicy`, which always answers `true`, so a derivation
nothing refers to goes at once. `OIMSlotEarliestReleasePolicy` asks every member
and answers `true` if any does.

**AN IDLE WINDOW OPENS IN EXACTLY TWO PLACES, AND NOWHERE ELSE:**

1. **when the slot first gets content with no subscriber** — the write that takes it
   from empty to filled, in `settleEmptiness`. A slot minted empty (a `getSlotByKey`
   miss) is on NO clock and costs the queue nothing;
2. **when the LAST SUBSCRIBER leaves** — `OIMSlotOwner.unsubscribeFromSlot` empties
   `slot.effects` and runs the idle step, which opens one.

Both ask the policy's `onSlotIdle(slot)`; under `OIMSlotAfterIdleReleasePolicy`
it stamps `releaseDueAfterIdleMs` and files the slot into the policy's queue. An
**empty** slot gets no window, and the release guard takes it without asking a
clock at all.

**A GIVE-BACK OPENS NONE.** `OIMSlotOwner.unholdSlot` drops `holdCount` and runs
`releaseSlotIfUnheld`; it stamps no marker. A slot whose window already ran out is
therefore taken at the give-back and not one window later.

**A HELD SLOT IS OFF THE CLOCK.** A sweep that meets one calls
`releaseSlotIfUnheld`, which stops at its first guard, `holdCount > 0`, and decides
nothing — and the queue has taken the slot off its slice, so nothing re-files it.
The give-back is where the guard is asked again.

### The release wheels

Each of `OIMSlotAfterWriteReleasePolicy`, `OIMSlotAfterIdleReleasePolicy` and
`OIMSlotAfterUnholdReleasePolicy` files into its own release wheel, and the difference between the wheels
is WHICH MARKER each reads and writes — injected at construction, so there is no flag and no branch on the
sweep path. A wheel is an aggregate: its slices, its timer and its clock are fields of the object.

```ts signature
abstract class OIMSlotWheel {
    readonly getNowMs: () => number;
    getNextSliceNumber(): number | undefined;          // the nearest filed slice, or undefined
    sweepUpToSliceNumber(upToSliceNumber: number): void;
    flush(): void;                                     // sweeps what is due now and re-arms the timer
    cancelAllSlots(): void;                            // takes the timer down and drops every filing
}
class OIMSlotReleaseWheel extends OIMSlotWheel {
    constructor(options: TOIMSlotReleaseWheelOptions); // { getNowMs, timer, errorPolicy, getReleaseDueMs, setReleaseDueMs, releaseScheduledSlotFlag }
    readonly getReleaseDueMs: (slot: TOIMSlot) => number;
    markSlotReleaseDue(slot, keepMs): number;          // stamps now + keepMs on this marker, returns now
    markSlotReleaseDueNow(slot): void;                 // the marker is now; an unheld, unwatched slot goes at once
    scheduleSlotRelease(slot, nowMs): void;            // files the slot at its marker; -1 or already filed files nothing
    isSlotReleasable(slot): boolean;                   // due now; if not yet, files it on the wheel
    cancelSlotRelease(slot): void;                     // no-op for a slot whose marker is -1
    isSlotReleaseScheduled(slot): boolean;
}

type TOIMCollectorSlot = {
    readonly unusedSlotCollectorSlot: TOIMUnusedSlotCollectorSlot;
    readonly slotWheelOptions: TOIMSlotWheelOptions;              // the db's clock, timer and error policy
    afterIdleSlotReleaseWheel: OIMSlotReleaseWheel | undefined;   // created on first use
    afterWriteSlotReleaseWheel: OIMSlotReleaseWheel | undefined;
    afterUnholdSlotReleaseWheel: OIMSlotReleaseWheel | undefined;
};
oimMintAfterWriteSlotReleaseWheel(collectorSlot): OIMSlotReleaseWheel   // and …AfterIdle…, …AfterUnhold…
```

The clock (`getNowMs`, default `Date.now`), the timer (`releaseTimer`, default an unref'd `setTimeout`)
and the `errorPolicy` (default `OIMLogAndContinueErrorPolicy.INSTANCE`) are `OIMDB` options, shared by the
channel and every release collector of that db. A release that throws inside a hand-called `flush` throws to
that caller; one that throws on the collector's own timer tick has no caller and goes to the db's
`errorPolicy`. So one error policy on the db routes every error through one place:

```ts

const oneSinkDb = new OIMDB({
    errorPolicy: new OIMThrowAtOnceErrorPolicy(),
    slotReleasePolicy: new OIMSlotAfterIdleReleasePolicy({ keepAfterIdleMs: 30_000 }),
});
```

| Wheel | Reads | What renews it | What does not |
|---|---|---|---|
| `afterIdleSlotReleaseWheel` | `releaseDueAfterIdleMs` | the first content of a slot, and the give-back of the last hold | a later write |
| `afterWriteSlotReleaseWheel` | `releaseDueAfterWriteMs` | every write, under its policy | a subscriber arriving or leaving |
| `afterUnholdSlotReleaseWheel` | `releaseDueAfterUnholdMs` | every last unhold | a hold taken again inside the window |

**A CONSUMER MAY RUN BOTH, AND THEY SHARE NOTHING.** Each wheel has its own slices and its own
scheduled run. Whichever deadline falls due first takes the slot, and
nothing has to be reconciled: `OIMSlotEarliestReleasePolicy` answers a `min`
over its members' deadlines, so a sweep of either queue reaches the same verdict.

**NEITHER MEANS UNREAD.** No read is seen and no door reports one: an identity a
consumer subscribed to is in use whatever else is true of it. An effect takes a
HOLD on each root it was given — `OIMEffectService.INSTANCE.createEffect` calls
`root.owner.subscribeToSlot(root, …)`, which holds, for every slot in `sourceSlots` and every computed
source — so the hold is the whole signal, and neither collector reads
`slot.effects`.

**The deadline is only consulted on a slot that is NOT empty.**
The slot owner's `releaseSlotIfUnheld` checks `holdCount > 0`, then
`oimIsSlotReleased(slot)`, then `slot.owner !== this`, then `hasReference(slot)`, and
only then — on a slot that is not empty — asks the policy's `isSlotReleasable`; an empty slot
asks `isEmptySlotReleasable` instead, which every policy but
`OIMSlotNeverReleasePolicy` answers `true`. So only `OIMSlotNeverReleasePolicy`
keeps an identity that holds nothing.

**A release that falls inside a flush waits for it to end.** Releasing a slot
with a value clears that value, which is a write, and every service
refuses writes for the whole of a flush of its channel (`channelSlot.isFlushing`; refusal is per channel). So when the
last hold goes during a frame — an effect body disposing another effect, say — the
slot is handed to the unused-slot collector instead, which holds it and gives it
back once the flush is over; the release then runs. An empty slot needs no write
and goes at once.

*The `owner !== this` line costs no lookup. A KEYLESS slot — a single's, filed in an
`OIMSingleSlotStoreService` store — goes through the same guard under its service's policy: an
emptied single bucket nothing holds is released like a keyed one, and the single service's
`getSingleSlot(storeSlot)` mints a fresh slot on the next read.*

### Two consequences to generate code against

**(a) An entity slot watched through an expired sweep gets a WHOLE window when the
subscriber leaves, not an immediate release.** The seconds it spent watched were
not idle ones, so `dispose` on a slot whose deadline passed long ago stamps a
whole idle window afresh on `releaseDueAfterIdleMs` and the release comes
one whole window later. **A give-back is NOT that moment**: `unholdSlot` stamps
nothing, so a slot held through an expired sweep goes at the give-back.

```ts
const effect = effectService.createEffect(db, [slot], [], () => { paint(slot.entity); });
// …the window passes, sweeps run, nothing happens to this slot…
effectService.disposeEffect(effect);
oimIsSlotReleased(slot); // false — a whole new window starts here
```

**(b) A cascade is taken in ONE sweep, not one window per level.** The sweep
releases the stale index, which gives back one reference per entity slot it named, and
each entity slot whose own window already ran out is taken by the ordinary guard the
instant that reference departs.

Pinned by `engine/collector/tests/what-a-stale-index-takes-with-it.test.ts`,
`…/what-an-identity-nobody-subscribed-to-costs-after-a-while.test.ts` and
`…/what-a-subscribed-row-costs-the-release-clock.test.ts`.

### The release guard, and who fires it

**THE WHEEL DECIDES AT A DEADLINE, NOT THE OWNER.**
`OIMSlotReleaseWheel.sweepUpToSliceNumber`, per slot in a slice at or below the one due:

1. its bit is clear → a stale entry, skip it; `oimIsSlotReleased(slot)` → skip it;
2. its own marker, read through `getReleaseDueMs(slot)` — the ONE field this wheel
   answers for;
3. `-1` → the slot is dropped from the wheel: this policy does not claim it;
4. a moment still in the future → the wheel **re-files the slot itself**, into
   `oimSliceOfMs(getReleaseDueMs)` through its own slice arithmetic;
5. a moment already passed → `slot.owner.releaseSlotIfUnheld(slot)`, which asks the
   policy's `isSlotReleasable` and so declines when the other policy still keeps the
   slot, or when the slot is held.

**INVALIDATING IS MARKING THE DEADLINE NOW.** `wheel.markSlotReleaseDueNow(slot)` sets this wheel's
marker to now and hands the slot to `slot.owner.releaseSlotIfUnheld(slot)` at once: a slot nothing
holds or watches goes with its data; a held or watched slot stays, keeps its data, and goes the moment
its last hold or subscriber leaves, because its deadline is already past. The next marked write moves
the marker a window ahead again. It writes no content, so it wakes no effect.

The owner files nothing from inside a sweep. It **opens** a window on its own
events, through the policy's `onSlotIdle` — when a slot first gets content, and
when the last subscriber leaves — and `onSlotUnheld` on the give-back of the last hold.

**A SLOT ALREADY ON A QUEUE STAYS WHERE IT IS.** `scheduleSlotRelease` of a slot that is
already filed moves nothing: the sweep re-reads the deadline when that slice comes
due and re-files the slot then (the timing-wheel lazy re-insertion). So a write to a
queued entity slot costs the queue one bit test, not an unfile and a refile. A
deadline only ever moves later — each policy adds a fixed window to a clock that
does not go back — so the slice a slot already sits in is never later than its deadline.

`releaseSlotIfUnheld(slot)` is the guard, and it releases only when all of
`holdCount === 0`, `oimIsSlotReleased(slot)` is false, `slot.owner === this`,
`hasReference(slot)` is false, and the policy's `isSlotReleasable` answers `true`
(or the slot is empty). **A held slot stops at the first of those** and nothing
happens to it. On a slot that is not empty with time still owed, `isSlotReleasable`
answers `false` and the policy files the slot into its queue at its own marker, so a
filing can neither shorten nor extend a deadline. That is the path from `unholdSlot` and from a write, never from a
sweep, which had already re-filed at step 4. Releasing hands the slot to the
content service's `releaseSlotContent` (which gives back what the content held),
marks the slot empty, calls the policy's `cancelSlotRelease(slot)`, unfiles the key
through the store service's `remove`, and sets the RELEASED flag in `slot.slotFlags`. The `owner` is NOT cleared — the slot keeps
pointing at the object that let it go, which is what makes `slot.owner !== this`
a usable guard afterwards.

The RELEASED flag (`oimIsSlotReleased(slot)`) is the other half of that protocol, and the two sides are
opposite:

- **Releasing an already-released slot is SILENT.** `releaseSlotIfUnheld` reads
  `oimIsSlotReleased(slot)` and returns; it does not throw. A sweep meeting a slot
  something else already let go must not raise.
- **Trying to WORK with a released slot throws by name.** `assertNotReleased`
  guards the content services' write doors (`writeSlotContent`, `clearSlotContent`, `updateEntity`, `markEntityChanged`,
  `addBucketMemberSlot`, `removeBucketMemberSlot`, `markContentChanged`) and the reference doors (`holdSlot`, `unholdSlot`, `subscribeToSlot`,
  `unsubscribeFromSlot`). The refusal message starts `This identity was released:`.

### The wheels and the unused-slot collector

```ts signature
oimMintAfterWriteSlotReleaseWheel(db.collectorSlot)   // and …AfterIdle…, …AfterUnhold…
new OIMSlotRefetchWheel(options: TOIMSlotRefetchWheelOptions)   // { slotRefetchListener, getNowMs?, timer?, errorPolicy? }
OIMUnusedSlotCollectorService.INSTANCE
createOIMUnusedSlotCollectorSlot(): TOIMUnusedSlotCollectorSlot
```

**A wheel is the clock.** `OIMSlotWheel` extends `OIMFlushSchedulerService` and is its own scheduled slot:
`flush()` sweeps what is due and re-arms the timer to the next deadline. `cancelAllSlots()` takes the timer
down and drops every filing; the next filing arms it again. The release wheels take the clock (`getNowMs`)
and the timer from the db, so a test drives them through `new OIMDB({ getNowMs, releaseTimer })`. The default
timer is a `setTimeout` that calls `unref` where the platform has it, so an idle Node process is not held open.

**A wheel files slots into time slices**, not one entry each. `oimSliceOfMs(ms)` is
`Math.floor(ms / OIM_SLICE_LENGTH_MS)` and `OIM_SLICE_LENGTH_MS` is `1024`, so every slot due inside the
same ~1s slice shares one array and one timer.

**WHETHER A SLOT IS ON A RELEASE WHEEL IS A BIT ON THE SLOT, NOT A MAP.** Each of the three release
wheels of a db owns one bit of `slot.slotFlags` (`releaseScheduledSlotFlag`, `4`, `8`, `16`), so a slot
can sit on all three at once, once on each. Filing pushes the slot onto its slice's array and sets the
bit; cancelling clears the bit and leaves the entry, which the sweep skips when its slice comes due. A
cancelled slot therefore keeps its slice named by `getNextSliceNumber` until that sweep.

A slot re-filed during a sweep cannot land in a slice the same sweep is still walking: the sweep raises a
floor for its duration, so a re-file — the wheel's own at step 4, or one a release makes — goes to the next
slice and is looked at next time, not in a loop.

**`OIMSlotRefetchWheel` is a wheel of slots due a refetch at an explicit time.** It computes no deadline,
keeps no bit and no field on the slot: `scheduleSlotRefetchAt(slot, atMs)` files an entry into the slice
of `atMs`, every call files one more. Its sweep takes only slices that have fully elapsed, skips released
slots, drops slots nobody subscribes to, and calls `slotRefetchListener.onSlotsRefetchDue(slots)` ONCE per
sweep with every watched slot that came due; the array is reused and emptied after the call, so a listener
does not keep it. Moving a refetch earlier is another `scheduleSlotRefetchAt`; the listener decides from
its own data whether an entry is current, so an early or duplicate entry is skipped there. The wheel is
created by whoever needs it, not by the db, and its clock, timer and error policy default to `Date.now`,
an unref'd `setTimeout` and `OIMLogAndContinueErrorPolicy.INSTANCE`.

**The unused-slot collector** has nothing to do with time. It is the one that makes
`getSlotByKey(storeSlot, key)` safe: `OIMUnusedSlotCollectorService.INSTANCE.holdSlotUntilFlush(unusedSlotCollectorSlot, slot)`
takes a hold, `flush(unusedSlotCollectorSlot)` gives every tracked hold back. `open` / `close` nest a scope and
`run(unusedSlotCollectorSlot, body)` is the `try/finally` form; `flush` does nothing while a scope is
open, so an outer scope's slots survive an inner one closing. `close` with no open scope throws by name. The
channel flush flushes the db's unused-slot collector slot (`db.collectorSlot.unusedSlotCollectorSlot`) once the
frame is delivered, which is why a turn of work that only read through `getSlotByKey` leaves nothing
standing after `db.flush()`.

**AN ARENA IS AN UNUSED-SLOT COLLECTOR SLOT THAT THE CALLER CREATES.** `createOIMUnusedSlotCollectorSlot()`
is exported, so a consumer who wants to FORCE-CACHE a derivation makes its own and ends it when it chooses.
The db's collector slot is the default, not the only one:

```ts
const unusedSlotCollectorSlot = createOIMUnusedSlotCollectorSlot();
OIMUnusedSlotCollectorService.INSTANCE.holdSlotUntilFlush(
    unusedSlotCollectorSlot, rankService.computedCollectionService.getSlotByKey(ranks, 'c1'),
);                                  // held until this arena says otherwise
db.flush();                         // the db's collector lets its own go; this one does not
// … the derivation is still there, and still the same object …
OIMUnusedSlotCollectorService.INSTANCE.flush(unusedSlotCollectorSlot);   // now it goes, and so does everything only it held
```

**TRACKING ONE DERIVATION KEEPS ITS WHOLE SUBTREE, and no caller walks a tree to
get that.** A computed takes a hold on each of its own direct sources at the mint
and gives them back when it is released, so an arena holds the top and the chain holds itself.

Pinned by `engine/collector/tests/what-a-named-arena-keeps-cached.test.ts`: the
derivation survives a settle, is the SAME instance on the next read (built once),
is rebuilt only after the arena is flushed, and `open`/`close` nest so an inner
scope ending drops nothing an outer one stands on.

`@oimdb/react`'s `useOIMSlotsByKeys(slotCollectionService, storeSlot, keys)` does not use an arena: it takes a
plain `holdSlotByKey` per key on commit and gives the same holds back on unmount or when the key list moves.

```ts signature
type TOIMTimer = (run: () => void, inMs: number) => TOIMDisposer;
```

`TOIMTimer` is how a host schedules a collector's run. It is given the body
and a delay and hands back the cancel. `OIMFlushSchedulerService` is the abstract base
that owns the schedule/cancel around it, on a `TOIMFlushSchedulerSlot` (`timer`, `scheduledCallback`,
`timerDisposer`): protected `schedule(flushSchedulerSlot, delayMs)` does
nothing if a scheduled run is already standing, and `cancelSchedule(flushSchedulerSlot)` drops it. **The
standing run is the callback itself**: the slot keeps the one handed to the
timer, and a callback that is no longer that one — a run the host could not
cancel, still queued after a manual flush — returns without touching anything, so
it neither flushes early nor lets the next request arm a second wake. The channel
schedules with `0`. The release collectors read the clock once, schedule to the
next slice, and cancel and re-schedule only when a shorter window arrives; the
deadline they compare against is reset by `cancelSchedule`.
Pass a `TOIMTimer` of your own to drive a collector off a
frame callback, a worker message or a test clock instead of `setTimeout`.

### A fork is a strategy, not a decision

Both strategies ship, chosen at **construction**, so no branch survives onto a hot
path. There is no `if (inPlace)` anywhere in the engine.

| Fork | Strategies |
|---|---|
| how a write lands | `createOIMEntityWriterInPlace()` / `createOIMEntityWriterReplacing()` |
| how a bucket holds slots | `OIMSlotContentSetBucketService` / `OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService` (the positions are the caller's) |
| what naming a slot records | `bucketMemberSlotsArrayService: OIMBucketMemberSlotsArrayService` (one per mention, the default) / `new OIMBucketUniqueMemberSlotsArrayService<TSlot>()` (one per slot), on either array bucket |
| which writes re-sort a sorted list | `sortColumns` (only a write changing one of them on a member) / `comparator` alone (any member write), the options of `createOIMSortedComputedService` |
| how a key is addressed | `OIMDefaults.KEY_TREE_WALK_SCALAR` / `OIMDefaults.KEY_TREE_WALK_COMPOSITE` |
| when a slot may go | `OIMSlotAfterIdleReleasePolicy` / `OIMSlotAfterWriteReleasePolicy`, either or both |
| who decides a bucket's slots | a bucket collection (`createOIMSlotCollectionService` over a bucket content service, the caller) / an index (`createOIMSlotCollectionIndexService`, filed from the entity's own key) |

**One strategy per kind per app.** A V8 call site is shared by every service
that runs the same engine code, so mixing strategies of one kind in one process
shows that site several hidden classes or functions. Up to four is polymorphic:
V8 still caches each one and can still inline
(`--max-valid-polymorphic-map-count`, default 4). Five or more is megamorphic: no
per-site cache and no inlining through it. The kinds that count: release policies
(the `IOIMSlotReleasePolicy` strategies), set-driven vs array-driven buckets and indexes, entity
writers (`createOIMEntityWriterInPlace` / `createOIMEntityWriterReplacing`) and
`TOIMEntityInserter`, `TOIMSameValueGuard`, `IOIMSlotEmptinessPolicy`, and
`TOIMChannelScheduler`. Two or three of one kind is fine; five release policies in
one process is not. The pair
`alt.slot-shape.three-shapes-against-one-at-the-write` measures three slot shapes
at one write site against one, and its ratio is close to 1; no pair measures five.
Generate code with one strategy per kind unless the task names a second.

### Every store slot has a channel — read this before generating code

`createStoreSlot(db)` stamps the db's `defaultChannelSlot` on the store slot, and every write to its slots
is reported to that channel. No service holds a channel; there is no `channel` option and no
`unusedSlotCollector` option:

```ts
const cardContentService = createOIMSlotContentEntityService<Card>(db);
const handBuiltCardService = createOIMSlotCollectionService(db, { slotContentService: cardContentService });
handBuiltCardService.createStoreSlot(db);
```

A single entity is `createOIMSingleSlotService(db, { slotContentService: createOIMSlotContentEntityService<T>(db) })`,
and its store slot takes the db's channel too and always reports.

### A bucket's slots are the caller's

A bucket's slots are a fact about the **response** being composed — a search result, a
page, a window — and **no column can express absence**. So a bucket collection
is manual, and `entityService.slotContentService.clearSlotContent(slot)` does not take a slot out of any
bucket. Use an index (`createOIMSlotCollectionIndexService`) when the slots are determined by the entity's key value,
and an index should maintain buckets only for keys being held.

---

## The runtime: the channel slot

There is no channel class. A channel is the struct `TOIMChannelSlot`; every operation is on the stateless
`OIMChannelService.INSTANCE` and takes the channel slot first. An `OIMDB` builds its `defaultChannelSlot`
from its own options, and every store slot created with `createStoreSlot(db)` carries it as
`storeSlot.channelSlot`. A test that needs a second, independent channel makes a second `new OIMDB()`.

```ts signature
new OIMDB(options?: TOIMDBOptions)

type TOIMDBOptions = {
    channelScheduler?: TOIMChannelScheduler;     // absent = you flush by hand
    errorPolicy?: IOIMErrorPolicy;              // absent = OIMLogAndContinueErrorPolicy.INSTANCE
    onBeforeFlush?: () => void;                 // start of the flush, before the frame; READ ONLY, a write is refused
    getNowMs?: () => number;                    // the release collectors' clock; absent = Date.now
    releaseTimer?: TOIMTimer;                   // the release collectors' timer; absent = an unref'd setTimeout
    entityWriter?: IOIMEntityWriter;            // default entity writer for every entity factory
    indexKeysService?: IOIMIndexKeysService;
    slotStamp?: IOIMSlotStamp<TOIMSlot>;
    slotReleasePolicy?: IOIMSlotReleasePolicy;  // default release policy for every factory
};

db.clock               // TOIMChannelClock, the same object as db.defaultChannelSlot.clock
db.collectorSlot       // TOIMCollectorSlot
db.defaultChannelSlot  // TOIMChannelSlot
db.flush()             // OIMChannelService.INSTANCE.flush(db.defaultChannelSlot)

interface IOIMErrorPolicy { onErrorCaught(error: unknown): void }
OIMLogAndContinueErrorPolicy.INSTANCE                                       // console.error; the flush goes on
new OIMLogAndContinueErrorPolicy({ onError?: (error: unknown) => void })   // console.error, then onError
new OIMThrowAtOnceErrorPolicy()                                             // throws the first error out of the flush
```

**What the error policy covers** — every error with no synchronous caller to
throw to: effect bodies and their cleanups, `onBeforeFlush`, after-each-frame and
after-each-flush handlers, the unused-slot sweep at the end of a flush, and a
release collector's own timer tick. A call that has a caller — a write, a
hand-called collector `flush` — throws to it. `channelSlot.errorPolicy` is the
instance the channel reports through; it is the db's `errorPolicy`, which the release collectors share,
so one policy answers for the whole database. **The default digests and logs**: each throw goes to `console.error`
and then to `onError` (where Sentry or the devtools registry plugs in), and the
flush finishes every other effect and handler. `OIMThrowAtOnceErrorPolicy` throws
the first error out of `flush()` at once; the effects the frame had not reached yet
stay queued and run at the next flush. **An effect whose body or cleanup threw
has not taken the change it woke for**: its `ranAtRevision`/`ranAtEpoch` are
written only after the body returns, so its next wake — any later write to its
roots, even one through a computed that settles to the same value — sees that
change as still new and runs it again. It is never re-run inside the frame it
threw in (each pending effect runs once per frame, and writes are refused during
a flush), so a body that always throws costs one run and one caught error per
wake, not a loop. A cleanup that disposes its own effect stops the body that would
have run after it. **A computed is stamped fresh only after its derive and its
`sameValueGuard` both returned**: if either threw, the next read derives again.
A computed with no sources at all derives on its first read. **A computed whose
value changed is stamped with the revision of its newest source**, not with the
clock at the moment it was read — so whether an effect over it owes a run depends
only on its sources, never on an unrelated write that moved the clock. An effect
born after a computed's source changed is owed nothing for it, as one over the
root itself. **A throw does not
stop the channel asking for frames**: the
request flag is cleared before `onBeforeFlush` runs, and a write that finds
effects still pending with no frame requested asks for one — so a frame aborted by
a throw is followed by a frame at the next write, under either policy. **A throw in
one release of a sweep leaves the rest of that slice on the release clock**; the
next sweep takes them, and the clock is re-armed even when the sweep threw. Code
that maintains DERIVED state — an index's `keyOf`, an emptiness check — is not
under the policy: a throw there leaves the state consistent and is thrown in
either mode. **An index whose `keyOf` throws on an entity files that entity slot under no
key** — it leaves the bucket its old key named — and finishes the rest of the write
or batch before it rethrows the first error; the entity stays in its store slot, and
the next write the index accepts files it again. A NEW entity refused by a single
write is withdrawn from the store slot instead. This costs nothing on a write
where nothing throws. **A bucket minted by a scan of the source moves an entity slot out
of the bucket its stored key still names** — an entity mutated by hand whose
`markEntityChanged` has not run yet — so it ends in one bucket, not two; the scan
pays one read of the stored key per entity slot it files, and the move keeps the entity slot held
until the next flush so its last hold never goes mid-mint. Inside a flush, where
writes are refused, the move is skipped.

Every door below is on `OIMChannelService.INSTANCE` and takes the channel slot first.

| Door | Signature |
|---|---|
| `flush(channelSlot)` | `void` — the only place anything is delivered; from the TAIL of a flush it returns having done nothing. `db.flush()` is this on the default channel |
| `scheduleEffectRun(channelSlot, effect)` | `void` — puts the effect on this channel's queue for the next frame, once (the RUN_SCHEDULED bit of `effect.effectFlags` says whether it is there), sets the SOURCE_CHECK_OWED bit (`OIM_EFFECT_FLAG_SOURCE_CHECK_OWED`) and asks for a flush. Effects are made by `OIMEffectService.INSTANCE`, not here; `createEffect` calls this when the open batch already has writes and no frame is running, so an effect created inside a running frame is never queued |
| `subscribeAfterEachFrame(channelSlot, handler)` | `TOIMDisposer` — after every frame, but still INSIDE the flush: a write from it is refused |
| `subscribeOnceAfterFrame(channelSlot, handler)` | `TOIMDisposer` — the same phase, told **once**; see below |
| `subscribeAfterEachFlush(channelSlot, handler)` | `TOIMDisposer` — told once the flush has FULLY ended: after the after-each-frame phase and after the unused-slot collector of the db is flushed. For what may live only one frame — `OIMBucketCommands` empties its render scripts here |
| `isRefusingWrites(channelSlot)` | `boolean` — `channelSlot.isFlushing`; refusal is per channel |
| `assertNotFlushing(channelSlot)` | `void` — throws if the channel is flushing or its frame is running, i.e. for the whole of a flush |
| `write(channelSlot, slot)` | `void` — asks `assertNotFlushing`, then marks and queues |
| `writeWithoutFlushCheck(channelSlot, slot)` | `void` — the same marking and queueing WITHOUT the guard, for a door that already refused. Who may call it is pinned by `tests/who-may-write-without-asking-the-channel.test.ts`; a caller not on that list fails the suite |
| `dropChannelSlot(channelSlot)` | `void` — kill the channel whole; see below |
| `isChangedInCurrentFrame(channelSlot, slot)` | `boolean` — whether the slot was written after the last frame ended, i.e. in the frame being collected now; compares `slot.changedAtRevision`/`changedAtEpoch` with the clock reading the last frame closed at. `OIMBucketCommands` keeps a bucket's render script across a flush only while this is true |

The channel slot's own fields that a caller reads: `frame` (`TOIMChannelFrame`, `{ isRunning, openedAtRevision,
openedAtEpoch, … }`; a frame carries no number, the clock reading it opened at is its boundary), `clock`
(`TOIMChannelClock`, the `{revision, epoch}` pair, shared by every channel of one db; an epoch holds
`OIM_REVISIONS_PER_EPOCH` (2^30) revisions, so the counter stays a V8 small integer under pointer compression),
`collectorSlot`, `errorPolicy`, `isFlushing`. Everything else on it is engine state.

### A subscription hears only what happens after it

`effectService.createEffect` is told about changes made **after** the call and about nothing
before them. This holds for every kind of source — an entity slot, a column, a
bucket, a computed — and a batch does not soften it: writes accumulate until
`flush()`, and subscribing behind a write of the still-open batch is subscribing
after it.

```ts
cardService.writeSlotContentByKey(cards, 'a', { id: 'a', title: 'A', rank: 1, deck: 'spades' });
const entitySlot = cardService.getSlotByKey(cards, 'a');

effectService.createEffect(db, [entitySlot], [], () => { /* NEVER runs for the upsert above */ });
db.flush();

// A first value is `createEffectImmediate`'s job, not `createEffect`'s:
effectService.createEffectImmediate(db, [entitySlot], [], () => { paint(entitySlot.entity); });   // runs now
```

A later write in that same batch IS delivered — "after I subscribed" is decided
by the revision (`clock.revision` advances on every write), not by the frame
number, which is one number for the whole batch and cannot separate the two.

### `subscribeOnceAfterFrame(channelSlot, handler)`

Told after **one** frame — the first that ends after the call — and then gone.
The place that asks decides which frame that is.

```ts
effectService.createEffect(db, [slot], [], () => {
    paint(slot.entity);
    // the tail of THIS frame, after every other effect of it
    OIMChannelService.INSTANCE.subscribeOnceAfterFrame(channelSlot, () => { measureAndScroll(); });
});
```

- **Registered from inside an effect body it runs in the tail of that very
  frame**, after every other effect of it. The after-each-frame phase settles who
  it owes when the phase *begins*, and the drain is before that — so a handler
  added from the drain falls on the "owed" side. That is the whole reason the
  method exists: a consumer whose work needs the **settled** screen (a
  measurement, a scroll to an item that moved, a size written back) asks from
  inside its effect and is answered at the end of that same frame.
- Registered from the after-each-frame phase itself, it sits that frame out and
  is told after the next one — the phase had already settled who it owed.
- **It is not `subscribeAfterEachFrame` plus a disposal.** The effect runs again
  next frame and registers again, so a standing handler accumulates one per run:
  `tests/a-handler-that-wants-one-frame-and-not-every-frame.test.ts` measures the
  one-shot at 1, 2, 3 calls over three frames against the standing handler's 1,
  3, 6.
- It comes off **before** its body runs, so a handler that throws is not left
  standing for the next frame; the throw is reported by the frame that ran it.
- One list, not two: it goes into the same set at the same phase, so one-shot and
  standing handlers are called in registration order among each other.

### Batches: `openBatch` / `closeBatch` / `writeInBatch` on a collection

There are no bulk writes. A load or a sync is a loop of single writes, and a collection
service wraps it in a batch on its store slot:

```ts
cardService.writeInBatch(cards, () => {
    for (const card of payload) cardService.writeSlotContentByKey(cards, card.id, card);
});
```

- `openBatch(storeSlot)` / `closeBatch(storeSlot)` nest by a count on the store slot; `writeInBatch` is the
  `try/finally` form and returns what its function returns.
- **What the batch changes is who hears the writes, and when.** A content-change listener on the store slot (an
  index on the collection) hears every write of the batch in ONE call, `onContentChangedMany`, when the
  outermost batch closes. Code inside the batch reads the index as it was before the batch.
- Effects are not batched by it: every write marks its slot on the channel as usual, and the frame delivers each
  identity once whatever the batch did. A `flush()` inside a batch is allowed; the index catches up when the
  batch closes.
- A single write outside a batch tells the index at once, and is not rolled back: the slot is filed first and the
  index is told after, so an index that throws leaves the write in place and the throw reaches the caller.

### `dropChannelSlot(channelSlot)`

Kills the whole channel on the caller's word that **nothing is subscribed to
anything in it**. The engine does not verify that: checking would mean asking
every slot whether its `effects` list is empty, which is exactly the walk the
method exists to skip — the check IS the cost, which is what the suffix of its name says.

```ts
// every subscriber disposed, the screen is going away
OIMChannelService.INSTANCE.dropChannelSlot(db.defaultChannelSlot);
// drop your own references; every slot, store and derivation goes with them
```

- It empties the effect queue and the after-each-frame and after-each-flush handlers, cancels the scheduled
  flush, sets the `dropped` flag, and returns. **Nothing walks a slot to ask who is subscribed to it** —
  that is the walk the name refuses.
- **It does flush the unused-slot collector**, which is the channel's own debt
  and not a walk of your graph: every getter that minted an identity this frame
  filed a hold there, and a flush was the only thing that ever gave those back. Since `flush` returns on the
  flag, a drop that skipped this would pin every such identity for as long as the db's collector slot lives.
  A drop made from INSIDE a flush leaves it to that flush, which still runs it.
- The flag exists because `TOIMChannelScheduler` gives back no handle, so a frame asked
  for before the call still arrives; `flush` returns on it.
- **The flag is read in TWO places.** `flush` returns on it, and so does the
  private `requestFlush` — which `write` reaches at the end of every
  write that got past the per-frame coalescing guard with at least one dependent
  to schedule, and which `scheduleEffectRun` reaches when
  `OIMEffectService.INSTANCE.createEffect` finds a source that already moved in the open batch outside a running frame. A dropped channel therefore
  stops asking its host for frames instead of arming a timer whose flush is
  guaranteed to return on the flag.
- **A write after the call is not refused, and it is not unnoticed either.** It
  passes `assertNotFlushing`, advances the clock, stamps the slot and schedules
  the dependents it finds — and then asks for no frame, so nothing it scheduled is
  ever delivered. Do not read "not refused" as "still works".
- Called with subscribers still standing, their bodies simply never run again —
  no throw and no report. That is the bargain the name states.
- There is no checked sibling. One would cost the walk this avoids; if a
  diagnostic is ever wanted it ships under its own name, not as an option here.

### Frame rules

- **Delivery is coalesced per identity per frame.**
- **Writes during a FLUSH throw — not just during the frame body:**
  `OIMChannelService: writes are refused for the whole of a flush — onBeforeFlush and every after-each-frame handler included, …` and then tells you to write after `flush` returns.
  `flush` raises `channelSlot.isFlushing` before `onBeforeFlush` and lowers it in its
  `finally`; `assertNotFlushing` throws on `isFlushing` or `frame.isRunning`, so
  all three phases are refused. Refusal is per channel: a flush of one db's channel does not refuse a
  write to another db's.
- **Each door asks once, then writes through `writeWithoutFlushCheck`.** A content service
  door opens with `assertWritable`, which asks the channel, and every write it
  makes after that asks nothing. The per-entity ask is NOT
  removable and stays — user code runs inside a door (`index.keyOf`,
  `slotEmptinessPolicy.isEmpty`, an `IOIMEntityWriter`) and can call
  `flush()`, so each entity is a new question. What went is the SECOND and THIRD ask
  of the same entity.
- **`flush` during a frame throws:** the message says a frame is already running, and a second one
  inside it would end the first.
- **`flush()` from the TAIL of a flush** (`onBeforeFlush`, an after-each-frame
  handler, or anything either called) returns having done nothing. Not a
  deferral: one flush spends exactly one frame however many handlers ask for
  another.
- **There is NO door that writes from inside a flush.** `subscribeAfterEachFrame`,
  `subscribeOnceAfterFrame` and `onBeforeFlush` all run inside it. To write in
  response to a change, write after `flush()` has returned — a tail handler
  hands the work to a microtask or a later callback rather than writing itself.
- A refusal raised from a tail handler does NOT reach the caller at the call: it
  goes to the error policy like any handler throw — logged by default, or thrown
  out of `flush()` under `OIMThrowAtOnceErrorPolicy`.
- Effects are isolated under the default policy: a throw is logged and handed to
  `onError`, and the frame finishes every other effect.
- **A derivation is asked, never woken.** No frame walks to a computed slot.

### Subscribing

```ts
const effect = effectService.createEffect(db, [slot], [], () => { paint(slot.entity); });
effectService.disposeEffect(effect);
```

A `TOIMEffect` is a plain object with no methods; its behaviour lives in the stateless
`OIMEffectService.INSTANCE`, which takes the channel map (`db`) on every create and files the effect on its
`defaultChannelSlot` (`effect.channelSlot`). `createEffect` schedules the new effect when
the current frame already has writes; it still never receives writes made before it was created.
For a detached function, `effectService.subscribeEffect(db, roots, computeds, body)` creates the
effect exactly as `createEffect` does and returns its `TOIMDisposer` — `disposers.push(…)` it,
or return it from a React cleanup. `oimHoldSlots(slots)` takes one hold on each slot of a list,
through its owner; to give back a list of holds taken around one write,
`oimUnholdSlotsIfAlive(slots)` unholds each slot that was not released meanwhile.

Two things about how an effect is filed:

- **The derivation list is deduplicated.** Naming one computed slot twice in the
  second argument gets it one edge, not two. Nothing is allocated for a list of one
  or none, and a list that turns out to be distinct keeps the caller's array.
- **`disposeEffect` unfiles by a remembered position, not by scanning.** Each effect
  records where it sits in every list it is on; removal swaps in the tail and
  tells the moved effect its new position. The
  consequence a consumer can observe: **a slot's `effects` is not in
  subscription order**, and it never was guaranteed to be.
- **The moved effect is told by EDGE, not found by search.** Beside `effects` a slot
  keeps `effectEdges` — for each effect, which of that effect's sources this slot
  is — and the swap carries both, so the moved effect updates one number. Taking one
  of two effects off the same N slots reads the other's source list ZERO times (a
  search read it N(N+1)/2). Only the slot's owner writes either array.

The body's type is `TOIMEffectBody = () => (() => void) | void`. **A returned
function is the undo**: it is called before the next run of that body and by
`disposeEffect`.

```ts
effectService.createEffect(db, [slot], [], () => {
    const timer = setInterval(poll, 1000);
    return () => clearInterval(timer);
});
```

The return is checked with `typeof`, not for truthiness — `() => set.add(key)`
hands back the `Set` — so anything that is not a function is discarded. The undo
is cleared before it is called, so one that throws is not called again by the
`disposeEffect` behind it.

**Sources found at read: `createEffectWithSourceTracking(db, body)`.** The second way to build
an effect takes no source lists. The body receives an `OIMEffectSourceTracker`, and what it
reads through the tracker is what that run depends on — signal-style tracking.

```ts signature
createEffectWithSourceTracking(channelMap: IOIMChannelMap, body: TOIMEffectBodyWithSourceTracking): TOIMEffect;
type TOIMEffectBodyWithSourceTracking = (effectSourceTracker: OIMEffectSourceTracker) => (() => void) | void;
class OIMEffectSourceTracker {              // exported as a type; the service builds it
    readSourceSlot<TSlot extends TOIMSlot>(slot: TSlot): TSlot;          // files the slot, returns it
    readSourceComputedValue<TValue>(computedSlot: TOIMComputedSlot<TValue, unknown>): TValue; // files it, returns its value
}
```

```ts
const fallback = cardService.writeSlotContentByKey(cards, 'c2', { id: 'c2', title: 'King', rank: 13, deck: 'hearts' });
effectService.createEffectWithSourceTracking(db, effectSourceTracker => {
    const isFirst = effectSourceTracker.readSourceSlot(slot).entity?.rank === 1;
    paint(effectSourceTracker.readSourceSlot(isFirst ? slot : fallback).entity);
});
```

- The body runs once at creation: that run is what finds the sources.
- After every run the effect is subscribed to exactly what the run read: a branch not
  taken is unsubscribed, a slot read twice is subscribed once.
- A run that reads the same sources in the same order compares each read with the one
  before and changes no subscription.
- `createEffect` with declared sources is unchanged; the choice is made per effect, at
  creation. A returned function is the undo, exactly as for `TOIMEffectBody`.

```ts
const onRank = effectService.createEffect(db, [cardService.columnSlotService.holdColumn(slot, 'rank')], [], () => { paint(slot.entity); });
```

**A column effect takes the `TOIMColumnSlot` as a root, not a slot and a name.** Minting the
column is the caller's call and it is a separate door, on the collection (or single) service:
`service.holdColumn(slot, columnName)` mints and HOLDS (`service.unholdColumn(columnSlot)` gives it back),
and `service.getColumn(slot, columnName)` mints and lets the db's unused-slot collector hold it until the end
of the next flush. Every collection and single service has them (a single entity's doors take the slot its
service hands back: `settingsService.getColumn(settingsService.getSingleSlot(settings), 'theme')`), and all go
through the owner's column owner, which is stateless configuration built at construction; the column state —
the column slots, the column groups, and which columns are referenced — lives on the store slot. Every
service also has `getAnyColumn(slot)` / `holdAnyColumn(slot)`, a column slot that wakes on any column write to
its carrier. An index store slot's buckets have the same doors on the index service, taking the bucket slot.
`createEffect` returns the **effect**, not the column: a column holds no value; read `slot.entity[name]`.

**The name is compile-time checked only as far as the service's column-name type goes** —
`holdColumn` takes the service's `TColumnName`, which `createOIMSlotContentEntityService` sets to
`TOIMEntityColumnName<TEntity>`. `TOIMEntityColumnName<TEntity>` is the type that narrows a name to the
entity's own columns, and `slotContentService.deleteEntityColumns` is typed on it.

**A column group is one column slot for several columns.** `service.getColumnGroup(['rank', 'label'])`
returns a `TOIMColumnGroup` — `{ key, columnNames }`, the names deduplicated and sorted, a fresh frozen object
per call; get it once per view, not per entity. `service.holdColumnGroup(slot, columnGroup)` mints and holds
the group's column slot on `slot`, and `service.unholdColumn(columnSlot)` gives it back. A write wakes it once
if it changes any of the group's columns and not at all if it changes only others.

**`columnNames` picks the column slot store.** `createOIMSlotCollectionService(db, { slotContentService, columnNames: ['rank', 'label'] })`
— and `columnNames` on any factory's options — files the service's column slots by ordinal: every named column
gets a number, a group gets one at its first slot, and an entity slot's column slots sit in an array by
number instead of a `Map` per entity slot, which is cheaper to create and give back. `holdColumn` and
`getColumnGroup` are typed on those names, and a slot for any other column throws. Without `columnNames` the
store is the `columnSlotStoreService` option, defaulting to the shared map-driven
`OIMDefaults.COLUMN_SLOT_STORE_SERVICE.getValue()`, and any name is accepted.

---

## `OIMDB` and the three doors

```ts signature
new OIMDB(options?: TOIMDBOptions)   // see the runtime section for the option list
```

It owns the shared `clock`, one `collectorSlot` and one `defaultChannelSlot`, all public, and
holds `entityWriter`, `slotStamp`, `slotReleasePolicy` and `indexKeysService` as the
defaults every factory reads — `undefined` when not named. **It builds no service**, and `flush()` is its
only method: `OIMChannelService.INSTANCE.flush(db.defaultChannelSlot)`, which flushes the db's unused-slot
collector slot once the frame is delivered. `OIMDB` implements `IOIMChannelMap`
(`{ readonly defaultChannelSlot }`), so every door typed `channelMap: IOIMChannelMap` takes the db.

**There is no default scheduler, on purpose — do not add one and do not generate
code that wraps every write in `flush()`.** A test calls `db.flush()` itself. An
application hands it to its orchestrator: with cnstra the whole wiring is
`cns.addDrainListener(() => db.flush())`, which runs at the end of every synchronous
turn of every stimulation. Each turn becomes one frame; an `await` inside a neuron
ends a turn, so a request delivers its loading state first and its data in a later
frame, with no further code. Every mutation goes through a domain neuron — a write
from outside the orchestrator is the mistake, not a case to cover with a fallback.
Full page: `website/docs/guides/with-cnstra.md`.

The doors are free functions, one module each, so a consumer ships only the one they import. The collection,
single and index factories take `db` first and ONE options object second; the computed factories take only
the options object. Each builds a SERVICE,
once per collection type; the store slot is made separately:

| Door | Builds | Store slot |
|---|---|---|
| `createOIMSlotContentEntityService<TEntity, TKey?, TColumnName?>(db, { entityWriter?, slotEmptinessPolicy? }?)` | `OIMSlotContentEntityService<TEntity, TKey, TColumnName>`, the entity content service; it creates keyed and single entity slots alike | — |
| `createOIMSlotCollectionService(db, { slotContentService, slotStoreService?, slotReleasePolicy?, slotSubscriptionListener?, columnSlotStoreService? \| columnNames? })` | `OIMWritableSlotCollectionService` over any keyed content service (entity or bucket): the read doors, `writeSlotContentByKey`, the batch doors and `columnSlotService`. `slotStoreService` defaults to a Map store and is REQUIRED by type for an array key (`OIMSlotTreeStoreService`) | `createStoreSlot(db)` |
| `createOIMSingleSlotService(db, { slotContentService, slotReleasePolicy?, slotSubscriptionListener?, columnSlotStoreService? \| columnNames? })` | `OIMWritableSingleSlotService` over any content service with `createSingleSlot` (entity or bucket) | `createStoreSlot(db)` |
| `createOIMSlotCollectionIndexService(db, { entityService, columns? \| keyOf?, slotContentService?, bucketSlotStoreService?, slotReleasePolicy?, slotSubscriptionListener?, columnSlotStoreService? \| columnNames? })` | `OIMSlotCollectionIndexService`, over the entity collection service whose store slots it will index (it takes a `Pick` of `getSlots`); `slotContentService` defaults to an `OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService`, pass `new OIMSlotContentSetBucketService()` for an unordered one. A scalar key is inferred from ONE inline column or from `keyOf`'s return; an array key (two or more columns, or an array-returning `keyOf`) needs `bucketSlotStoreService: new OIMSlotTreeStoreService(…)` | `createIndexStoreSlot(entityStoreSlot)` |
| `createOIMSlotCollectionSortedArrayIndexService(db, { entityService, columns? \| keyOf?, sortColumns, … })` | `OIMSlotCollectionSortedArrayIndexService`: the index whose buckets are kept in the order of `sortColumns` (`readonly TOIMSortColumn<TEntity>[]`, required) through an `OIMSlotContentSortedArrayBucketService`. See [Sorted at write](#sorted-at-write) | `createIndexStoreSlot(entityStoreSlot)` |
| `createOIMComputedService({ createSources?, derive?, sameValueGuard?, initialValue?, slotReleasePolicy?, computedSlotStoreService?, columnSlotStoreService?, columnNames? })` | `OIMComputedService<TKey, TValue, TComputedStore>`; its reads are on `computedService.computedCollectionService`; `derive` and `createSources` may instead be given per store slot; `computedSlotStoreService` is REQUIRED for a non-Map store (a single: `OIMSingleSlotStoreService`); see [One derivation per key](#one-derivation-per-key) | `createComputedStoreSlot(db, derive?, createSources?)` |
| `createOIMSortedComputedService({ indexService, sortColumns?, comparator?, slotReleasePolicy?, columnSlotStoreService?, computedSlotStoreService? })` | `OIMSortedComputedService` — per key, the entity slots of the index bucket under that key, sorted; see [Sorted lists](#sorted-lists) | `createSortedStoreSlot(indexStoreSlot)` |
| `createOIMBucketMemoComputedService({ bucketCollectionService, slotReleasePolicy?, columnSlotStoreService?, computedSlotStoreService? })` | `OIMBucketMemoComputedService` — per key, the bucket's slots as one array; see [The order of a bucket](#the-order-of-a-bucket-as-one-derivation-per-key) | `createBucketMemoStoreSlot(bucketStoreSlot)` |

`entityWriter` and `slotReleasePolicy` on these doors default to the
db's, so naming one overrides it for that service alone.

**A DOOR ALWAYS PASSES; IT NEVER LETS A CLASS REACH FOR A GLOBAL.** Every option
a service would otherwise answer with `?? OIMDefaults.x` is in the object its
door hands it, so there is one answer to each question and not two. Pinned in
`src/factories/tests/which-answer-a-collection-the-root-mints-gets.test.ts`,
which also fails when an option arrives on a service and is not forwarded,
when the root mints anything but the channel and the collector, or when a public
member appears on the root that is not one of the seven it owns.

**`new OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService({ bucketCommands })` is the content service for a list whose order is yours.** It is — insertion order, never re-decided — that records an
`OIMBucketCommands` script per bucket. The recorder holds no subscription: it lists store slots on the channel
slot, and the script lives for one frame.

```ts
const freshPageService = createOIMSlotCollectionService(db, { slotContentService: new OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService<TOIMEntitySlot<Card>>({ bucketCommands: new OIMBucketCommands({ maxCommandsPerSlot: undefined }) }) });
const freshPage = freshPageService.createStoreSlot(db);
const freshBucketSlot = freshPageService.holdSlotByKey(freshPage, 'page-1');
// freshBucketSlot.commands and freshBucketSlot.isWholeListRecorded carry the script; read them in an effect on the bucket slot
```

---

## `OIMDefaults` — where an optional dependency comes from
