Every optional property of the factories falls back to an entry
on `OIMDefaults`. It is a class of static `OIMDefaultValue` fields and nothing else — never
construct one, never subclass it.

| Accessor | Type | What it hands back |
|---|---|---|
| `OIMDefaults.COLUMN_SLOT_STORE_SERVICE` | `IOIMSlotStoreService<string, TOIMColumnSlot>` | a map-driven store service for column slots; the factories pass it to every service they build without `columnNames` |
| `OIMDefaults.COMPUTED_COLUMN_SLOT_STORE_SERVICE` | `IOIMSlotStoreService<string, TOIMComputedColumnSlot>` | a map-driven store service for the column slots of computed services, keyed or single; the computed factories pass it to every one they build without `columnNames` |
| `OIMDefaults.INDEX_KEYS_SERVICE` | `IOIMIndexKeysService` | `OIMAppendingIndexKeysService`; the factories pass it when `db.indexKeysService` is not set |
| `OIMDefaults.KEY_TREE_WALK_SCALAR` | `OIMScalarKeyTreeWalk` | the chain-of-values walk |
| `OIMDefaults.KEY_TREE_WALK_COMPOSITE` | `OIMCompositeKeyTreeWalk` | the chain-of-identities walk |
| `OIMDefaults.STANDALONE_SLOT_OWNER` | `OIMSlotOwner` | the owner of a slot nobody filed |
| `OIMDefaults.ENTITY_WRITER` | `IOIMEntityWriter` | `createOIMEntityWriterInPlace()` |
| `OIMDefaults.ENTITY_SLOT_EMPTINESS` | `IOIMSlotEmptinessPolicy<TOIMEntitySlot>` | "empty means `slot.entity === undefined`" |
| `OIMDefaults.STORE_SLOT_LISTENER` | `IOIMStoreSlotListener` | `OIMNoStoreSlotListener`: hears nothing. Not a constructor option: every service reads it when it is built and calls `onStoreSlotCreated(storeSlot)` for each store slot it creates. A tool that wants to see every store slot sets its own with `setValue` before the first service is built; once one has been built, `setValue` throws |

**NOTHING IS CONSTRUCTED AT MODULE LOAD.** Every entry is an `OIMDefaultValue`
whose `getValue()` mints on its first call (`??=`) and hands the same instance back
for the rest of the process. A consumer that never reaches for a key tree walk never
builds one.

Each has a matching `setValue(value)`, which is how a process replaces a default
everywhere at once:

```ts
OIMDefaults.ENTITY_WRITER.setValue(createOIMEntityWriterReplacing());
```

**`setValue` THROWS ONCE `getValue` HAS HANDED THE FIRST ONE OUT.** `getValue`
marks the entry as handed out; `setValue` refuses after that, by name —
`OIMDefaults.ENTITY_WRITER has already been handed out, and whoever took it keeps
it …`, the name in the message being the field's upper-case name. Whoever took it keeps
it, so replacing it then would leave two implementations live in one process,
the older one inside every object built before the call, and the second half of
the program would disagree with the first about what a write does.

Setting it before anything reads it works, and so does setting it twice before
the first read. Each property is tracked on its own, so calling
`OIMDefaults.COLUMN_SLOT_STORE_SERVICE.getValue()` does not close
`OIMDefaults.KEY_TREE_WALK_SCALAR`. **Set every default you intend to replace at
startup**, before you construct an `OIMDB` or a service. Pinned by
`packages/core/src/factories/tests/what-a-default-replaced-too-late-does.test.ts`.

**Each default is its own module, so reaching one retains only its arm.** Every
default lives in its own file under `packages/core/src/factories/defaults/` with its
own `OIMDefaultValue`; a service reads the modules it needs and
neither key tree walk enters its bundle. `OIMDefaults` itself delegates to all of
them, so importing `OIMDefaults` retains every arm.
`packages/core/tests/what-an-import-retains.test.ts` pins it — *"a default is one
door to its own arm, and the defaults class to all of them"*.

---

## Entity services

**An entity collection is two objects: the content service and the collection service.** The entity content
service (`OIMSlotContentEntityService`) is the writes and reads of entities, built once per collection type
with its slot owner; the collection service (`OIMSlotCollectionService`) over it is the read and column doors.
Neither holds an entity: each `createStoreSlot(db)` is one instance of that type's store.

```ts signature
createOIMSlotContentEntityService<TEntity, TKey?, TColumnName?>(db, {
    entityWriter?: IOIMEntityWriter;                                   // db.entityWriter, then OIMDefaults.ENTITY_WRITER
    slotEmptinessPolicy?: IOIMSlotEmptinessPolicy<TOIMEntityContentSlot<TEntity>>;  // OIMDefaults.ENTITY_SLOT_EMPTINESS
}?): OIMSlotContentEntityService<TEntity, TKey, TColumnName>

createOIMSlotCollectionService(db, {
    slotContentService,
    slotStoreService?: IOIMSlotStoreService<TKey, TSlot, TStore>;      // Map; REQUIRED for an array key
    slotReleasePolicy?: IOIMSlotReleasePolicy;                         // db.slotReleasePolicy, then OIMSlotAtEmptyReleasePolicy
    slotSubscriptionListener?: IOIMSlotSubscriptionListener;           // OIMNoSlotSubscriptionListener
    columnSlotStoreService?: IOIMSlotStoreService<string, TOIMColumnSlot>; // OIMDefaults.COLUMN_SLOT_STORE_SERVICE
    columnNames?: readonly TColumnName[];                              // the ordinal column store over those names
}): OIMWritableSlotCollectionService<TKey, TOIMEntitySlot<TEntity, TKey>, TStore, TEntity, …>
collectionService.createStoreSlot(db): TOIMStoreSlot<TStore, TOIMEntitySlot<TEntity, TKey>, Partial<TEntity>, typeof collectionService>
```

**Each collection type has its own column owner.** It is stateless configuration built with the slot owner
over `columnSlotStoreService` (or the ordinal store `columnNames` names); the column state — the column slots,
the column groups, and which columns are referenced — lives on the store slot. The doors are on the
collection's `columnSlotService` (`getColumn`, `holdColumn`, `unholdColumn`, `getColumnGroup`, `holdColumnGroup`,
`getAnyColumn`, `holdAnyColumn`). The column owner has two strategies, chosen by the factory: write-driven
column slots, woken by the marks a write makes (`OIMPushColumnSlotOwner`, entities and buckets), and
derive-driven column slots, each a computed slot over its carrier (`OIMPullColumnSlotOwner`, computeds).

Example, over the `db`, `cardService`, `cards` and `slot` of the setup block:

```ts
const effect = effectService.createEffect(db, [slot], [], () => { console.log(slot.entity?.title); });
cardService.slotContentService.updateEntity(slot, { title: 'Ace of Spades' });
db.flush();
effectService.disposeEffect(effect);
```

Assembled with a store service of your own:

```ts
const baseCardService = createOIMSlotCollectionService(db, {
    slotContentService: createOIMSlotContentEntityService<Card, string>(db),
    slotStoreService: new OIMSlotMapStoreService<TOIMEntitySlot<Card, string>>(),
});
const baseCards = baseCardService.createStoreSlot(db);
```

The writer is omitted because the db and `OIMDefaults` supply it, and so is the column store. The slot stamp
is not an option of any factory: it is `new OIMDB({ slotStamp })`, for every collection of that db.

### Public properties

| Property | Of | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `slotContentService` | the collection service | the content service: the write doors on a slot |
| `columnSlotService` | the collection service | `OIMColumnSlotService`: the column doors |
| `slotService` | the store slot | the service that created it |

A store slot is not a slot, so nothing holds, subscribes or wakes it: there is no
`effectService.createEffect(db, [cards], …)` that hears the population. "Something in this population changed" is an
index over the store slot and a subscription to its bucket — the bucket's door
is written when an entity slot joins or leaves it — or a content-change listener on the store slot
(`OIMContentChangeListenerService.INSTANCE.addContentChangeListener(storeSlot, listener, readColumnNames)`,
removed by the same listener object). The slot owner is what `slot.owner` points at for every slot the type
filed, in every one of its store slots; `slot.storeSlot` names which store slot.

**THERE IS NO DOOR THAT HANDS BACK "THE ENTITY SLOTS THAT HOLD A VALUE".** A store slot
keeps no bucket of its own. To read the whole population, walk `getSlots(storeSlot)` — every
slot filed in that store slot, in store order — and skip the ones whose
`oimIsSlotEmpty` says they hold nothing:

```ts
cardService.getSlotCount(cards);                     // how many ids are filed, empty ones included
for (const filedSlot of cardService.getSlots(cards)) {
    if (oimIsSlotEmpty(filedSlot)) continue;
    paint(filedSlot.entity);
}
```

To have that answer MAINTAINED and subscribable instead of walked, declare an
index keyed on the entity's own id (`keyOf: (card: Card) => card.id`) and hold the key
you want. An index's bucket is an injected lifetime — a
`slotReleasePolicy` — so it is the consumer who says how long the
answer outlives its last reader.

An index maintains buckets only while they are held, filing entity slots from the source
store slot on every write by the entity's key value. The bucket is created on first
`holdSlotByKey` by walking the source store slot's slots once, and released on the last give-back.

**`holdColumn(slot, columnName)`** is on the collection's `columnSlotService` and takes a hold on a column slot;
`service.columnSlotService.unholdColumn(columnSlot)` gives that hold back. **`service.columnSlotService.getColumn(slot, columnName)`**
returns the same column slot without a hold: a column slot it mints is held by the
unused-slot collector until the end of the next flush, so `getColumn` is
the door that does not hold but tracks. `findSlotByKey(storeSlot, key)?.entity` reads the entity
itself, so it mints nothing: a miss answers `undefined` and leaves no slot behind.

### The doors every service has

**The read doors are the collection service's and take the store slot first; the write doors are the content
service's.** Every collection service (entity, bucket, index, and a computed's `computedCollectionService`) has
the read doors below; a single slot service has `getSingleSlot` / `holdSingleSlot` / `findSingleSlot` /
`hasSingleSlotContent` in their place.

```ts signature
class OIMSlotCollectionService<TKey, TSlot, TStore, TSlotContentService, TColumnName, …> {
    readonly slotContentService: TSlotContentService;
    createStoreSlot(channelMap: IOIMChannelMap): TOIMStoreSlot<TStore, TSlot, TPatch>;
    createStoreSlotFrom(sourceStoreSlot: TOIMStoreSlot): TOIMStoreSlot<TStore, TSlot, TPatch>;
    findSlotByKey(storeSlot, key): TSlot | undefined;
    hasSlotContentByKey(storeSlot, key): boolean;
    getSlotByKey(storeSlot, key): TSlot;
    holdSlotByKey(storeSlot, key): TSlot;
    getSlots(storeSlot): IterableIterator<TSlot>;
    getSlotCount(storeSlot): number;
    isSameKey(key, otherKey): boolean;
    openBatch(storeSlot): void;
    closeBatch(storeSlot): void;
    writeInBatch<TResult>(storeSlot, write: () => TResult): TResult;
    readonly columnSlotService: OIMColumnSlotService;   // getColumn / holdColumn / getAnyColumn / holdAnyColumn / getColumnGroup / holdColumnGroup / unholdColumn
}
// createOIMSlotCollectionService returns OIMWritableSlotCollectionService, which adds:
//     writeSlotContentByKey(storeSlot, key, content, changedSlots?): TSlot
// createOIMSingleSlotService returns OIMWritableSingleSlotService, which adds:
//     writeSingleSlotContent(storeSlot, content, changedSlots?): TSlot;  clearSingleSlotContent(storeSlot): void
```

| Door | Of | Signature | Mints? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `getSlotCount(storeSlot)` | collection | `number` | no |
| `getSlots(storeSlot)` | collection | `IterableIterator<TSlot>` | no |
| `findSlotByKey(storeSlot, key)` | collection | `TSlot \| undefined` — the store lookup alone; takes no hold and leaves nothing tracked | no |
| `getSlotByKey(storeSlot, key)` | collection | `TSlot` — never `undefined`; minted if missing, then tracked by the unused-slot collector | **yes** |
| `holdSlotByKey(storeSlot, key)` | collection | `TSlot` — minted if missing, `holdCount` up by one | **yes** |
| `hasSlotContentByKey(storeSlot, key)` | collection | `boolean` — **does this key have content right now**, not whether an identity is filed under it: a slot a read or a hold minted and nobody wrote answers `false`. It hands back no slot, which is why it can answer without minting, and it is not a read: the answer is about the past the moment it returns | no |
| `isSameKey(key, otherKey)` | collection | `boolean` — whether two keys name one slot here, answered by the store service (SameValueZero for a Map store, part by part for a tree store) | no |
| `writeSlotContentByKey(storeSlot, key, content, changed?)` | collection | `TSlot` — **total; always the identity it resolved or minted**. A hit writes the whole value through `slotContentService.writeSlotContent`, a miss mints and `insertSlotContent`s | **yes** |
| `writeSlotContent(slot, content)` | content | `boolean` — on a slot you already hold; the boolean is about the CONTENT | no |
| `clearSlotContent(slot)` | content | `void` — it takes the value, not the identity | no |
| `markContentChanged(bucketSlot)` | bucket content | `void` — re-settle emptiness and re-ask the guard after a write you made another way; the entity counterpart is `markEntityChanged(slot, changedColumns?)` | no |
| `slot.owner.holdSlot(slot)` / `slot.owner.unholdSlot(slot)` | `void` — the `IOIMSlotOwner` pair; `unholdSlot` on an unheld slot throws by name | no |
| `slot.owner.releaseSlotIfUnheld(slot)` | `void` — run the release guard; it releases nothing unless the slot is unheld, unreferenced, still owned here and out of grace | no |

**`releaseSlotIfUnheld` is PUBLIC and it is still not a "release" door.** It is public because the release queue calls it through
`slot.owner`, and it is a guard, not a command: on a held, referenced, foreign-
owned or in-grace slot it returns having done nothing, and on an
already-released one it returns silently rather than throwing.

**`writeSlotContentByKey` does not file a key whose content is refused.** On a MISS it
mints, writes inside a `try`, and on a throw runs the release guard on what it
just minted before re-raising — so the caller's error is the only thing that
leaves. The HIT path looks
the key up first and never mints, so a refused write on an existing key leaves
that key exactly as it was.

**REFUSED IS NOT UNCHANGED**, and the two get opposite answers:

| | What happened | What the caller gets |
|---|---|---|
| **Refused** | The write threw; **no content ever arrived** | The throw. A key minted for it is unwound — `writeSlotContentByKey` files nothing |
| **Unchanged** | The write **did** happen and the content was already there | The identity, like any other write. Nothing is unwound |

`writeSlotContentByKey` is **total**: whatever it decides about the content, it hands back
the identity it resolved or minted. A door that mints must leave a reference
behind, which is the one test that admits a door at all.

**`changed?` — the verdict, into an array you own.**

```ts
const changed: TOIMEntitySlot<Card, TOIMStoreKey>[] = [];
cardService.writeSlotContentByKey(cards, 'c1', { id: 'c1', title: 'Ace', rank: 1, deck: 'spades' }, changed);   // pushed exactly when the content differed
```

- **Optional, yours, and appended to** — never read by the engine, never cleared.
  The slot is pushed exactly when the write put in content different from what
  the slot held.
- A batch therefore comes out of one loop as the list of entity slots that **actually
  changed**, which is what a consumer owning a bucket this engine does not
  maintain needs.
- It is an out-parameter and not a return because the return is spoken for (see
  above), and a `{ slot, changed }` record would allocate once per write on the
  path this exists to make cheaper. What it costs a caller who does not want it
  is one `undefined` compare per write.

---

## Writing

The keyed write is on the collection; every other write is on its content service, `service.slotContentService`,
and takes the slot alone. There is no `keyOf`: the caller names the key. There are no bulk writes: a load is a
loop of single writes inside `service.writeInBatch(storeSlot, () => { … })`.

| Call | Signature |
|---|---|
| `service.writeSlotContentByKey(storeSlot, key, entity, changedEntitySlots?)` | `(storeSlot, TKey, TEntity, TOIMEntitySlot<TEntity, TKey>[]?) => TOIMEntitySlot<TEntity, TKey>` — **total**: a miss mints and fills, a hit writes the whole value |
| `writeSlotContent(slot, entity)` | `(slot, TEntity) => boolean` — the whole value onto a slot you hold; columns it had and `entity` does not, go |
| `updateEntity(slot, patch)` | `(slot, Partial<TEntity>) => slot` |
| `updateEntityColumn(slot, columnName, value)` | `<C extends keyof TEntity & string>(slot, C, TEntity[C]) => slot` — one column, no patch object and no walk over it |
| `clearSlotContent(slot)` | `(slot) => void` — the entity goes; the identity stays while anything refers to it |
| `markEntityChanged(slot, changedColumns?)` | `(slot, readonly (keyof TEntity & string)[]?) => void` |
| `deleteEntityColumns(slot, columnNames)` | `(slot, readonly TOIMEntityColumnName<TEntity>[]) => slot` — the named columns go |
| `service.writeInBatch(storeSlot, write)` | `<TResult>(storeSlot, () => TResult) => TResult` — an index on the collection hears the whole batch in one call |
| `service.findSlotByKey(storeSlot, key)?.entity` | the entity alone; mints nothing |

- **The store keeps your object by default.** Under the default `oimInsertEntityWithoutCopy` the
  slot holds the object you hand in, so with the in-place writer a later update edits that
  same object; pass `entityInserter: oimInsertEntityWithCopy` to store `{ ...entity }`
  and leave your object untouched. After an insert, change the object only through the
  content service (`updateEntity`, or `markEntityChanged` after a hand edit): editing it and calling
  `writeSlotContent` with the same object again wakes nobody, because no column reads as changed. `oimInsertEntityWithSanitizedCopy` also removes an own
  `__proto__` key: pick it for untrusted JSON.
- `updateEntity` takes a **patch** — named columns move, unnamed ones stay.
  `writeSlotContentByKey` and `writeSlotContent` take a **whole value**, and a column the new value does not name
  is removed from the entity.
- A write that moves no column wakes nobody.
- **`writeSlotContentByKey` always hands back the slot**, whatever the write changed.
- **`changedEntitySlots?`**: optional, yours, appended with the
  entity slots whose content was different from what they already held. One array reused
  across a whole batch is the intended use, so a
  pass over its slots costs the entities that changed rather than the entities that
  arrived. It is never cleared — you empty it.

```ts
const changed: TOIMEntitySlot<Card, TOIMStoreKey>[] = [];
cardService.writeInBatch(cards, () => {
    for (const card of payload) cardService.writeSlotContentByKey(cards, card.id, card, changed);
});
for (const slot of changed) reindex(slot);   // the re-sent entities are not in here
changed.length = 0;
```

### `markEntityChanged` — you mutated the entity yourself, now say so

```ts signature
markEntityChanged(
    slot: TOIMEntitySlot<TEntity, TKey>,
    changedColumns?: readonly (keyof TEntity & string)[],
): void
```

Every other write door computes what moved: the writer walks the patch
(`oimPatchEntityColumns`, `oimPutEntityColumns`) and puts each value through `sameValueGuard`. A caller who edited the stored object by hand
already knows the answer, and this door takes it instead of recomputing it — no
patch object, no copy, no per-column comparison. The shape is: mutate
`slot.entity`, then report it.

```ts
slot.entity!.title = 'two';
cardService.slotContentService.markEntityChanged(slot, ['title']);
```

- **The hand mutation already compiles.** `TOIMEntitySlot` declares
  `readonly entity: TEntity | undefined`, and `readonly` forbids REPLACING the
  object, not writing its columns — `entity.title = 'two'` needs no cast, only
  the usual narrowing of `| undefined`. `TOIMSlotEditable<TSlot>` is what strips
  `readonly` from the field itself, which is what assigning `slot.entity` needs.
- **With a list, only the named columns wake. Without it, every watched column
  does** — the column owner walks the slot's whole column store, and a
  column slot exists there only while something holds it or subscribes to it
  (the slot owner drops it otherwise, in `releaseSlotIfUnheld`), so "watched" is exactly
  what the store holds. **Pass the list.** The no-argument form is the convenient
  one and it gives back the per-column walk this door exists to skip.
- **An empty list wakes nothing at all** — not the columns, not the entity slot, not the
  store slot's listeners. `[]` is the caller saying nothing moved, so it returns before
  anything is marked: a write that changes nothing wakes nobody here too.
- **With either of the other two it wakes the entity slot and the store slot's content-change listeners**, so an
  effect on the slot itself and an index over the store slot both see a hand mutation.
- **It re-stamps emptiness** whenever emptiness can depend on the mutation — with no column list,
  on a slot whose `entity` is `undefined`, and on a content service with a `slotEmptinessPolicy` other than
  `OIMSlotEntityPresenceEmptinessPolicy.INSTANCE`, a release policy that releases written slots, or a db with a
  `slotStamp` — so a hand mutation that emptied the entity leaves `oimIsSlotEmpty(slot)`
  true rather than lying, and the release guard can take the identity when it should.
- **It refuses inside a frame**, through the same `assertWritable` →
  `OIMChannelService.INSTANCE.assertNotFlushing(channelSlot)` as every other write, and throws on a released
  identity.
- **The column names are type-checked**: `keyof TEntity & string` rejects a
  misspelt name, a bare runtime `string`, and a slot of another entity type.

---

## Write strategies

A **writer** is the operations that move an entity's columns, and nothing
else: it reaches no channel, takes no holds and knows nothing about lifetime.
Both strategies ship as factories; the fork is chosen once, as the content service's `entityWriter`
(or for every collection of a db, `new OIMDB({ entityWriter })`).

```ts signature
interface IOIMEntityWriter {
    readonly fillEntity: (slot: TOIMEntityContentSlot, entity: object) => void;
    readonly putEntity: (slot: TOIMEntityContentSlot, entity: object, changedColumnNames: string[] | undefined) => boolean;
    readonly patchEntity: (slot: TOIMEntityContentSlot, patch: object, changedColumnNames: string[] | undefined) => boolean;
    readonly patchColumn: (
        slot: TOIMEntityContentSlot, columnName: string, value: unknown, changedColumnNames: string[] | undefined,
    ) => boolean;
    readonly deleteColumns: (slot: TOIMEntityContentSlot, names: readonly string[]) => readonly string[];
    readonly clearEntity: (slot: TOIMEntityContentSlot) => void;
}

type TOIMEntityWriterOptions = {
    sameValueGuard?: TOIMSameValueGuard;
    entityInserter?: TOIMEntityInserter;
    putEntityColumns?: typeof oimPutEntityColumns;      // oimPutEntityColumns | oimPutEntityColumnsGuarded
    patchEntityColumns?: typeof oimPatchEntityColumns;  // oimPatchEntityColumns | oimPatchEntityColumnsGuarded
    patchEntityColumn?: typeof oimPatchEntityColumn;    // oimPatchEntityColumn | oimPatchEntityColumnGuarded
};

createOIMEntityWriterInPlace(options?: TOIMEntityWriterOptions): IOIMEntityWriter    // stored object keeps its identity
createOIMEntityWriterReplacing(options?: TOIMEntityWriterOptions): IOIMEntityWriter  // a new object per write that changed something
```

`entityInserter` is the first-write strategy: `oimInsertEntityWithoutCopy` (the default) stores
your object itself, `oimInsertEntityWithCopy` stores `{ ...entity }`, `oimInsertEntityWithSanitizedCopy`
stores a copy with an own `__proto__` key removed (for untrusted JSON).

`deleteColumns` hands back **the names that actually moved**, a frozen empty
array when nothing did — that list is what the entity content service routes to
column subscribers, and it is why a write that changes nothing wakes nobody.
**`putEntity` and `patchEntity` answer whether anything moved, and name the moved
columns only into the array they are handed**: one pass compares and writes (a put
then walks the stored columns the new value lacks), and with `undefined` they build
no list at all. The entity content service asks whether the slot has changed-column readers — the slot has
column slots, or its store slot has a content listener such as an index — and hands
an array only then, so a write of an entity nobody reads by column allocates no names.
The list it builds goes on to the listeners: an index wakes a bucket column exactly
when a member's value of it changed, left, or became `undefined`. The first write
into an empty slot tells listeners `undefined` ("everything"), not an empty list. `sameValueGuard` defaults to `oimSameValueZeroGuard` and is the
per-column comparison that decides "moved".

`putEntity` is PUT, `patchEntity` is PATCH (HTTP semantics). PUT makes the stored entity
the value handed in — changed columns written, columns the value lacks removed — in ONE
call, returning both sets of names; PATCH writes only the columns named. `writeSlotContentByKey`
of a key that already has a value and `slotContentService.writeSlotContent(slot, entity)` are PUT: a whole-entity
write that drops a column is ONE channel write of the slot, and the replacing writer
builds ONE new object.

Pick `createOIMEntityWriterReplacing` when something downstream compares by
reference — a React `useSyncExternalStore` snapshot, a memo, a shallow-equal
selector. Under `createOIMEntityWriterInPlace` the entity reference never moves,
so a value comparison never fires and a binding needs a counter bumped inside its
handler. Replacing allocates one object per changed write; in-place allocates
none.

Neither writer `delete`s: a column a PUT drops or `deleteColumns` takes away is
written `undefined` — into the stored object in place, into a spread copy when
replacing — so the entity keeps its hidden class, and the key stays in
`Object.keys` and `in`. A column holding `undefined` counts as absent — a later write that
leaves it out does not report it, and taking the entity away does not wake its
readers.

**Neither strategy reports anything.** Reporting is `OIMSlotContentEntityService`'s:
after the writer returns, it marks the slot on the channel and tells the store slot's content-change listeners
once for the whole write.

**A writer of your own** reuses the column walks both shipped writers run:

```ts signature
oimPatchEntityColumns(slot, patch: object, sameValueGuard, changedColumnNames: string[] | undefined,
    targetOf: (entity: Record<string, unknown>) => Record<string, unknown>): Record<string, unknown> | undefined
oimPatchEntityColumn(slot, columnName: string, value: unknown, sameValueGuard, changedColumnNames: string[] | undefined,
    targetOf: (entity: Record<string, unknown>) => Record<string, unknown>): Record<string, unknown> | undefined
oimPutEntityColumns(slot, entity: object, sameValueGuard, changedColumnNames: string[] | undefined,
    targetOf: (entity: Record<string, unknown>) => Record<string, unknown>): Record<string, unknown> | undefined
oimPutEntityColumnsGuarded(slot, entity: object, sameValueGuard, changedColumnNames: string[] | undefined,
    targetOf: (entity: Record<string, unknown>) => Record<string, unknown>): Record<string, unknown> | undefined
oimPatchEntityColumnsGuarded(slot, patch: object, sameValueGuard, changedColumnNames, targetOf)        // same signature as the unguarded walk
oimPatchEntityColumnGuarded(slot, columnName: string, value: unknown, sameValueGuard, changedColumnNames, targetOf)
```

Each compares every column through `sameValueGuard`, writes the moved ones into
the object `targetOf` hands back on the first move (the stored entity in place, a
copy when replacing), pushes their names into `changedColumnNames` when it is an
array, and returns that object; `undefined` means nothing moved or the slot holds
no entity. The put walk also writes `undefined` over every column the new value
lacks. Each walk is a strategy, an option of the writer factories (`TOIMEntityWriterOptions`), and each
ships two arms:

| Option | Default (unguarded) | Guarded arm |
|---|---|---|
| `putEntityColumns` | `oimPutEntityColumns` — skips neither `__proto__` keys nor inherited stored columns | `oimPutEntityColumnsGuarded` — skips both |
| `patchEntityColumns` | `oimPatchEntityColumns` — every enumerable key of the patch, `__proto__` included | `oimPatchEntityColumnsGuarded` — skips a `__proto__` key and a key the patch does not own |
| `patchEntityColumn` | `oimPatchEntityColumn` | `oimPatchEntityColumnGuarded` — refuses the column name `__proto__` |

Take the guarded arms, at a cost on every write, for values that can carry a `__proto__` key or are class
instances — `createOIMEntityWriterInPlace({ putEntityColumns: oimPutEntityColumnsGuarded,
patchEntityColumns: oimPatchEntityColumnsGuarded, patchEntityColumn: oimPatchEntityColumnGuarded })`, the
same options on `createOIMEntityWriterReplacing`. The writer decides only where the result goes — this one
stores every value frozen:

```ts
const copyColumns = (entity: Record<string, unknown>): Record<string, unknown> => ({ ...entity });

function storeFrozen(slot: TOIMEntityContentSlot, next: Record<string, unknown> | undefined): boolean {
    if (next === undefined) return false;
    (slot as TOIMSlotEditable<TOIMEntityContentSlot>).entity = Object.freeze(next);
    return true;
}

const replacingWriter = createOIMEntityWriterReplacing();

const freezingWriter: IOIMEntityWriter = {
    fillEntity: (slot, entity) => { storeFrozen(slot, copyColumns(entity as Record<string, unknown>)); },
    clearEntity: replacingWriter.clearEntity,
    putEntity: (slot, entity, changedColumnNames) =>
        storeFrozen(slot, oimPutEntityColumns(slot, entity, oimSameValueZeroGuard, changedColumnNames, copyColumns)),
    patchEntity: (slot, patch, changedColumnNames) =>
        storeFrozen(slot, oimPatchEntityColumns(slot, patch, oimSameValueZeroGuard, changedColumnNames, copyColumns)),
    patchColumn: (slot, columnName, value, changedColumnNames) =>
        storeFrozen(slot, oimPatchEntityColumn(slot, columnName, value, oimSameValueZeroGuard, changedColumnNames, copyColumns)),
    deleteColumns: (slot, names) => {
        const deleted = replacingWriter.deleteColumns(slot, names);
        if (deleted.length !== 0) storeFrozen(slot, slot.entity as Record<string, unknown>);
        return deleted;
    },
};
```

---

## Single entities

A single entity — one value under no key, such as settings or a session — is a store slot of an
`OIMSingleSlotService` over an entity content service; its store service is `OIMSingleSlotStoreService.INSTANCE`,
which files at most one slot per store slot. It has no key and no by-key doors: its doors name the one slot.

```ts signature
createOIMSingleSlotService(db, {
    slotContentService: createOIMSlotContentEntityService<TEntity>(db),
    slotReleasePolicy?, slotSubscriptionListener?, columnSlotStoreService?, columnNames?,
}): OIMWritableSingleSlotService<TOIMEntityContentSlot<TEntity>, TEntity, …>

class OIMWritableSingleSlotService<TSlot, TContent, TSlotContentService, …> {
    readonly slotContentService: TSlotContentService;
    readonly columnSlotService: OIMColumnSlotService;
    createStoreSlot(channelMap: IOIMChannelMap): TOIMStoreSlot<TOIMSingleSlotStore<TSlot>, TSlot, TPatch, this>;
    writeSingleSlotContent(storeSlot, content, changedSlots?): TSlot;   // minted if missing
    clearSingleSlotContent(storeSlot): void;
    findSingleSlot(storeSlot): TSlot | undefined;     // mints nothing
    hasSingleSlotContent(storeSlot): boolean;         // mints nothing
    getSingleSlot(storeSlot): TSlot;                  // minted if missing, tracked until the next flush
    holdSingleSlot(storeSlot): TSlot;                 // minted if missing, holdCount up by one
}
```

One service serves every single entity of that type: each `createStoreSlot(db)` is another one, and starts
with no value until something writes it. Its store slot is a `TOIMSingleSlotStoreSlot`, which is what
`@oimdb/persist`'s single-entity source takes.

```ts
type Settings = { theme: 'light' | 'dark'; zoom: number };

const settingsService = createOIMSingleSlotService(db, { slotContentService: createOIMSlotContentEntityService<Settings>(db) });
const settings = settingsService.createStoreSlot(db);
settingsService.writeSingleSlotContent(settings, { theme: 'light', zoom: 1 });
const settingsSlot = settingsService.holdSingleSlot(settings);
const themeColumn = settingsService.columnSlotService.holdColumn(settingsSlot, 'theme');
const themeEffect = effectService.createEffect(db, [themeColumn], [], () => { console.log(settingsSlot.entity?.theme); });
settingsService.slotContentService.updateEntity(settingsSlot, { theme: 'dark' });
db.flush();
effectService.disposeEffect(themeEffect);
settingsService.columnSlotService.unholdColumn(themeColumn);
settingsSlot.owner.unholdSlot(settingsSlot);
```

**The slot is reached only through the service.** `getSingleSlot(storeSlot)` hands back the live slot, and
mints a fresh one — tracked by the unused-slot collector until the next flush — when there is none;
`holdSingleSlot(storeSlot)` does the same and takes a hold. `writeSingleSlotContent` and `clearSingleSlotContent`
are the store doors, and every slot door of the content service (`updateEntity`, `updateEntityColumn`,
`deleteEntityColumns`, `writeSlotContent`, `markEntityChanged`, `clearSlotContent`) takes that slot.

The slot is of the keyed entity slot's literal shape (with `key: undefined` and `indexKeys: undefined`), and its
`storeSlot` is `settings` — so
`effectService.createEffect(db, [settingsSlot], [], …)` works and a column of it is a root like any other.
Its key is `undefined`, and its store is `{ slot }` (`TOIMSingleSlotStore`). Its lifetime is the
`slotReleasePolicy` (the db's, then `OIMSlotAtEmptyReleasePolicy`), so a single entity that holds a value
stays; one emptied and unheld is released, and the slot `getSingleSlot` mints next holds no entity. The value
is stored by the writer's `entityInserter`, which by default keeps the object handed in rather than a copy.

---

## Buckets

A bucket collection is, like an entity collection, a content service and the collection service over it.
The content service is the strategy — how a bucket keeps its member slots — and it is chosen at the factory:

```ts signature
createOIMSlotCollectionService(db, {
    slotContentService: new OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService<TBucketMemberSlot>(),   // or one of the others below
    slotStoreService?: IOIMSlotStoreService<TKey, TOIMBucketSlot<TSlots, TKey>, TStore>;      // Map; REQUIRED for an array key
    slotReleasePolicy?, slotSubscriptionListener?, columnSlotStoreService?, columnNames?,
}): OIMWritableSlotCollectionService<TKey, TOIMBucketSlot<TSlots, TKey>, TStore, readonly TBucketMemberSlot[], …>

new OIMSlotContentSetBucketService<TBucketMemberSlot>({ bucketCommands? })
new OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService<TBucketMemberSlot>({ bucketCommands?, bucketMemberSlotsArrayService? })
new OIMSlotContentSortedArrayBucketService<TBucketMemberSlot>({ compareBucketMemberSlots, bucketCommands?, bucketMemberSlotsArrayService? })
// bucketMemberSlotsArrayService: OIMBucketMemberSlotsArrayService (every mention, the default)
//                                or new OIMBucketUniqueMemberSlotsArrayService<TBucketMemberSlot>() (each slot once)
```

A bucket holds bucket member slots of any slot type — entity slots, bucket slots, computeds — and its
type parameter `TBucketMemberSlot extends TOIMSlot` (default `TOIMEntitySlot`) is that slot type, not the
entity type. The services hold no bucket: `createStoreSlot(db)` is one keyed set of buckets, the read doors
of the collection service take that store slot first, and the bucket doors of the content service take the
bucket slot.

```ts
const colourService = createOIMSlotCollectionService(db, { slotContentService: new OIMSlotContentSetBucketService<TOIMEntitySlot<Card>>() });
const colours = colourService.createStoreSlot(db);
const red = colourService.holdSlotByKey(colours, 'red');
colourService.slotContentService.writeSlotContent(red, [slot, cardService.getSlotByKey(cards, 'c2')]);
db.flush();
for (const deckSlot of colourService.slotContentService.getBucketMemberSlots(red)) { paint(deckSlot.entity); }
colourService.slotContentService.clearSlotContent(red);
red.owner.unholdSlot(red);
```

Every door below is the bucket content service's and takes the bucket slot:

| Door | Signature |
|---|---|
| `writeSlotContent(bucketSlot, bucketMemberSlots)` | `boolean` — states the whole bucket; idempotent; true when anything arrived or departed |
| `getBucketMemberSlotsMissingFrom(bucketSlot, bucketMemberSlots)` | `TBucketMemberSlot[]` — the members the given list leaves out, so a sync can write into them (clear a group key, set a deleted flag) instead of dropping them |
| `addBucketMemberSlot(bucketSlot, bucketMemberSlot)` / `addBucketMemberSlots(bucketSlot, bucketMemberSlots)` | joins the named bucket member slots and touches nothing else. REMOVES NOTHING |
| `removeBucketMemberSlot(bucketSlot, bucketMemberSlot)` / `removeBucketMemberSlots(bucketSlot, bucketMemberSlots)` | takes the named bucket member slots out and touches nothing else |
| `clearSlotContent(bucketSlot)` | empties it |
| `getBucketMemberSlots(bucketSlot)` | `Iterable<TBucketMemberSlot>` |
| `getBucketMemberSlotCount(bucketSlot)` | `number` |
| `hasBucketMemberSlot(bucketSlot, bucketMemberSlot)` | `boolean` — the content service's own membership test: one `Set.has` on a set bucket; on an array bucket its `bucketMemberSlotsArrayService.hasBucketMemberSlot` (a `Set.has` when unique, `indexOf` otherwise) |
| `markBucketColumnsChanged(bucketSlot, patch, changedColumns)` | `void` — tell the bucket's column slots which member columns moved |
| `markContentChanged(bucketSlot)` | `void` — re-settle emptiness and re-ask the release guard after a write made another way |
| `fillBucketMemberSlots(bucketSlot, bucketMemberSlots)` | `void` — fills a bucket slot nobody was told about yet; it throws on one that was already announced, which `addBucketMemberSlots` / `writeSlotContent` are for |

The entities of a bucket by key are the index's door, `indexService.getEntitiesByKey(indexStoreSlot, key)`
([The index that fills itself](#the-index-that-fills-itself--oimindexservice)).

### Which door: you hold the answer, or you hold the delta

`writeSlotContent` is for a caller who has THE LIST THAT SHOULD BE THERE and does not
know what changed — a search result, a page from a server, a filter re-run. One
call, and the engine works out the arrivals and the departures. Its cost is
proportional to WHAT THE BUCKET HOLDS, not to the change: the difference builds a
map over the whole incoming list and walks the standing one, so a batch of ten
into a bucket of two hundred pays for two hundred and ten.

`addBucketMemberSlots` / `removeBucketMemberSlots` are for a caller who KNOWS THE DELTA — an entity arrived
over a socket, a card was dragged in, an infinite list appended a page, an entity was
deleted. The standing slots keep the holds they already have. Adding costs what you
name. Removing k slots from an ordered bucket of n is ONE pass, n + k, through the content service's
`removeSlots` (the erase-remove idiom, as in Java's ArrayList.removeAll); k separate
`removeBucketMemberSlot` calls are up to k·n. The recorded `remove` commands come
in LIST order, not argument order, each at its position after the earlier ones
applied, so replaying them draws the same list. A set-driven bucket removes them in
the order you name them.

**`addBucketMemberSlots` removes nothing.** If the authoritative list SHRANK and you call
`addBucketMemberSlots`, the entity slots that left stay in the bucket, held. Not knowing what left is
exactly when `writeSlotContent` is the right door, and its cost is the price of not
knowing.

The keyed doors are the collection service's and take the store slot first —
`decksService.getSlotByKey(decks, key)`, `decksService.holdSlotByKey(decks, key)` — and a hold is given back
with `bucketSlot.owner.unholdSlot(bucketSlot)`. The by-key write is `decksService.writeSlotContentByKey(decks, key, members)`; on a bucket slot you hold it is
`decksService.slotContentService.writeSlotContent(bucketSlot, members)`.

A bucket's emptiness is the content service's `isSlotEmpty(bucketSlot)`, a member count of zero, so
an emptied bucket that nothing holds and nothing watches is released by the
guard on the same call that emptied it.

**A bucket never sorts.** Its order is what the caller put in — `addBucketMemberSlots`
appends, `insertBucketMemberSlotAt` inserts, a move moves, `writeSlotContent` takes the
sequence given. A sorted list is a computed over an index:
[Sorted lists](#sorted-lists); or the bucket of a `createOIMSlotCollectionSortedArrayIndexService` index, which
orders itself: [Sorted at write](#sorted-at-write).

`writeSlotContent(bucketSlot, members)` runs `assertWritable` — the frame guard
(`assertNotFlushing`) and the released-identity check — then the reconcile (an empty `arrived` and
`departed` is an unchanged write, which wakes nobody), the holds taken on arrivals, the holds given back by
departures and the single channel write of the bucket slot. It is handed a slot, so it hands back a
`boolean`: true when anything arrived or departed.

`writeSlotContent` **joins before it evicts**, so a slot named by both the old and the
new list never reaches zero references. It empties with one `drainSlots` rather
than one removal at a time — per-slot eviction on an array-driven bucket is
n(n-1)/2 element moves.

The commit itself is the strategy's, through the content service's protected `reconcileSlots` — the
reconciliation pattern (diff, then patch): bring the bucket to the new list and fill
two out-queues with one entry per hold taken and one per hold given
up, so the write links each of the first and unlinks each of the second. Both
empty means nothing changed. Each content service reconciles its own way:

- **Array-driven**: the caller's sequence IS the slots, so the same sequence is
  left alone and any other sequence — a reordered one included — is drained and
  re-added whole.
- **Set-driven** takes the set difference and never rebuilds: an untouched member
  keeps its hold.

**NO FRAME NUMBER IS PASSED ON THIS PATH.** `reconcileSlots` and `drainSlots` take none. A render script lives for exactly one frame:
`OIMBucketCommands` records onto the bucket slot (`bucket.commands`) as the writes land and
empties it once the flush has fully ended, so a consumer reads it INSIDE the
frame and what it reads can only describe the writes it was woken for.
`clearSlotContent` asks whether the bucket is empty **before** it
touches the store, so an already-empty bucket records nothing for a call that
reports nothing.

### Bucket content services

| Class | Storage type | One add records |
|---|---|---|
| `OIMSlotContentSetBucketService<TBucketMemberSlot>({ bucketCommands? })` | `TOIMBucketSlotsSetStore<TBucketMemberSlot>` = `Set<TBucketMemberSlot>` | one per slot |
| `OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService<TBucketMemberSlot>({ bucketCommands?, bucketMemberSlotsArrayService? })` | `TOIMBucketSlotsArrayStore<TBucketMemberSlot>` = `{ bucketMemberSlots, uniqueBucketMemberSlots, sortedCount }` | one per **mention**; one per slot, order kept, with `new OIMBucketUniqueMemberSlotsArrayService()` |
| `OIMSlotContentSortedArrayBucketService<TBucketMemberSlot>({ compareBucketMemberSlots, bucketMemberSlotsArrayService? })` | `TOIMBucketSlotsArrayStore<TBucketMemberSlot>` | one per mention or per slot, at its sorted place |

The first two are the ones a caller picks between, and neither sorts: the array-driven services keep the
caller's order. The last is the one the sorted-at-write index builds for itself
([Sorted at write](#sorted-at-write)); its `repositionBucketMemberSlot(bucketSlot, bucketMemberSlot)` moves one
member to its place after its sort columns changed.

Which slots an array bucket keeps is its `bucketMemberSlotsArrayService`, the only writer of the list and the
`Set` beside it: `OIMBucketMemberSlotsArrayService` keeps every mention and no `Set`;
`OIMBucketUniqueMemberSlotsArrayService` keeps each slot once and the list and its `Set` together, so the two never
disagree. With the unique one `hasBucketMemberSlot` answers from the `Set` (no array walk); with the default it
walks the array.

Nothing positional is on the abstract `OIMSlotContentBucketService`: the reads `getBucketMemberSlotAt` and
`getBucketMemberSlotPosition` are on the array-based services (array-driven and sorted), and the five
position writes on the array-driven one only. The set-driven service has none — a `Set` has no place to name,
so asking it does not compile. A content service keeps no per-bucket state.

The protected `removeSlot` answers WHERE the slot was, so the door recording an edit script never asks for a
position the removal itself had to compute. Two of its answers are not positions, and both are exported as
named constants:

| returns | means |
|---|---|
| `0` and up | the index the slot occupied, now vacated |
| `OIM_NOTHING_WAS_REMOVED` (`-1`) | the bucket did not hold it; nothing changed |
| `OIM_REMOVED_WITHOUT_A_POSITION` (`-2`) | removed from a store that keeps no positions, which is the set-driven service |

A removal answering the third is recorded as `recordWholeList(bucketSlot)`: a set has no index to patch,
so the consumer is told to re-read the bucket rather than handed a fabricated one.

`OIM_NOTHING_WAS_INSERTED` (`-1`) is the insert's answer when nothing was inserted, which is a repeat on an array bucket
with `OIMBucketUniqueMemberSlotsArrayService`. The recorded insert names the index the slot LANDED on — `at` clamped to the
ends of the list — and not `getBucketMemberSlotPosition`, because the default ordered list keeps one place per
**mention**: inserting a slot the bucket already holds gives it a second position, and the position read
names the FIRST. A command script built from it would tell the consumer to patch at an index the slot is not
at, and the consumer's list would diverge from the bucket's permanently.

**A bucket's storage is `bucketSlot.bucketSlotsStore`.** The bucket's own type carries it
(`TOIMBucketSlot<TOIMBucketSlotsArrayStore<TOIMEntitySlot<Card>>>`), so a mismatched pairing is a compile
error. **One content service instance may serve two bucket collections** — it keeps no per-bucket state.

### Positions the caller decides

A bucket whose positions are the caller's is one over `OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService`, which is
the `pageService` of the setup block. The two position reads and the five writes are that content service's, they take the bucket
slot and no store slot, and an index is valid only until the next write:

| Door | What it does |
|---|---|
| `getBucketMemberSlotAt(bucketSlot, index)` | who sits there, `undefined` past the end |
| `getBucketMemberSlotPosition(bucketSlot, bucketMemberSlot)` | where it sits, `-1` when it does not |
| `insertBucketMemberSlotAt(bucketSlot, at, bucketMemberSlot)` | puts it at `at`, clamped to the ends of the list |
| `removeBucketMemberSlotAt(bucketSlot, at)` | takes it out and hands it back, `undefined` past the end |
| `removeBucketMemberSlotRange(bucketSlot, at, count)` | takes a run out and hands it back |
| `moveBucketMemberSlotToPosition(bucketSlot, from, to)` | moves one slot; refuses `from === to` and either end out of range |
| `moveBucketMemberSlotRangeToPosition(bucketSlot, from, count, to)` | moves a run; the landing is read in the list WITHOUT the run in it |

Every position and count must be a whole number: `NaN` or a fraction throws
(`a position must be a whole number`) before anything moves, because the list
and `splice` would read it two different ways. `±Infinity` is allowed and clamps
like any other out-of-range position.

Each wraps a store change in the frame guard, the holds, the report and the
release question. The default ordered list records one place per MENTION, so
`insertBucketMemberSlotAt` of a slot the bucket already holds gives it a second position —
take `bucketMemberSlotsArrayService: new OIMBucketUniqueMemberSlotsArrayService()` when a position must name
exactly one entity slot.

Per strategy, generating code:

```ts
const slotContentBucketService = pageService.slotContentService;

// kanban, between columns
const cardItWasDroppedOn = cardService.getSlotByKey(cards, 'c2');
slotContentBucketService.removeBucketMemberSlotAt(todo, slotContentBucketService.getBucketMemberSlotPosition(todo, slot));
slotContentBucketService.insertBucketMemberSlotAt(
    done, slotContentBucketService.getBucketMemberSlotPosition(done, cardItWasDroppedOn) + 1, slot,
);

// priority queue — raise to the front, then nudge down two
slotContentBucketService.moveBucketMemberSlotToPosition(todo, slotContentBucketService.getBucketMemberSlotPosition(todo, slot), 0);
slotContentBucketService.moveBucketMemberSlotToPosition(
    todo, slotContentBucketService.getBucketMemberSlotPosition(todo, slot),
    slotContentBucketService.getBucketMemberSlotPosition(todo, slot) + 2,
);

// a whole list at once, in the order the server sent
slotContentBucketService.writeSlotContent(todo, cardService.writeInBatch(cards, () => (payload).map(entity => cardService.writeSlotContentByKey(cards, entity.id, entity))));
```

### The render script: `OIMBucketCommands`

```ts signature
new OIMBucketCommands(options: { maxCommandsPerSlot?: number })   // default OIM_MAX_COMMANDS_PER_SLOT

// a bucket content service takes it at construction, once:
new OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService({ bucketCommands: new OIMBucketCommands({ maxCommandsPerSlot: Infinity }) });
```

**Recording is a strategy chosen when the bucket content service is built.** `bucketCommands` is read once
into a readonly field; left out of a content service built with `new`, it is `OIMNoBucketCommands`, whose
every method is empty, so a bucket nobody renders positionally pays one empty call per write and allocates no
command. There is no setter: a content
service records into the one recorder it was built with. One recorder serves every bucket of every store slot
and of every db — it is stateless.

It writes the script onto the BUCKET slot itself, and is handed the member count for the cap below. The bucket
content service already writes the bucket slot on every mutation, so a consumer subscribes to the bucket and
reads the script inside the effect:

```ts
effectService.createEffect(db, [todo], [], () => {
    if (todo.isWholeListRecorded) render(Array.from(pageService.slotContentService.getBucketMemberSlots(todo)));
    else applyToTheRenderedList(todo.commands ?? []);
});
```

`TOIMBucketSlot` carries two fields for it, and a consumer reads both:

| Field | What it says |
|---|---|
| `commands` | `readonly TOIMOrderedListCommand[]`, or `undefined` before the first write — what this frame's writes did, in order |
| `isWholeListRecorded` | the script was given up on; read the bucket's slots and rebuild |

**READ BOTH INSIDE THE FRAME.** They are reset once the flush has FULLY ended —
after `db.flush()` returns, `commands` is empty and `isWholeListRecorded` is
`false` — so the only places they exist are an effect body and a
`OIMChannelService.INSTANCE.subscribeAfterEachFrame(channelSlot, handler)` handler. No frame number is passed
back: a consumer that did not read this frame's script reads the list instead.

A script is stamped with the clock reading it started at (`commandsStartedAtRevision`/`commandsStartedAtEpoch`),
and it is stale once a frame has opened after that stamp (`channelSlot.frame.openedAtRevision`/`openedAtEpoch`).
The recorder clears a stale script before it records into it, as well as in the after-flush reset, so a write
that lands after a flush but before that reset starts a new script instead of extending one consumers already
read. The reset is subscribed with `subscribeAfterEachFlush` on the first script a channel slot ever sees, and
walks only the buckets that recorded.

A positional write is always recorded as a position. `isWholeListRecorded` is set by a write of the whole bucket — `writeSlotContent`,
`clearSlotContent`, `moveBucketMemberSlotRangeToPosition` — by a removal from a bucket whose
content service keeps no positions, which has no index to patch, and by the script
outgrowing the list
it describes. `maxCommandsPerSlot` is that ratio; it defaults to
`OIM_MAX_COMMANDS_PER_SLOT`, which is 1, the same ratio
`oimOrderedListCommandsOfTransition` takes as `maxCommandsPerSlot`. `Infinity` refuses the collapse
outright, which is what a consumer animating item moves needs: a whole-list answer
tells it everything changed and costs it every move it meant to animate.

`IOIMBucketCommands` is the interface the bucket content service records through:
`recordInsert(bucketSlot, index, bucketMemberSlot, bucketMemberSlotCount)`,
`recordRemove(bucketSlot, index, count, bucketMemberSlotCount)`, `recordMove(bucketSlot, from, to, bucketMemberSlotCount)`
and `recordWholeList(bucketSlot)`. They take positions, not a command object, so the
empty strategy is handed nothing to allocate. A consumer does not call the record methods; the
content service's own write doors do.

### A single bucket

One bucket under no key is a store slot of an `OIMSingleSlotService` over a bucket content service, with
`OIMSingleSlotStoreService.INSTANCE` as the store service:

```ts signature
createOIMSingleSlotService(db, {
    slotContentService: new OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService<TBucketMemberSlot>(),   // or the set one
    slotReleasePolicy?, slotSubscriptionListener?, columnSlotStoreService?, columnNames?,
}): OIMWritableSingleSlotService<TOIMBucketContentSlot<TSlots>, readonly TBucketMemberSlot[], …>
```

```ts
const handService = createOIMSingleSlotService(db, { slotContentService: new OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService<TOIMEntitySlot<Card>>({ bucketCommands: new OIMBucketCommands({ maxCommandsPerSlot: undefined }) }) });
const hand = handService.createStoreSlot(db);
const handSlot = handService.holdSingleSlot(hand);
handService.slotContentService.writeSlotContent(handSlot, [slot]);
handService.slotContentService.insertBucketMemberSlotAt(handSlot, 0, cardService.getSlotByKey(cards, 'c2'));
effectService.disposeEffect(effectService.createEffect(db, [handSlot], [], () => {
    render(Array.from(handService.slotContentService.getBucketMemberSlots(handSlot)));
}));
handSlot.owner.unholdSlot(handSlot);
```

One bucket, no key: the single-slot store files its one bucket slot as the store's `slot`. The bucket slot is a
`TOIMBucketContentSlot<TSlots>` of the keyed bucket slot's shape (`key: undefined`), what an effect subscribes to and what a reader is handed,
so the channel's write door still sees three slot shapes. Every door of the bucket content service takes it as
it takes a keyed bucket slot, and `markBucketColumnsChanged(bucketSlot, patch, changedColumns)` is how the
caller that changed members says which of their columns moved, as the index does for a keyed bucket. Each
door writes the bucket slot to the channel once.

**Its lifetime is the `slotReleasePolicy`.** With none named (here or on the db) it is
`OIMSlotAtEmptyReleasePolicy.INSTANCE`, so an emptied single bucket that nothing holds or watches is
released, and `getSingleSlot(storeSlot)` mints a fresh, empty one on the next read. Hold the
slot (`holdSingleSlot(storeSlot)`) for as long as you write into it, or name `OIMSlotNeverReleasePolicy.INSTANCE`.

### The index that fills itself — `OIMSlotCollectionIndexService`

```ts signature
createOIMSlotCollectionIndexService<TEntity, TSourceKey, TColumns?, TKey?, TSourceStore?, TSlots?, TSlotContentService?>(db, {
    entityService: Pick<OIMSlotCollectionService<TSourceKey, TOIMEntitySlot<TEntity, TSourceKey>, TSourceStore, unknown>, 'getSlots'>;
    ...TOIMIndexKeyOptions<TKey, TEntity, TColumns>;          // { columns } | { keyOf } | { keyOf, columns }
    slotContentService?: OIMSlotContentBucketService<TOIMEntitySlot<TEntity>, TSlots>;  // default: array-driven, no commands
    bucketSlotStoreService?: IOIMSlotStoreService<TKey, TOIMBucketSlot<TSlots, TKey>, TStore>; // REQUIRED for an array TKey
    slotReleasePolicy?: IOIMSlotReleasePolicy;
    columnSlotStoreService?: IOIMSlotStoreService<string, TOIMColumnSlot>;
    columnNames?: readonly string[];
}): OIMSlotCollectionIndexService<TKey, TEntity, TSlots, TSourceKey, TSourceStore, TSlotContentService, …>

class OIMSlotCollectionIndexService<…> extends OIMSlotCollectionService<…> {
    createIndexStoreSlot(sourceStoreSlot: TOIMStoreSlot<TSourceStore, TOIMEntitySlot<TEntity, TSourceKey>, Partial<TEntity>>): TOIMIndexStoreSlot<…>;
    disposeIndexStoreSlot(indexStoreSlot: TOIMIndexStoreSlot<…>): void;
    getEntitiesByKey(indexStoreSlot, key): (TEntity | undefined)[];
    getSlotsByKeys(indexStoreSlot, keys): TBucketSlot[];
    holdSlotsByKeys(indexStoreSlot, keys): TBucketSlot[];
    getBucketColumnByKey / holdBucketColumnByKey(indexStoreSlot, key, columnName): TOIMColumnSlot;
    getAnyBucketColumnByKey / holdAnyBucketColumnByKey(indexStoreSlot, key): TOIMColumnSlot;
}
```

`OIMSlotCollectionIndexService` is a collection service of buckets, so it has every read door of one, and its
`slotContentService` is the bucket content service narrowed by type to its reads (`getBucketMemberSlots`,
`getBucketMemberSlotCount`, `hasBucketMemberSlot`, and the positional reads where the strategy has them) — the
index is the only writer of its buckets. The strategy is chosen at the factory:
`OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService` by default, `OIMSlotContentSetBucketService` passed as
`slotContentService`, and the sorted one built by `createOIMSlotCollectionSortedArrayIndexService`. Only the array-based
content services answer by position: `getBucketMemberSlotAt(bucketSlot, index)` (O(1), `undefined` past the
end) and `getBucketMemberSlotPosition(bucketSlot, entitySlot)` (walks the array, O(n), `-1` for a non-member).
The index's default content service records no commands; pass one built with `bucketCommands` for a render
script.

**One index service per entity collection type; one index store slot per entity store slot.**
`indexService.createIndexStoreSlot(entityStoreSlot)` registers the index on that entity store slot
and hands back the index's bucket store slot, a `TOIMIndexStoreSlot` — a store slot of buckets
that also names its `sourceStoreSlot`. Entity slots are filed into it by a key derived from the entity. You
read through the index service, passing that store slot; the index is what writes its buckets.
**No bucket exists for a key until it is minted**: `getSlotByKey`,
`holdSlotByKey`, `getSlotsByKeys` and `holdSlotsByKeys` mint it and fill it from the source entities
written before it, without a flush, so minting inside an effect body does not throw.
`getSlotsByKeys` / `holdSlotsByKeys` fill every new bucket in ONE pass over the source. How long it lives after that is **the
`slotReleasePolicy`'s ordinary business**, exactly as for a hand-held bucket; the index injects no lifetime of its
own. With none named it is `OIMSlotAtEmptyReleasePolicy.INSTANCE`: the bucket stands while it has members and is
maintained on every write.

```ts
const byDeckService = createOIMSlotCollectionIndexService(db, {
    entityService: cardService,
    keyOf: (card: Card) => card.deck,
});
const byDeck = byDeckService.createIndexStoreSlot(cards);

const spades = byDeckService.holdSlotByKey(byDeck, 'spades');
effectService.createEffect(db, [spades], [], () => render(Array.from(byDeckService.slotContentService.getBucketMemberSlots(spades))));
```

A set-driven index names its content service with the bucket member slot type and the index key type spelled
out — `new OIMSlotContentSetBucketService()` infers `<TOIMSlot, TOIMStoreKey>` and fails to type-check:

```ts
const bySuitService = createOIMSlotCollectionIndexService(db, {
    entityService: cardService,
    columns: ['deck'],
    slotContentService: new OIMSlotContentSetBucketService<TOIMEntitySlot<Card>, string>(),
});
const bySuit = bySuitService.createIndexStoreSlot(cards);
```

- **Passing the entity store slot to `createIndexStoreSlot` is the whole wiring.** It registers
  a content-change listener on that store slot (`OIMContentChangeListenerService.INSTANCE.addContentChangeListener`);
  the entity services know nothing about indexes. Call `createIndexStoreSlot` twice over one entity
  store slot and it files into both. `entityService` is used only for its `getSlots`, to fill a new bucket
  from the source.
- **The key comes from `columns`, `keyOf`, or both** — the same pair as the sorter's
  `sortColumns` / `comparator` (`TOIMIndexKeyOptions`). `{ columns: ['deck'] }`: the key is
  the value of that ONE column, typed by `TOIMIndexKey<TEntity, TColumns>` from the
  column itself. `{ keyOf }`: any function, read again on every write, because a
  function does not say which columns it reads. `{ keyOf, columns }`: the columns are the
  ones `keyOf` reads. With `columns`, a patch or put whose changed columns include none of
  them keeps the entity's key and calls nothing; a write of the whole value (a fill, a
  clear, `markEntityChanged(slot)` with no names) always reads the key again.
- **A key of several columns**: `createOIMSlotCollectionIndexService(db, { entityService, columns: ['deck', 'suit'],
  bucketSlotStoreService: new OIMSlotTreeStoreService(OIMDefaults.KEY_TREE_WALK_SCALAR.getValue()) })` makes the key
  the array of those values in order, typed as a tuple. Only that store knows the key is an array (its
  `isSameKey`), so a fresh array with the same parts moves nothing. `createOIMSlotCollectionIndexService` takes a scalar key
  unless it is handed a `bucketSlotStoreService`: two columns or an array `keyOf` without one do not compile.
  `getSlotsByKeys` / `holdSlotsByKeys` fill array-keyed buckets one pass over the
  source per key (the cost of `getSlotByKey` each); only a scalar key gets one pass for all.
- **Entity slots are filed on write**, using the index's key. Writes inside `writeInBatch` on the collection
  notify once per batch; the index groups the entity slots by key and moves each group with one bucket write.
- **Reading**, each taking the index store slot first: `getSlotByKey`, `holdSlotByKey`, `findSlotByKey`,
  `hasSlotContentByKey`, `getSlotsByKeys`, `holdSlotsByKeys`, `getSlots`, `getSlotCount`, `getEntitiesByKey`, and the bucket column
  slot doors `getAnyBucketColumnByKey`, `holdAnyBucketColumnByKey`,
  `getBucketColumnByKey`, `holdBucketColumnByKey`; on a bucket slot, `slotContentService.getBucketMemberSlots`,
  `getBucketMemberSlotCount`, `hasBucketMemberSlot`; and `unholdColumn` (below).
  `getEntitiesByKey` resolves the bucket with `getSlotByKey`, so a key with no bucket MINTS one — one `keyOf`
  walk over the source — and an empty unheld bucket is released at the flush, so reading an empty key every
  frame walks every frame. Hold a key you read repeatedly.
- **The channel** is the index store slot's `channelSlot`, the source store slot's — what a
  React hook checks before subscribing.
- **`disposeIndexStoreSlot(indexStoreSlot)`** unsubscribes from the source store slot, empties that
  store slot's buckets and gives back every entity slot it held. The minting doors (`getSlotByKey`,
  `holdSlotByKey`, `getSlotsByKeys`, `holdSlotsByKeys`, `getEntitiesByKey`, the bucket column doors)
  throw after it, for that store slot;
  the two give-backs (`slot.owner.unholdSlot`, `indexService.unholdColumn`)
  still take back a hold given out before it, so a cleanup that runs late does not
  throw.
- **A key with no bucket is not maintained at all**, so a write under such a key
  costs nothing beyond one key read and one comparison — no bucket store, no
  maintenance nodes. What decides it is the BUCKET, not the hold: a standing bucket
  is maintained whether anyone holds it or not.
- **Order is not the bucket's business, unless you pick the strategy that makes it so.**
  A bucket keeps its arrival order; a sorted list is
  `createOIMSortedComputedService(db, { indexService, sortColumns?, comparator? })`
  — see [Sorted lists](#sorted-lists) — or the index is built with
  `createOIMSlotCollectionSortedArrayIndexService`, whose buckets are already in order — see
  [Sorted at write](#sorted-at-write). A second computed over the bucket handles
  projection or filtering.
- **Members are read through the bucket content service**: `Array.from(indexService.slotContentService.getBucketMemberSlots(bucketSlot))`.
  There is no `.value`.
- **Subscription is on the bucket, not a computed.** The bucket is a ROOT slot, so it
  goes in the FIRST array of `createEffect` — not the second. **The bucket wakes on
  membership only**: an entity slot joining or leaving. A write to an entity that stays in the
  bucket does not wake it — subscribe to that entity's own slot for that.
- **Bucket lifetime is the `slotReleasePolicy` option, not the index's.** Name nothing (here or on the db)
  and it is `OIMSlotAtEmptyReleasePolicy.INSTANCE`: an unheld bucket stays while it has members and goes
  once empty; `OIMSlotNeverReleasePolicy.INSTANCE` keeps it for good; pass an `OIMSlotAfterIdleReleasePolicy`
  and it cools on its queue; pass `OIMSlotAtUnholdReleasePolicy.INSTANCE` and it dies at the last give-back,
  and the next hold builds a fresh one by walking the source again.

**The bucket's any-column slot exists, but it is not the recommended path.**
`holdAnyBucketColumnByKey(indexStoreSlot, key)` (and `getAnyBucketColumnByKey(indexStoreSlot, key)`) returns a
`TOIMColumnSlot` on the bucket slot that wakes when the content of a member changes —
any write to a member inside. A member joining or leaving is NOT its business: that wakes
the bucket slot (`getSlotByKey` / `holdSlotByKey`). A reader that wants both subscribes
to both, and the subscriber picks by which slots it puts in `createEffect`.

```ts
const deckIndexService = createOIMSlotCollectionIndexService(db, { entityService: cardService, keyOf: (card: Card) => card.deck });
const deckIndex = deckIndexService.createIndexStoreSlot(cards);
const spadesBucket = deckIndexService.holdSlotByKey(deckIndex, 'spades');
const spadesAnyColumn = deckIndexService.holdAnyBucketColumnByKey(deckIndex, 'spades');
const entitiesEffect = effectService.createEffect(db, [spadesBucket, spadesAnyColumn], [], () => {
    console.log(deckIndexService.getEntitiesByKey(deckIndex, 'spades'));
});
effectService.disposeEffect(entitiesEffect);
deckIndexService.columnSlotService.unholdColumn(spadesAnyColumn);
spadesBucket.owner.unholdSlot(spadesBucket);
```

A column slot taken with `getAnyBucketColumnByKey` and subscribed to is held by the
effect, so a plain getter is enough: the slot lives while the effect does and goes at the
next `flush()` after `disposeEffect`; one nobody kept is gone at the next `flush()`.

**Do not reach for it to render a list.** Every edit of every member wakes whoever
reads it, so a list bound to it re-renders whole for a one-field change. Subscribe
the list to the bucket (membership) and each item to its own entity slot — that is the
path the engine is built for. The any-column slot is for a reader that genuinely
needs the whole list each time: an export, an aggregate over the entities, a log.

It costs nothing until someone asks for one: a write is checked against it only after
the index has been asked for the first any-column slot.

**The content-change hook.** `OIMContentChangeListenerService.INSTANCE.addContentChangeListener(storeSlot, listener, readColumnNames): void`
and `removeContentChangeListener(storeSlot, listener): boolean` file and unfile a listener on that one store
slot, by the listener object. `addReadColumn` / `removeReadColumn` / `addReadAnyColumn` / `removeReadAnyColumn`
declare reads without a listener of their own, which is how an index declares its bucket columns.
**Which columns a listener reads** is declared when it is added: `readColumnNames` lists them, and
`undefined` means every column. Removing the listener gives its columns back. An
index store slot declares its key `columns` (all columns when the key is an opaque `keyOf`), and
adds each column its bucket column slots watch, and all columns once a bucket any-column slot was
asked for. Column slots on entities are not in it: a write finds them on the entity
itself. A write whose changed columns no listener reads costs one `Map.has` per name:
no listener is called, nothing is buffered, and the names array is reused across writes. A write that names no columns
(a fill, a clear) always reaches the listeners. A listener of your own that must see
every column write is added with `readColumnNames` `undefined`. **The filter is the union, per store
slot, not per listener**: once a write touches a column ANY listener of that store reads, every
listener of that store is called, so a listener that declared a narrower set still checks
`changedColumns` itself, as `OIMSlotCollectionIndexService` does against its key columns.
`IOIMContentChangeListener<TSlot, TPatch>` has two methods:
`onContentChanged(slot, patch, changedColumns)` and
`onContentChangedMany(slotChannelQueue, patchChannelQueue, changedColumnsChannelQueue)` — three
parallel `OIMChannelQueue`s read with `getEntryCount()` / `getEntryAt(i)`, valid only during the
call, so a listener copies what it keeps — `patch` is what an update
wrote, `changedColumns` the names `markEntityChanged(slot, columns)` was given, either
`undefined` when the write carries none. A single write outside a batch delivers one `onContentChanged` as soon as it is filed; inside
`writeInBatch` (or `openBatch` / `closeBatch`) on the collection the writes are queued on the store slot and
delivered as ONE `onContentChangedMany` when the outermost batch closes. Code inside the batch reads the index
as it was before the batch.
This hook is the only seam an index uses; an index of your own is a listener.

**Bucket column slots.** An index hands out one column slot per bucket and column:
`getBucketColumnByKey(indexStoreSlot, key, columnName)`, `holdBucketColumnByKey(indexStoreSlot, key, columnName)`,
`indexService.unholdColumn(columnSlot)`. It is a `TOIMColumnSlot` whose `carrierSlot` is the
bucket slot, and it is written when a write changes that column on any member of the
bucket (the index calls its bucket content service's `markBucketColumnsChanged(bucketSlot, patch, changedColumns)`,
as the caller does on a single bucket).
The any-column doors `getAnyBucketColumnByKey(indexStoreSlot, key)` / `holdAnyBucketColumnByKey(indexStoreSlot, key)`
return the same kind of slot, written when any column of any member changes. A give-back is
`slot.owner.unholdSlot(slot)`.

```ts
const decksService = createOIMSlotCollectionIndexService(db, { entityService: cardService, keyOf: (card: Card) => card.deck });
const decks = decksService.createIndexStoreSlot(cards);
const rankOfSpades = decksService.holdBucketColumnByKey(decks, 'spades', 'rank');
effectService.disposeEffect(effectService.createEffect(db, [rankOfSpades], [], () => {}));
decksService.columnSlotService.unholdColumn(rankOfSpades);
```

### Sorted lists

```ts signature
createOIMSortedComputedService<TKey, TEntity extends object, TSlots, TSourceKey, TSourceStore, TComputedStore?>({
    indexService: OIMSlotCollectionIndexService<TKey, TEntity, TSlots, TSourceKey, TSourceStore>;
    sortColumns?: readonly TOIMSortColumn<TEntity>[];   // { column: TOIMSortableColumnName<TEntity>; direction: 'asc' | 'desc' }
    comparator?: (left: TEntity, right: TEntity) => number;
    slotReleasePolicy?: IOIMSlotReleasePolicy;          // default OIMSlotAtUnholdReleasePolicy.INSTANCE
    columnSlotStoreService?: IOIMSlotStoreService<string, TOIMComputedColumnSlot>;
    computedSlotStoreService?: IOIMSlotStoreService<TKey, TOIMComputedSlot<…>, TComputedStore>;  // Map; REQUIRED for any other store
}): OIMSortedComputedService<TKey, TEntity, TSlots, TSourceKey, TSourceStore, TComputedStore>

createSortedStoreSlot(indexStoreSlot: TOIMIndexStoreSlot<…>): TOIMStoreSlot<TComputedStore, TOIMSortedComputedSlot<TEntity, TKey>>
readonly computedCollectionService: OIMSlotCollectionService<TKey, TOIMSortedComputedSlot<TEntity, TKey>, TComputedStore, …>
```

`slotReleasePolicy` decides whether a key's sorted list outlives its last hold. The
default lets it go at the unhold, so holding the key again sorts from scratch;
`OIMSlotNeverReleasePolicy.INSTANCE` keeps every key that was ever read and re-sorts it
only when a read finds it changed — the arm for a view that switches between groups.
Pass the same policy to the index the list reads, or its bucket is rebuilt instead.

An `OIMSortedComputedService` takes no db: its store slots run on the channel slot of the index store slot
they sort. One per index service. `createSortedStoreSlot(indexStoreSlot)` makes one sorted store slot over
one index store slot, and the read doors of `computedCollectionService` take that store slot first:
`getSlotByKey`, `holdSlotByKey`, `findSlotByKey`, `getSlots`, `getSlotCount`, and the column doors; per key a
computed slot whose value, read through `slot.computedValueService.getValueForSlot(slot)`, is that key's entity
slots sorted. A hold is given back with `slot.owner.unholdSlot(slot)`.

- **`sortColumns` decide which writes re-sort**: only a write that changes one of them on a
  member. A `TOIMSortableColumnName<TEntity>` is a column whose values are strings,
  numbers or bigints.
- **`comparator` decides the order.** Without it the order is `oimColumnsComparator(sortColumns)`:
  the columns in turn, each by its `direction`, an undefined or null value last. An
  entity slot with no entity sorts last.
- **Only `comparator`** → any write to a member re-sorts, since nothing names the
  columns it reads.
- **Neither** → a member keeps the place it first took; an arrival is appended.
- **Both `sortColumns` and `comparator`** → the two split the job: `comparator` orders,
  `sortColumns` is the list of columns whose change wakes the sort. **List every column
  the comparator reads**: a change to a column it reads but `sortColumns` omits does not
  re-sort, and the list stays in its old order until something listed changes. This
  is the combination to reach for when the order needs a rule `oimColumnsComparator`
  cannot express — a locale compare, a computed key, a tie-break — and the sort
  should still wake only for the columns that rule reads, instead of for every write
  to a member as with `comparator` alone.

  ```ts
  const cardsInDeckService = createOIMSlotCollectionIndexService(db, {
      entityService: cardService,
      keyOf: (card: Card) => card.deck,
  });
  createOIMSortedComputedService({
      indexService: cardsInDeckService,
      sortColumns: [{ column: 'title', direction: 'asc' }, { column: 'rank', direction: 'asc' }],
      comparator: (l, r) => l.title.localeCompare(r.title, 'de') || l.rank - r.rank,
  }).createSortedStoreSlot(cardsInDeckService.createIndexStoreSlot(cards));
  // a write to `title` or `rank` re-sorts; a write to `note` does not
  ```

Its sources are the bucket slot of the key (membership) plus the bucket column slot
of each column — or the bucket's any-column slot when only a comparator is given. It is
a pull computed: re-derived on the read that asks; an effect subscribes to it in the
SECOND array of `createEffect`. A re-sort that yields the same sequence
(`oimSameSlotSequence`) keeps the previous array, so its identity is stable.

```ts
const decksService = createOIMSlotCollectionIndexService(db, { entityService: cardService, keyOf: (card: Card) => card.deck });
const decks = decksService.createIndexStoreSlot(cards);
const byRankInDeckService = createOIMSortedComputedService({
    indexService: decksService,
    sortColumns: [{ column: 'rank', direction: 'asc' }],
});
const byRankInDeck = byRankInDeckService.createSortedStoreSlot(decks);
const spadesByRank = byRankInDeckService.computedCollectionService.holdSlotByKey(byRankInDeck, 'spades');
const sortedEffect = effectService.createEffect(db, [], [spadesByRank], () => {
    render(spadesByRank.computedValueService.getValueForSlot(spadesByRank));
});
effectService.disposeEffect(sortedEffect);
spadesByRank.owner.unholdSlot(spadesByRank);
```

### Sorted at write

A second way to get a sorted list. `createOIMSortedComputedService` sorts at read, over any
index. `createOIMSlotCollectionSortedArrayIndexService` keeps the index's own buckets sorted at write, and
the user picks one at construction.

```ts signature
createOIMSlotCollectionSortedArrayIndexService<TEntity extends object, TSourceKey, TColumns?, TKey extends TOIMStoreKey?, TSourceStore?, TStore?>(db, {
    entityService, ...TOIMIndexKeyOptions<TKey, TEntity, TColumns>,     // as createOIMSlotCollectionIndexService, scalar key
    sortColumns: readonly TOIMSortColumn<TEntity>[];                   // REQUIRED
    bucketSlotStoreService?, slotReleasePolicy?, columnSlotStoreService?, columnNames?,
}): OIMSlotCollectionSortedArrayIndexService<…>   // its slotContentService is an OIMSlotContentSortedArrayBucketService
```

```ts
declare const someCardSlot: TOIMEntitySlot<Card, TOIMStoreKey>;
const cardsByDeckService = createOIMSlotCollectionSortedArrayIndexService(db, {
    entityService: cardService,
    columns: ['deck'],
    sortColumns: [{ column: 'rank', direction: 'asc' }, { column: 'id', direction: 'desc' }],
});
const cardsByDeck = cardsByDeckService.createIndexStoreSlot(cards);
const spades = cardsByDeckService.holdSlotByKey(cardsByDeck, 'spades');
for (const cardSlot of cardsByDeckService.slotContentService.getBucketMemberSlots(spades)) { /* in rank order */ }
cardsByDeckService.slotContentService.getBucketMemberSlotAt(spades, 0);
cardsByDeckService.slotContentService.getBucketMemberSlotPosition(spades, someCardSlot);
```

- **Reads come back in order**: `getBucketMemberSlots`, `getBucketMemberSlotAt` and
  `getBucketMemberSlotPosition` on `OIMSlotContentSortedArrayBucketService` answer in `sortColumns` order,
  so no sorted computed is needed.
- **A lazy insertion buffer.** A write appends the arrival to an unsorted tail of the bucket's
  array (`TOIMBucketSlotsArrayStore`: the array store plus `sortedCount`). The first read
  settles the tail: binary insertion when the tail is short, one sort of the array when it is
  long. A bucket nobody reads is never sorted.
- **The index re-files a member when one of its sort columns changes, and only then.** A write
  to a column that is neither the key nor a sort column neither reorders the bucket nor wakes it.
  A re-file wakes the bucket once per frame.
- **There are no positional writes** on this bucket (`insertBucketMemberSlotAt` and the other
  position writes belong to `OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService`): the order is the comparator's,
  not the caller's.
- **Bucket commands are always `OIMNoBucketCommands`**: this strategy records no per-flush
  script.
- **Parts**: `OIMSlotContentSortedArrayBucketService` (options
  `TOIMSlotContentSortedArrayBucketServiceOptions`: `compareBucketMemberSlots`; adds
  `repositionBucketMemberSlot(bucketSlot, bucketMemberSlot)`), `OIMSlotCollectionSortedArrayIndexService`.

**Choosing between the two arms.** Sort-at-write suits point updates: a change to a sort
