column re-files one member. Sort-at-read (`createOIMSortedComputedService` over any index)
suits bulk loads. Both are shipped; neither is a default.

**`indexKeys` on each entity slot.** Each indexable slot carries, per index store slot, the key the entity is
filed under now, so a moved entity slot leaves its old bucket in O(1), also under the in-place
writer. Only the index writes it, through the `IOIMIndexKeysService` (`get(slot, position)`,
`set(slot, position, indexKey)`), at the position `createIndexStoreSlot` allocated
(`indexStoreSlot.indexKeysPosition`). Positions are allocated per entity store slot
(`sourceStoreSlot.indexKeysPositions`). Pick the strategy once per db, `new OIMDB({ indexKeysService })`
(default `OIMDefaults.INDEX_KEYS_SERVICE.getValue()`):

| strategy | on `disposeIndexStoreSlot` | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `OIMAppendingIndexKeysService` (default) | the index's position is never reused; its stale entry stays on each entity slot | an entity slot's `indexKeys` grows to the highest position any index wrote on it (K indexes made and disposed → an array of K on an entity slot the last one filed), and a stale entry keeps its key reachable. Writes pay nothing for a disposed index: only live listeners are kept |
| `OIMReclaimingIndexKeysService` | wipes that position on every entity slot of the source store slot and reuses it | O(N) per dispose |

Switch to `OIMReclaimingIndexKeysService` only if you create indexes dynamically and often. Creating
indexes dynamically and often is expensive, so avoid it.

### The channel of a bucket store slot

A bucket store slot takes its channel slot at `createStoreSlot(db)` (an index store slot, from its source
store slot). The refusal to write during a flush lives inside `OIMChannelService.INSTANCE.write`.

---

## Derivations

```ts signature
type TOIMComputedSources = {
    readonly sourceSlots: readonly TOIMSlot[];
    readonly sourceComputeds: readonly TOIMComputedSlot[];
};
```

In a `createSources` result (of `createOIMComputedService`'s options, or of `createStoreSlot`) both `sourceSlots` and `sourceComputeds` are optional; a missing one means none.

```ts signature
type TOIMComputedSlot<TValue = unknown, TKey = unknown> = TOIMIndexableSlot<TKey> & Readonly<TOIMDerivation> & {
    readonly owner: IOIMSlotOwner;
    readonly computedValueService: IOIMComputedValueService<TValue>;
    readonly value: TValue;
    readonly checkedAtRevision: number;
    readonly checkedAtEpoch: number;
    readonly isDeriving: boolean;
    readonly allRootSlots: readonly TOIMSlot[] | undefined;
};

interface IOIMComputedValueService<TValue = unknown> {
    getValueForSlot(computedSlot: TOIMComputedSlot<TValue>): TValue;
}
```

A computed is a SLOT, the plain data type `TOIMComputedSlot`. Its owner is the slot owner of the
`OIMComputedService` that minted it, and the service is the only writer of the slot. The value service
(`OIMComputedValueService`, which every computed slot carries as `computedValueService`) holds the
`sameValueGuard` ONCE, the store slot holds its `derive` and `createSources` and its channel slot's clock,
and the value service serves the value. Every source list in this engine —
`createEffect`'s third argument and `sourceComputeds` — is typed
`readonly TOIMComputedSlot[]`; a source computed is a slot taken from its own
service, through `computedCollectionService.getSlotByKey(storeSlot, key)` (`undefined` for a single). Inside
`derive`, `computedSlot.value` is the previous value.

A derivation is **asked, never woken**. A chain short-circuits on "did anything I
read move?", so `filter → sort → page` over quiet roots is a walk of integer
comparisons. A cycle cannot be built.

**Creating a service or a store slot takes no hold.** A computed slot is held on every slot in its
`sourceSlots` and on every entry of its `sourceComputeds`, and the holder is its
owner: it takes them when it mints the slot and gives them back when the slot's content is released.
The slot dies when nothing holds it; the store slot lives on and mints a fresh slot on
the next read or hold.

### One derivation per key

```ts signature
class OIMComputedService<TKey, TValue, TComputedStore> {
    constructor(options: TOIMComputedServiceOptions<TKey, TValue, TComputedStore>);
    readonly computedCollectionService: OIMSlotCollectionService<TKey, TOIMComputedSlot<TValue, TKey>, TComputedStore,
        OIMComputedValueService<TKey, TValue>, Extract<keyof TValue, string>, TOIMComputedColumnSlot, OIMPullColumnSlotOwner>;
    createComputedStoreSlot(channelMap: IOIMChannelMap, derive?, createSources?): TOIMComputedStoreSlot<TComputedStore, TValue, TKey>;
}

createOIMComputedService<TKey, TValue, TComputedStore = Map<TKey, TOIMComputedSlot<TValue, TKey>>>({
    createSources?: (key: TKey, storeSlot: TOIMStoreSlot | undefined) => Partial<TOIMComputedSources>;
    derive?: (computedSlot: TOIMComputedSlot<TValue, TKey>) => TValue;
    sameValueGuard?: TOIMSameValueGuard<TValue>;   // default Object.is
    initialValue?: TValue;
    slotReleasePolicy?: IOIMSlotReleasePolicy;     // default OIMSlotAtUnholdReleasePolicy.INSTANCE
    columnSlotStoreService?: IOIMSlotStoreService<string, TOIMComputedColumnSlot>;  // OIMDefaults.COMPUTED_COLUMN_SLOT_STORE_SERVICE
    columnNames?: readonly Extract<keyof TValue, string>[];
    computedSlotStoreService?: IOIMSlotStoreService<TKey, TOIMComputedSlot<TValue, TKey>, TComputedStore>;  // Map; REQUIRED for any other store
}): OIMComputedService<TKey, TValue, TComputedStore>
```

The factory takes no db: a computed service is configuration, and each store slot takes its channel slot at
`createComputedStoreSlot(db, …)`.

**`derive` and `createSources` come from the store slot or from the service.** Each one a store
slot is given (`createComputedStoreSlot(db, derive, createSources)`) is used for that store slot; each one it is
not given comes from the service's options. A store slot that would end up without one of the two throws by name at
`createComputedStoreSlot`. So one service per value type can serve many derivations, each its own store slot.

Doors of a keyed computed store slot are the read doors of `computedCollectionService`, each taking it first:
`getSlotByKey(storeSlot, key)`, `holdSlotByKey(storeSlot, key)`, `findSlotByKey(storeSlot, key)`,
`getSlots(storeSlot)`, `getSlotCount(storeSlot)`, and the column doors; the value is
`slot.computedValueService.getValueForSlot(slot)`, and a give-back is `slot.owner.unholdSlot(slot)`.

**A single computed is its own service.** `createOIMSingleComputedService<TValue>({ … })` builds an
`OIMSingleComputedService`, whose store slots each hold at most one computed slot, read through
`computedSingleSlotService` (`getSingleSlot`, `holdSingleSlot`, `findSingleSlot`). Like a keyed one, a store slot
outlives every computed slot it mints and mints a fresh one on the next read or hold once the previous one is gone.

```ts
const topRankService = createOIMSingleComputedService<number>({
    sameValueGuard: oimSameValueZeroGuard,
    initialValue: -1,
});
const topRank = topRankService.createComputedStoreSlot(
    db,
    () => cardService.getSlotByKey(cards, 'c1').entity?.rank ?? -1,
    () => ({ sourceSlots: [cardService.getSlotByKey(cards, 'c1')] }),
);
const heldTopRank = topRankService.computedSingleSlotService.holdSingleSlot(topRank);   // the same slot while anything holds it
heldTopRank.computedValueService.getValueForSlot(heldTopRank);
heldTopRank.owner.unholdSlot(heldTopRank);        // gone; the next holdSingleSlot(topRank) mints a new one
```

A single computed store slot has no key and a store of one slot. `getSingleSlot(storeSlot)` hands a slot without a hold — a fresh one goes to the unused-slot collector and is let go at the
next flush unless something holds it — and `holdSlotByKey(storeSlot, undefined)` holds the live slot, minting
one if the previous is gone. A computed slot goes at its last unhold once no effect reads it
(`OIMSlotAtUnholdReleasePolicy`, the default), and gives back the holds it took on its
sources. A last unhold during a flush releases at the end of that flush, through the
db's unused-slot collector, as for every non-empty slot. The holds a computed takes on its sources and
gives back are one stateless service, shared by both shapes.

**`createSources` takes the key and the store slot, and nothing else. There is no `keep`.** A build that
needs a source resolves it with `holdSlotByKey` or `getSlotByKey` like any other caller,
and the holds the service itself takes are the ones named in
`sourceSlots` / `sourceComputeds` — so the source list IS the dependency
list, and a source a build closes over without naming is a source nothing holds.

**A derivation is never empty.** `OIMComputedService` answers
"empty" with `false`, so a filed derivation is released only when nothing holds
it, nothing watches it, and the grace is `0` — which is what
`OIMSlotAtUnholdReleasePolicy` answers, and the default when no `slotReleasePolicy` is given.

```ts setup
const rankService = createOIMComputedService<TOIMStoreKey, number>({
    createSources: ({ key }) => ({ sourceSlots: [cardService.getSlotByKey(cards, key)] }),
    derive: (computedSlot) => cardService.getSlotByKey(cards, computedSlot.key).entity?.rank ?? -1,
    sameValueGuard: oimSameValueZeroGuard,
    initialValue: -1,
});
const ranks = rankService.createComputedStoreSlot(db);
```

```ts
const rank = rankService.computedCollectionService.holdSlotByKey(ranks, 'c1');
rank.computedValueService.getValueForSlot(rank);
rank.owner.unholdSlot(rank);
```

### Computed columns

A computed's value can be subscribed to by field. `getColumn(slot, columnName)`, `holdColumn(slot, columnName)`,
`getColumnGroup(names)`, `holdColumnGroup(slot, group)`, `unholdColumn(columnSlot)`, and the
any-column pair `getAnyColumn(slot)` / `holdAnyColumn(slot)` are on `computedCollectionService`
(so on the sorted and memo services too), for keyed and single store slots alike; a single one passes
`getSlotByKey(storeSlot, undefined)` as the slot. Column names are typed as the keys of the value.

A computed service's column owner is the derive-driven strategy: each column slot is a computed slot
over the carrier computed, its value `carrier.value[column]` (a tuple of the group's fields, ordered by the sorted column names, for a group,
the whole value for the any-column), compared with `Object.is`. It is a `TOIMComputedColumnSlot`
(`TOIMComputedSlot<unknown, string>`), so it goes in the SECOND array of `createEffect`, and its value
is read off `columnSlot.value`. It wakes an effect only when that field of the derived value changes.
Pinned by `facade/computed/tests/what-a-computed-column-wakes-on.test.ts`.

```ts
type Summary = { top: number; count: number };
const summaryService = createOIMSingleComputedService<Summary>();
const summary = summaryService.createComputedStoreSlot(
    db,
    () => ({ top: slot.entity?.rank ?? -1, count: cardService.getSlotCount(cards) }),
    () => ({ sourceSlots: [slot] }),
);
const summarySingleSlotService = summaryService.computedSingleSlotService;
const summaryTop = summarySingleSlotService.columnSlotService.holdColumn(summarySingleSlotService.getSingleSlot(summary), 'top');
const topEffect = effectService.createEffect(db, [], [summaryTop], () => { paint(slot.entity); });
effectService.disposeEffect(topEffect);
summarySingleSlotService.columnSlotService.unholdColumn(summaryTop);
```

### The order of a bucket, as one derivation per key

```ts signature
createOIMBucketMemoComputedService<TKey, TBucketMemberSlot extends TOIMSlot, TSlots, TBucketStore, TComputedStore?>({
    bucketCollectionService: OIMSlotCollectionService<TKey, TOIMBucketSlot<TSlots, TKey>, TBucketStore, OIMSlotContentBucketService<TBucketMemberSlot, TSlots>, …>;
    slotReleasePolicy?: IOIMSlotReleasePolicy;      // default OIMSlotAtUnholdReleasePolicy.INSTANCE
    columnSlotStoreService?: IOIMSlotStoreService<string, TOIMComputedColumnSlot>;
    computedSlotStoreService?: IOIMSlotStoreService<TKey, TOIMComputedSlot<readonly TBucketMemberSlot[], TKey>, TComputedStore>;
}): OIMBucketMemoComputedService<TKey, TBucketMemberSlot, TSlots, TBucketStore, TComputedStore>

createBucketMemoStoreSlot(bucketStoreSlot: TOIMStoreSlot<TBucketStore, TOIMBucketSlot<TSlots, TKey>, readonly TBucketMemberSlot[]>): TOIMStoreSlot<TComputedStore, TOIMBucketMemoComputedSlot<TBucketMemberSlot, TKey>>
```

It takes no db: a memo store slot runs on the channel slot of the bucket store slot it reads. The class is
`new OIMBucketMemoComputedService(options)` (options type `TOIMBucketMemoComputedServiceOptions`), whose
`computedCollectionService` reads the per-key derivations; `createBucketMemoStoreSlot(bucketStoreSlot)` makes
one memo store slot over one bucket store slot.

Subscribe to THIS, not to the bucket, when a consumer wants the list as an array
it can compare by identity. The value is the bucket's slots in the bucket's order;
it is produced on the read that asks for it and never while nothing reads it, and
its `changedAtRevision` and `changedAtEpoch` move only when the list a reader would
see actually changed. The list is handed back by IDENTITY: it is the same array for
as long as the list holds, so a consumer memoising on identity needs no comparison
of its own. For a SORTED list use [`createOIMSortedComputedService`](#sorted-lists).

The source list is ONE slot — the bucket — and it never grows: a bucket
change is a move of the bucket's value, not of the derivation's sources.

```ts
const orderService = createOIMBucketMemoComputedService({
    bucketCollectionService: orderedService,
});
const order = orderService.createBucketMemoStoreSlot(ordered);
const deck = orderService.computedCollectionService.holdSlotByKey(order, 'spades');        // mints the bucket too, and holds it
effectService.createEffect(db, [], [deck], () => render(deck.computedValueService.getValueForSlot(deck)));
```

---

## Key stores

```ts signature
interface IOIMSlotStoreService<TKey, TSlot extends TOIMKeyedSlot = TOIMKeyedSlot, TStore = unknown> {
    createStore(): TStore;
    ownKey<TOwnedKey extends TKey>(key: TOwnedKey): TOwnedKey;
    isSameKey(key: TKey, otherKey: TKey): boolean;
    get(store: TStore, key: TKey): TSlot | undefined;
    set(store: TStore, key: TKey, slot: TSlot): void;
    remove(store: TStore, key: TKey): void;
    getSlots(store: TStore): IterableIterator<TSlot>;
    getSlotCount(store: TStore): number;
}
```

**The store service is STATELESS and the storage is its first argument.** It
builds the storage with `createStore()` and the store slot keeps it, as `storeSlot.store`; `getSlotCount` is a
method taking that storage, not a getter. One store service instance can
therefore serve every store slot of every service in a process.

**`ownKey(key)` is the key a slot is minted with, and the store never touches a
slot.** The content service asks it once, before the slot owner's `createSlot`, so the slot's `key` is
written by its owner and no one else. The map-driven store answers the key itself;
the tree-driven one answers a copy of the composite key, so a caller reusing the
array it handed in cannot change the key of a slot already filed.

**`isSameKey(key, otherKey)` is what the store means by one key.** The map-driven
store answers SameValueZero; the tree-driven one compares length and then every
part by SameValueZero, so two arrays with the same parts are one key. Every collection
service answers the same question as `service.isSameKey(key, otherKey)`, asking
its own store service; an index deciding whether a key moved first checks `===` (the key
columns did not change) and otherwise asks its bucket store service.

```ts signature
type TOIMSlotStoreTree<TSlot, TCompositeKeyPart> = {
    readonly root: TOIMCompositeKeyNode<TSlot, TCompositeKeyPart>;
    readonly slots: Set<TSlot>;
};

type TOIMCompositeKeyNode<TAtKey = unknown, TCompositeKeyPart = TOIMEntitySlot> = {
    childNodes: Map<TCompositeKeyPart, TOIMCompositeKeyNode<TAtKey, TCompositeKeyPart>> | undefined;
    atThisKey: TAtKey | undefined;
};
```

`TOIMSlotStoreTree` is what `OIMSlotTreeStoreService.createStore()` builds:
the tree's root plus a flat `Set` of every filed slot, which makes `getSlots()` and
`getSlotCount()` O(1) rather than a walk, and keeps `getSlots()` in filing order like every other store.
`TOIMCompositeKeyNode` is one level of that tree — a `Map` from composite key part to the
level below, created only when the first longer key is filed under it (a leaf has
`childNodes: undefined`), and the slot, if any, whose key ends here. Both are exported so a caller can annotate the storage they
are holding; neither is something you build by hand.

| Store | Key type |
|---|---|
| `OIMSlotMapStoreService<TSlot>` | `TOIMStoreKey` = `string \| number` |
| `OIMSlotTreeStoreService<TOIMStoreKey, TSlot>` built with `OIMDefaults.KEY_TREE_WALK_SCALAR.getValue()` | `readonly TOIMStoreKey[]` — **a chain of VALUES** |
| `OIMSlotTreeStoreService<TOIMEntitySlot, TSlot>` built with `OIMDefaults.KEY_TREE_WALK_COMPOSITE.getValue()` | `readonly TOIMEntitySlot[]` — **a chain of entity SLOTS** |
| `OIMSingleSlotStoreService.INSTANCE` | `void` — one slot per store slot, its store a `TOIMSingleSlotStore` (`{ slot }`); what every single is built on |

Two stores for keys, one per shape of address, and the single-slot store for no key. The chain store descends one `Map`
lookup per composite key part, keeps `[a]` and `[a, b]` apart, and has **no encoding step**:
`JSON.stringify` and a NUL-join were both rejected — the latter was not
injective, so `['a b']` and `['a', 'b']` were one key.

**The two DESCENTS are a fork chosen at construction, and the choice is about
lifetime.** The store takes an `IOIMKeyTreeWalk<TCompositeKeyPart>` as its only
constructor argument; there is no runtime branch on what a composite key part is, and the
first type parameter is the composite key part type. Do not treat the strategies as one store
with looser typing, and do not expect a class per strategy — there is one store class
and two walks.

```ts signature
interface IOIMKeyTreeWalk<TCompositeKeyPart> {
    mintNodeAt<TAtKey>(
        rootCompositeKeyNode: TOIMCompositeKeyNode<TAtKey, TCompositeKeyPart>,
        compositeKey: readonly TCompositeKeyPart[],
    ): TOIMCompositeKeyNode<TAtKey, TCompositeKeyPart>;
    nodeAt<TAtKey>(
        rootCompositeKeyNode: TOIMCompositeKeyNode<TAtKey, TCompositeKeyPart>,
        compositeKey: readonly TCompositeKeyPart[],
    ): TOIMCompositeKeyNode<TAtKey, TCompositeKeyPart> | undefined;
    deleteKey<TAtKey>(
        rootCompositeKeyNode: TOIMCompositeKeyNode<TAtKey, TCompositeKeyPart>,
        compositeKey: readonly TCompositeKeyPart[],
    ): TAtKey | undefined;
}
```

`deleteKey` takes the value filed at the key and hands it back, in one descent:
one `Map.get` per key part and no array of the path. On the way back up it
unlinks every node the delete left empty and stops at the first one that still
holds a value or leads to a longer key, so `['u1', 'p7', 'x']` survives a delete
of `['u1', 'p7']`. A key that is only a prefix of filed keys, or reaches nothing,
deletes nothing and returns `undefined`.

| Walk | Class | Shared instance | What a composite key part is | Holds? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| scalar | `OIMScalarKeyTreeWalk` | `OIMDefaults.KEY_TREE_WALK_SCALAR.getValue()` | `TOIMStoreKey` | no |
| composite | `OIMCompositeKeyTreeWalk` | `OIMDefaults.KEY_TREE_WALK_COMPOSITE.getValue()` | `TOIMEntitySlot` | **yes — one hold per edge** |

**The hold is the whole difference.** `OIMCompositeKeyTreeWalk.mintNodeAt` calls
`holdCompositeKeyPart` the first time it creates an edge, which runs
`entitySlot.owner.holdSlot(entitySlot)`; `deleteKey` calls `unholdCompositeKeyPart` on
exactly the edges it unlinked, deepest first and only after every unlink is done, which runs `entitySlot.owner.unholdSlot(entitySlot)` unless
`oimIsSlotReleased(entitySlot)` — so an entity slot stays addressable for
as long as its composite key parts are, and a composite key part nothing else refers to goes the
moment the last entity keyed on it does. The scalar walk holds nothing: a value has
no identity to keep alive. Both throw `an empty key is not a key` on `[]`.

Construct the classes yourself only if you want your own instance; both walks are
stateless, and the shared one on `OIMDefaults` is what you normally pass.

```ts
// A CHAIN OF VALUES — `['deck-1', 'red']`.
type TScalarChain = readonly TOIMStoreKey[];
type Tally = { deck: string; day: string; count: number };
type TTallyStore = import('@oimdb/core').TOIMSlotStoreTree<TOIMEntitySlot<Tally, TScalarChain>, TOIMStoreKey>;

const tallyService = createOIMSlotCollectionService<
    ReturnType<typeof createOIMSlotContentEntityService<Tally, TScalarChain>>, TTallyStore
>(db, {
    slotContentService: createOIMSlotContentEntityService<Tally, TScalarChain>(db),
    slotStoreService: new OIMSlotTreeStoreService<TOIMStoreKey, TOIMEntitySlot<Tally, TScalarChain>>(
        OIMDefaults.KEY_TREE_WALK_SCALAR.getValue(),
    ),
});
const tallies = tallyService.createStoreSlot(db);
tallyService.writeSlotContentByKey(tallies, ['spades', 'mon'], { deck: 'spades', day: 'mon', count: 1 });
tallyService.getSlotByKey(tallies, ['spades', 'mon']);
```

```ts
// A CHAIN OF IDENTITIES — each composite key part is a slot, and each edge takes a counted
// hold on it, so the entity keeps its composite key parts resolvable for as long as it is
// addressable.
type User = { id: string };
type Group = { id: string };
declare const alice: TOIMEntitySlot<User, TOIMStoreKey>;
declare const admins: TOIMEntitySlot<Group, TOIMStoreKey>;

type Enrolment = {
    user: TOIMEntitySlot<User, TOIMStoreKey>;
    group: TOIMEntitySlot<Group, TOIMStoreKey>;
    since: number;
};
type TChain = readonly TOIMEntitySlot[];
type TEnrolmentStore = import('@oimdb/core').TOIMSlotStoreTree<TOIMEntitySlot<Enrolment, TChain>, TOIMEntitySlot>;

const enrolmentService = createOIMSlotCollectionService<
    ReturnType<typeof createOIMSlotContentEntityService<Enrolment, TChain>>, TEnrolmentStore
>(db, {
    slotContentService: createOIMSlotContentEntityService<Enrolment, TChain>(db),
    slotStoreService: new OIMSlotTreeStoreService<TOIMEntitySlot, TOIMEntitySlot<Enrolment, TChain>>(
        OIMDefaults.KEY_TREE_WALK_COMPOSITE.getValue(),
    ),
});
const enrolments = enrolmentService.createStoreSlot(db);
enrolmentService.writeSlotContentByKey(enrolments, [alice, admins], { user: alice, group: admins, since: 2026 });
enrolmentService.getSlotByKey(enrolments, [alice, admins]);
```

**Never put a scalar in a composite-walk key.** It is a type error, and
past a cast it throws a TypeError inside the mint, setting `holdCount` on a
string, after the edge is already in the tree. `OIMDefaults.KEY_TREE_WALK_SCALAR.getValue()` is
the walk for that key — the same store class, the other strategy.

**Compare a chain with the strategy that matches it**: `oimSameSlotSequence` for identities
(reference, per composite key part), `oimSameKeySequence` for a chain or list of values.
`oimSameSlotSequence` over a scalar chain is the `NaN` defect — it answers "a different
address" for the address the tree is looking at.

---

## Lifetime — the owner protocol

**`slot.owner` is the only reference a slot carries, and it is never
`undefined`.** Every slot minted anywhere has one; a slot nothing filed carries
`OIMDefaults.STANDALONE_SLOT_OWNER.getValue()`, a slot a collection filed carries that collection type's slot owner (an `OIMSlotOwnerService`) — keyed or single alike — and a slot that has been released KEEPS its owner
and raises the RELEASED flag in `slot.slotFlags` instead, which the doors below read.

```ts signature
interface IOIMSlotOwner {
    holdSlot(slot: TOIMSlot): void;
    unholdSlot(slot: TOIMSlot): void;
    releaseSlotIfUnheld(slot: TOIMSlot): void;
    subscribeToSlot(slot: TOIMSlot, effect: TOIMEffect, edge: number): number;
    unsubscribeFromSlot(slot: TOIMSlot, at: number, effect: TOIMEffect): boolean;
}
```

At a deadline the release queue reads its MARKER off the slot, decides, and calls
`releaseSlotIfUnheld` itself. The owner has no "how long is left" question.

| Door | What it is for |
|---|---|
| `holdSlot(slot)` | `holdCount++`. That is all — no handle, no `{ slot, release }` record. **Throws by name** on a released slot |
| `unholdSlot(slot)` | `holdCount--`, then run `releaseSlotIfUnheld`. **It opens no window** — nothing is stamped here, so a slot whose deadline has passed goes at this call. **Throws by name** on a released slot, and when `holdCount` is already `0`: a second unhold against one hold would release a slot somebody else is reading |
| `releaseSlotIfUnheld(slot)` | run the release guard. Releases only an unheld, unreferenced, still-owned, out-of-grace slot; **returns silently** on one already released |
| `subscribeToSlot(slot, effect, edge)` | push the effect onto `slot.effects` and its `edge` (which of the effect's sources this slot is) onto `slot.effectEdges`, and hand back **the position**, which the effect remembers. **It takes a hold** through `holdSlot`, so a subscribed slot is a held one and nothing can subscribe without holding. **Throws by name** on a released slot: a subscriber filed on one would never be woken |
| `unsubscribeFromSlot(slot, at, effect)` | swap the tail of both arrays into `at`, tell the moved effect its new position at its edge (one write, no search), and **if that emptied the list, `onSlotIdle(slot)` opens a fresh idle window**, then give the subscription's hold back through `unholdSlot`; hand back whether it unfiled. Unfiling by remembered position is why taking N subscribers off one identity is O(N) and not quadratic. **Throws by name** on a released slot |

**`OIMSlotOwner`** is the base class and it is concrete: it implements all five.
Its `releaseSlotIfUnheld` does nothing, its
`unsafeMutateSlot(slot, mutateSlot)` hands `mutateSlot` the slot as `TOIMSlotEditable` with no
guard at all (it exists so a library that adds its own release wheel can keep its own bit in
`slot.slotFlags`; the engine owns bits `1`, `2`, `4`, `8` and `16`, so a library starts at `32`;
it is on the owner so a subclass can hook every such mutation), and a `protected
onSlotIdle` does nothing; a `protected assertNotReleased` is what every refusing
door above calls. `OIMSlotOwnerService` overrides `onSlotIdle` and
`releaseSlotIfUnheld`, asking its release policy and its content service; the clock is the slot's channel slot's.
Extend `OIMSlotOwner` when you own slots that no collection files.
**`OIMDefaults.STANDALONE_SLOT_OWNER`** is one shared instance of it — the owner of a
computed slot nobody has filed. It never releases anything, which is exactly what
"filed nowhere, so nothing can unfile it" means. A single's slot is not such a slot: its
owner is its collection type's slot owner, and that release policy applies to it.

### The column owner

**Columns are a module of every collection.** The column slots of a carrier slot live
in `carrierSlot.columnSlotStore`, a field of the base `TOIMSlot`, so any slot can carry
them — an entity slot, a bucket slot, a computed slot. `OIMColumnSlotOwner` is abstract, an
`OIMSlotOwner` subclass, with two strategies:
`OIMPushColumnSlotOwner` (plain column slots woken by marks on a write; entity and bucket collections,
keyed and single) and `OIMPullColumnSlotOwner` (each column slot a computed slot over its carrier;
computed collections, keyed and single). The factory hands the strategy's factory to the slot owner as
`createColumnSlotOwner`. Each collection type has its own column owner, and every column slot it mints names that
owner as its `owner`. The owner holds only the column slot store service; the column state — the column
groups and which columns are referenced — lives on the store slot. The collection exposes it only
through its column doors: `getColumn(slot, columnName)`, `holdColumn(slot, columnName)`,
`unholdColumn(columnSlot)`, `getColumnGroup(names)`, `holdColumnGroup(slot, group)` (on
a single the same doors, with the slot `getSingleSlot(storeSlot)` hands back; the computed ones take a computed slot
and return a `TOIMComputedColumnSlot`), and `getAnyColumn(slot)` / `holdAnyColumn(slot)`.
A column slot is released the moment its last effect is disposed and nothing holds it:
disposing the effect gives its hold back through the column owner, which then runs its own
`releaseSlotIfUnheld`, which stops on `holdCount > 0` or a non-empty `effects`,
takes the column out of the carrier slot's column store — dropping that store
entirely when it empties — sets the RELEASED flag of `columnSlot`, and then runs
`carrierSlot.owner.releaseSlotIfUnheld(carrierSlot)`, because a carrier kept alive only by
a watched column is one nothing watches any more. This guard is the one place a store
lookup survives — it compares `columnSlotStoreService.get(columnSlotStore, columnSlot.key)`
against the column slot — because a column is filed on its carrier slot, not in the
store slot that the `owner` check covers.
`OIMSlotOwnerService`'s release guard refuses while `slot.columnSlotStore` stands,
so a slot with any live column slot is never released.

---

## Ordered lists

### Disposers

The disposers this package hands back are the unsubscribes `OIMChannelService.INSTANCE.subscribeAfterEachFrame`
and its siblings return, and the one `effectService.subscribeEffect(db, sourceSlots, sourceComputeds, body)`
returns. An effect from `createEffect` has none, so the caller writes
`() => effectService.disposeEffect(effect)`. A hold is given back through its owner, not through a disposer.

```ts
const effect = effectService.createEffect(db, [slot], [], () => { paint(slot.entity); });
const disposers: TOIMDisposer[] = [];
disposers.push(() => { effectService.disposeEffect(effect); });
disposers.push(() => { slot.owner.unholdSlot(slot); });
for (let i = disposers.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) disposers[i]();
```

### `oimOrderedListCommandsOfTransition`

```ts signature
oimOrderedListCommandsOfTransition(
    prev: readonly TOIMEntitySlot[],
    next: readonly TOIMEntitySlot[],
    maxCommandsPerSlot?: number,   // commands per slot of `next`; left out, it NEVER resets
): TOIMOrderedListCommand[]

type TOIMOrderedListCommand =
    | { type: 'insert'; index: number; slot: TOIMEntitySlot }
    | { type: 'remove'; index: number }
    | { type: 'move'; from: number; to: number }
    | { type: 'reset'; slots: readonly TOIMEntitySlot[] };
```

A free function, not a method on `OIMChannelService`: a class's methods cannot be
dropped one at a time by a bundler.

`prev` MUST BE A SNAPSHOT TAKEN WHERE YOU RENDERED. Every member read on a bucket
content service hands back the LIVE list — declared `Iterable`, not an array, so
`Array.from(bucketService.slotContentService.getBucketMemberSlots(bucketSlot))` is required and is the copy. A `prev` kept
live is the same array as `next` on the following frame: the diff is empty,
no reorder is ever drawn, and nothing throws. The other safe `prev` is
`createOIMBucketMemoComputedService`'s value — a fresh array on every write that
changed the list, the same array while it did not.

A LIST MAY NAME ONE SLOT TWICE, and then it holds that slot twice.
`OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService` records every mention, so an ordered bucket's list is exactly such a list. The
mentions of one identity are matched in the order they appear, and the script
reproduces `next` mention for mention. The minimal move count (`common − LIS`)
is claimed for lists whose identities are distinct: where the two lists name one
identity a different number of times, which mentions are matched decides how
long the common subsequence can be, and matching them in order does not always
leave the longest.

---

## Types

```ts signature
type TOIMStoreKey = string | number;
type TOIMDisposer = () => void;
type TOIMEffectBody = () => (() => void) | void;   // a returned function is the undo
type TOIMEffectBodyWithSourceTracking = (effectSourceTracker: OIMEffectSourceTracker) => (() => void) | void;
type TOIMSameValueGuard<TValue = unknown> = (prev: TValue, next: TValue) => boolean;
type TOIMChannelScheduler = (flush: () => void) => void;
type TOIMSortColumn<TEntity extends object> = { column: TOIMSortableColumnName<TEntity>; direction: 'asc' | 'desc' };
type TOIMSortableColumnName<TEntity extends object> =   // a column whose values are string | number | bigint
    { [TColumn in keyof TEntity]-?: NonNullable<TEntity[TColumn]> extends string | number | bigint ? TColumn : never }[keyof TEntity] & string;

// EVERY property is `readonly`. A slot is written through its owner and its
// service, never by assigning to it; `TOIMSlotEditable` is how the engine
// itself drops that guard where it is the one mutator.
type TOIMSlot = {
    readonly effects: TOIMEffect[] | undefined;
    readonly effectEdges: number[] | undefined; // beside each effect, which of its sources this slot is
    readonly changedAtRevision: number;
    readonly changedAtEpoch: number;
    readonly holdCount: number;
    readonly releaseDueAfterWriteMs: number; // -1 until a write stamps it
    readonly releaseDueAfterIdleMs: number;  // -1 until idleness stamps it
    readonly releaseDueAfterUnholdMs: number; // -1 until the last unhold stamps it
    readonly slotFlags: number;        // OIM_SLOT_FLAG_EMPTY = 1, OIM_SLOT_FLAG_RELEASED = 2
    readonly columnSlotStore: unknown; // the column slots this slot carries; undefined while none
    readonly storeSlot: TOIMStoreSlot | undefined;
    readonly owner: IOIMSlotOwner;     // never undefined, never cleared
};

// A store slot is NOT a slot: nothing holds, subscribes or wakes it. It is the state of one
// collection instance — its store, its channel slot, its listeners and column state — and every
// service that touches it is stateless. Only the fields a consumer reads are shown.
type TOIMStoreSlot<TStore = unknown, TSlot extends TOIMSlot = TOIMSlot, TPatch = unknown> = {
    readonly store: TStore;
    readonly channelSlot: TOIMChannelSlot;
    readonly contentChangeListeners: IOIMContentChangeListener<TSlot, TPatch>[] | undefined;
    readonly contentChangeListenerReadColumnNames: (readonly string[] | undefined)[] | undefined;
    readonly indexKeysPositions: TOIMIndexKeysPositions | undefined;
    readonly sourceStoreSlot: TOIMStoreSlot | undefined;   // an index store slot's source
    readonly isDisposed: boolean;                          // an index store slot after disposeIndexStoreSlot
    readonly slotService: TSlotService;                    // the service that created the store slot
    readonly batchDepth: number;                           // openBatch / closeBatch nesting
    // … column-reader counts, column groups, batch queues, bucket write queues: the services' own
};

type TOIMSingleSlotStore<TSlot> = { slot: TSlot | undefined };
type TOIMSingleSlotStoreSlot<TSlot extends TOIMSlot, TPatch = unknown> = TOIMStoreSlot<TOIMSingleSlotStore<TSlot>, TSlot, TPatch>;

type TOIMIndexStoreSlot<TStore, TBucketSlot, TBucketPatch, TSourceSlot, TSourcePatch, TKey, TSourceStore> =
    TOIMStoreSlot<TStore, TBucketSlot, TBucketPatch> & {
        readonly sourceStoreSlot: TOIMStoreSlot<TSourceStore, TSourceSlot, TSourcePatch>;
        readonly indexKeysPosition: number;
        readonly contentChangeListener: IOIMContentChangeListener<TSourceSlot, TSourcePatch>;
        readonly requestedKeys: readonly TKey[] | undefined;
        readonly bucketColumnNames: Set<string>;
        readonly isAnyBucketColumnRead: boolean;
        readonly isDisposed: boolean;
    };

type TOIMComputedStoreSlot<TStore = unknown, TValue = unknown, TKey = unknown> =
    TOIMStoreSlot<TStore, TOIMComputedSlot<TValue, TKey>> & {
        readonly derive: ((computedSlot: TOIMComputedSlot<TValue, TKey>) => TValue) | undefined;
        readonly createSources: ((key: TKey, storeSlot: TOIMStoreSlot | undefined) => Partial<TOIMComputedSources>) | undefined;
    };

type TOIMSlotEditable<TSlot> = { -readonly [K in keyof TSlot]: TSlot[K] };

type TOIMKeyedSlot<TKey = unknown> = TOIMSlot & { readonly key: TKey };
type TOIMIndexableSlot<TKey = unknown> = TOIMKeyedSlot<TKey> & { readonly indexKeys: unknown[] | undefined };

type TOIMEntitySlot<TEntity extends object = object, TKey = unknown> = TOIMIndexableSlot<TKey> & {
    readonly entity: TEntity | undefined;
    readonly data: unknown[] | undefined;
};

// `data` belongs to the consumer: the core never reads or writes it, and clearing or
// removing the slot (`slotContentService.clearSlotContent(slot)`) does not reset it. Each index keeps its
// last key for the entity slot in `indexKeys`, through the db's `IOIMIndexKeysService`.

type TOIMColumnSlot = TOIMSlot & {
    readonly carrierSlot: TOIMSlot;    // the entity slot or bucket slot it hangs off
    readonly key: string;
};

type TOIMComputedColumnSlot = TOIMComputedSlot<unknown, string>;   // a computed's getColumn / holdColumn return it; it goes in createEffect's second list

type TOIMBucketContentSlot<TSlots = unknown> = TOIMSlot & {
    readonly owner: IOIMSlotOwner;
    readonly storeSlot: TOIMStoreSlot<unknown, TOIMBucketContentSlot<TSlots>>;
    readonly bucketSlotsStore: TSlots;
    readonly commands: readonly TOIMOrderedListCommand[] | undefined;   // emptied when the flush has ended
    readonly isWholeListRecorded: boolean;                               // reset to false with it
    readonly commandsStartedAtRevision: number;                          // the clock the script started at
    readonly commandsStartedAtEpoch: number;
};
type TOIMBucketSlot<TSlots = unknown, TKey extends NonNullable<unknown> = NonNullable<unknown>> =
    TOIMBucketContentSlot<TSlots> & TOIMIndexableSlot<TKey>;   // a keyed bucket slot; a single bucket is the content slot alone

// `holdSlotByKey(storeSlot, key)` hands back the slot itself; give the hold back with `slot.owner.unholdSlot(slot)`.

type TOIMBucketSlotsSetStore<TBucketMemberSlot extends TOIMSlot = TOIMSlot> = Set<TBucketMemberSlot>;
type TOIMBucketSlotsArrayStore<TBucketMemberSlot extends TOIMSlot = TOIMSlot> = {
    bucketMemberSlots: TBucketMemberSlot[];
    uniqueBucketMemberSlots: Set<TBucketMemberSlot> | undefined;   // kept by OIMBucketUniqueMemberSlotsArrayService
    sortedCount: number;
};

type TOIMEntityColumnName<TEntity extends object> =
    [TEntity] extends [never] ? never
        : object extends TEntity ? string : keyof TEntity & string;

type TOIMDerivation = TOIMComputedSources & {   // what a computed slot and a TOIMEffect share
    ranAtRevision: number; ranAtEpoch: number;
};

type TOIMTimer = (run: () => void, inMs: number) => TOIMDisposer;
```

**`TOIMSlotEditable<TSlot>` strips `readonly` from every property.** It is exported
because the rule "data has one mutator" is enforced by the slot types being
readonly everywhere else: a class that IS the sole mutator of a slot's property
casts through this type at the one place it writes, and every other reader is
stopped by the compiler. `IOIMSlotStamp.stamp` takes one, which is what lets a
stamp write `releaseDueAfterWriteMs` and nothing else write it. **Do not reach for this to
work around a compile error** — if you need it and you do not own the property,
the mutation belongs on whoever does.

Comparison helpers — one per shape of address, plus the value rule. Use the one
that matches what you are comparing; they are not interchangeable.

| Helper | Compares | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `oimSameValueZeroGuard(prev, next)` | a stored value, or one scalar address | SameValueZero |
| `oimSameSlotSequence(prev, next)` | `readonly TOIMSlot[]` — a chain of identities | positional, by reference |
| `oimSameKeySequence(keys, otherKeys)` | `readonly TKey[]` — a list of keys or a chain of values | positional, SameValueZero per key |

---
