## Known defects

### A scalar in a `KEY_TREE_WALK_COMPOSITE` key throws

`OIMSlotTreeStoreService` built with `OIMDefaults.KEY_TREE_WALK_COMPOSITE.getValue()` keys on
`readonly TOIMEntitySlot[]`, so a string or a number in the key throws
a TypeError past a cast, setting `holdCount` on a string. The store for a tuple
of scalars is `OIMSlotTreeStoreService` built with
`OIMDefaults.KEY_TREE_WALK_SCALAR.getValue()` —
see **Key stores** above. The fix is the other walk, never a cast.

### `TOIMEffect` is a type-only export

`effectService.createEffect(...)` and `effectService.createEffectImmediate(...)` are the whole of
legitimate construction. An object literal typed `TOIMEffect` subscribes to nothing and
schedules nothing: when one of its sources already moved in the open batch, a
later write to that source is swallowed by the coalescing guard and the effect
silently sits out the frame it is owed. Scheduling it is what `createEffect`
does after constructing it.

### Mixing `import` and `require` of `@oimdb/core` throws at the second load

Every `@oimdb` package ships both formats — `dist/index.js` for `import`,
`dist/index.cjs` for `require` (with `dist/index.d.cts` under the `require`
condition so a CommonJS consumer's declarations match its runtime), both named
in the `exports` map. A runtime loads a package once per format, so a process
that reaches the core both ways would hold two copies of every class and every
module-level value — two `OIMDefaults`, so a default set through one never
reaches a service built by the other.

So `src/index.ts` registers its copy under `Symbol.for('@oimdb/core')` on
`globalThis`, and the second copy to load throws
`@oimdb/core is loaded twice in this process`. The same throw fires for two
installed copies of the package.

`@oimdb/react` loaded twice fails loudly instead: every hook throws
`useOIMDB: no <OIMDBProvider db={...}> above this component.` with the provider plainly above it, because a React
context's identity is its lookup key.

Do not generate code that reaches `@oimdb/core` — or any package that passes
core objects around — through both spellings in one process. Pick one.

---

## Other packages

`@oimdb/react`, `@oimdb/persist` (with its five backends) and `@oimdb/exodra` build
on the current core — persist and exodra have sections of their own below. Every
remaining package imports only names the core exports. Read a package's own
source before generating code against it.

`@oimdb/react` — `<OIMDBProvider db={db}>` carries the `OIMDB` (`useOIMDB()`) and nothing else: the effect
service is stateless (`OIMEffectService.INSTANCE`) and every hook subscribes with
`OIMEffectService.INSTANCE.subscribeEffect(db, …)`. A hook that resolves or takes a slot filed on another `OIMDB`
throws, since nothing below would wake. Every hook that reads a collection takes the collection service, typed as a
`Pick` of `OIMSlotCollectionService` with only the members it calls, and then the store slot:
`useOIMEntity(entityCollectionService, entityStoreSlot, key)`,
`useOIMField(entityCollectionService, slot, name)` (calls `getColumn(slot, name)`; no store slot, the slot carries it),
`useOIMBucketSlots(bucketCollectionService, bucketSlot)` and
`useOIMBucketSlotsByKey(bucketCollectionService, bucketStoreSlot, key)` (both read
`bucketCollectionService.slotContentService.getBucketMemberSlots`; an index service and its index store slot fit too), and
`useOIMValue(binding)`, where a binding is `{ sourceSlots?, sourceComputeds?, derive }` (a missing list means none)
and must keep its identity across renders.
`useOIMComputedValue(computedSlot: TOIMComputedSlot<TValue>): TValue` is the one-computed case: it subscribes to
the slot, settles it and reads `computedSlot.value`, with no binding to memoise.
`useOIMComputedValueByKey(computedService.computedCollectionService, computedStoreSlot, key)` reads one key of a
computed store slot (plain, sorted, bucket memo) with the same by-key body as `useOIMEntity` /
`useOIMBucketSlotsByKey`: resolve on commit with `holdSlotByKey`, effect over that slot, resolve-hold given back,
a key built inline settled by meaning.
The computed SERVICE is the caller's, built once at module scope with `createOIMComputedService(options)` (no db).
`useOIMComputedCollection(computedService, derive, createSources, deps): TOIMComputedStoreSlot` builds only a store
slot per mount — `computedService.createComputedStoreSlot(db, derive, createSources)` in a `useMemo` on `deps`;
`derive` / `createSources` may be `undefined` when the service has them.
`useOIMSingleComputedValue(computedService, derive, createSources, deps): TValue` is the same for a void-keyed
service whose `computedSlotStoreService` is `OIMSingleSlotStoreService.INSTANCE`, read through
`useOIMComputedValueByKey(computedService.computedCollectionService, computedStoreSlot, undefined)`, so a flush
between render and subscribe is safe.
`useOIMSlotsByKeys(slotCollectionService, storeSlot, keys)` holds the identities its keys name for as long as the
component is mounted (a `holdSlotByKey` per key on commit, the same holds given back on unmount or when the list
moves) and subscribes to nothing; it needs no provider.
Singles are not keyed collections: `createOIMSingleSlotService(db, { slotContentService })` returns an
`OIMWritableSingleSlotService` (`getSingleSlot(storeSlot)`, `holdSingleSlot(storeSlot)`), read by
`useOIMSingleEntity(singleSlotService, singleSlotStoreSlot): TEntity | undefined` and
`useOIMSingleBucketSlots(singleSlotService, singleSlotStoreSlot): readonly TOIMEntitySlot<TEntity>[]` — the by-key
mechanics without a key (getSingleSlot on render, holdSingleSlot on commit, resolve-hold given back once the
effect exists; the bucket members are copied per render). See `packages/react/README.md`.

What each imports from `@oimdb/core`, read out of `src/`. The source moves —
re-read the imports rather than trusting this table.

| Package | Imports from the core | Imports a name the core does not export? |
|---|---|---|
| `@oimdb/persist` | `IOIMChannelMap`, `IOIMContentChangeListener`, `IOIMEntityWriter`, `OIMChannelService`, `OIMPushColumnSlotOwner`, `OIMContentChangeListenerService`, `OIMEffectService`, `OIMSingleSlotService`, `OIMSlotCollectionService`, `OIMSlotContentBucketService`, `OIMSlotContentEntityService`, `TOIMBucketSlot`, `TOIMChannelClock`, `TOIMChannelSlot`, `TOIMColumnSlot`, `TOIMDefaultSlotStore`, `TOIMDisposer`, `TOIMEffect`, `TOIMEntitySlot`, `TOIMSingleSlotStore`, `TOIMSingleSlotStoreSlot`, `TOIMSlot`, `TOIMStoreKey`, `TOIMStoreSlot`, `oimHoldSlots`, `oimIsAnySlotChangedAfter`, `oimIsSlotReleased`, `oimSameValueZeroGuard`, `oimUnholdSlotsIfAlive` | no |
| `@oimdb/redux-adapter` | `IOIMChannelMap`, `IOIMContentChangeListener`, `OIMChannelService`, `OIMPushColumnSlotOwner`, `OIMContentChangeListenerService`, `OIMEffectService`, `OIMSlotCollectionService`, `OIMSlotContentBucketService`, `OIMSlotContentEntityService`, `TOIMBucketSlot`, `TOIMColumnSlot`, `TOIMDefaultSlotStore`, `TOIMDisposer`, `TOIMEffect`, `TOIMEntityColumnName`, `TOIMEntitySlot`, `TOIMStoreKey`, `TOIMStoreSlot` | no |
| `@oimdb/exodra` | `IOIMChannelMap`, `OIMChannelService`, `OIMEffectService`, `OIMSlotContentBucketService`, `OIM_FROZEN_EMPTY_SLOTS`, `TOIMBucketSlot`, `TOIMComputedSlot`, `TOIMDisposer`, `TOIMEffect`, `TOIMEntitySlot`, `TOIMOrderedListCommand`, `TOIMSlot`, `TOIMStoreKey`, `oimOrderedListCommandsOfTransition`, `oimRefreshSourceComputeds`, `oimSameKeySequence` | no |
| `@oimdb/react` | `IOIMChannelMap`, `OIMComputedService`, `OIMDB`, `OIMEffectService`, `OIMSingleSlotService`, `OIMSlotCollectionService`, `OIMSlotContentBucketService`, `OIM_FROZEN_EMPTY_SLOTS`, `TOIMBucketSlot`, `TOIMColumnSlot`, `TOIMComputedSlot`, `TOIMComputedSources`, `TOIMComputedStoreSlot`, `TOIMDisposer`, `TOIMEntityColumnName`, `TOIMEntityColumnValue`, `TOIMEntitySlot`, `TOIMIndexableSlot`, `TOIMKeyedSlot`, `TOIMSingleSlotStore`, `TOIMSlot`, `TOIMStoreKey`, `TOIMStoreSlot`, `oimHoldSlots`, `oimRefreshSourceComputeds`, `oimSameKeySequence`, `oimUnholdSlotsIfAlive` | no |
| `@oimdb/devtools` | `IOIMChannelMap`, `IOIMStoreSlotListener`, `OIMChannelService`, `OIMComputedService`, `OIMDefaults`, `OIMSlotCollectionService`, `TOIMBucketSlot`, `TOIMComputedStoreSlot`, `TOIMDefaultSlotStore`, `TOIMDisposer`, `TOIMEntitySlot`, `TOIMKeyedSlot`, `TOIMStoreKey`, `TOIMStoreSlot` | no |
| `@oimdb/async` | — | deprecated stub, `export {}` |
| `@oimdb/snapshot-manager` | — | empty stub |

Every package in the table has a `type-check` script (`tsc --noEmit`) that CI
runs on each commit, and `@oimdb/core`, `@oimdb/persist`, `@oimdb/react`,
`@oimdb/redux-adapter` and `@oimdb/exodra` pass it. Their documentation pages
name only shipped exports, but the source is still the final word on a signature.

## `@oimdb/persist`

The persistence engine for `@oimdb/core` and its five backend packages. The
engine names the parts and wires them; a backend package supplies the storage.
Every constructor in the family takes ONE options object.

| package | exports |
|---|---|
| `@oimdb/persist` | the engine, plus the key-value backend `OIMPersistKeyValueBackend` and its strategies; error types `TOIMPersistErrorHandler`, `TOIMPersistErrorContext`, `TOIMPersistOperation` and `TOIMPersistErrorReport` (`{ error, persistErrorContext }`, one failure as `onPersistError` receives it or as it lands in the `AggregateError`) |
| `@oimdb/persist-memory` | `OIMPersistMemoryBackend`, `OIMPersistMemoryWriteBatch`, `OIMPersistMemoryRecordsService`, `OIMPersistMemorySnapshotService`, `TOIMPersistMemoryServiceOptions` |
| `@oimdb/persist-json` | `OIMPersistJsonMemoryBackend`, `TOIMPersistJsonMemoryBackendOptions`, `TOIMPersistJsonDump`; depends on `@oimdb/persist-memory` |
| `@oimdb/persist-idb` | `OIMPersistIndexedDbBackend`, `OIMPersistIndexedDbWriteBatch`, `OIMPersistIndexedDbRecordsService`, `OIMPersistIndexedDbSnapshotService`, `TOIMPersistIndexedDbBackendOptions`, `TOIMPersistIndexedDbRecordsServiceOptions`, `TOIMPersistIndexedDbSnapshotServiceOptions`, `TOIMPersistIndexedDbPrimaryKey`, `TOIMPersistIndexedDbTableRecord` |
| `@oimdb/persist-localstorage` | `OIMPersistLocalStorageKeyValueBackend`, `TOIMPersistLocalStorageKeyValueBackendOptions` |
| `@oimdb/persist-async-kv` | `OIMPersistAsyncKVStorage`, `TOIMPersistAsyncKVStorageOptions`, `TOIMPersistAsyncKVMultiStorage` |

### The wiring

A persistor owns one backend, one scheduler and a list of resources. A resource is
one thing being persisted: a source (the in-memory side), a strategy (where it
lives in the backend) and what to do on hydrate.

```ts
import {
    OIMPersistEntityWriter, OIMPersistCollectionWriteRecordSource, OIMPersistRecordsResource,
    OIMPersistMicrotaskScheduler, OIMPersistor,
} from '@oimdb/persist';
import { OIMPersistMemoryBackend, OIMPersistMemoryRecordsService, OIMPersistMemoryWriteBatch } from '@oimdb/persist-memory';

const persistEntityWriter = new OIMPersistEntityWriter<Card, TOIMStoreKey>({
    entityWriter: createOIMEntityWriterInPlace(),
});
const persistedCardCollectionService = createOIMSlotCollectionService(db, { slotContentService: createOIMSlotContentEntityService<Card>(db, { entityWriter: persistEntityWriter }) });
const persistedCardEntityStoreSlot = persistedCardCollectionService.createStoreSlot(db);

const persistMemoryBackend = new OIMPersistMemoryBackend();
const persistor = new OIMPersistor<OIMPersistMemoryBackend, OIMPersistMemoryWriteBatch>({
    persistBackend: persistMemoryBackend,
    persistScheduler: new OIMPersistMicrotaskScheduler(),
    onPersistError: (error, persistErrorContext) => {
        console.error(persistErrorContext.persistOperation, error);
    },
});
const cardPersistResourceRecords = persistor.addPersistResource(new OIMPersistRecordsResource({
    persistRecordSource: new OIMPersistCollectionWriteRecordSource({
        entityCollectionService: persistedCardCollectionService,
        entityStoreSlot: persistedCardEntityStoreSlot,
        persistEntityWriter,
    }),
    persistRecordsService: new OIMPersistMemoryRecordsService<TOIMStoreKey, Card>({ storageKey: 'cards' }),
}));

await persistor.hydrate();
persistor.start();
persistedCardCollectionService.writeSlotContentByKey(persistedCardEntityStoreSlot, 'c1', { id: 'c1', title: 'Ace', rank: 1, deck: 'spades' });
await persistor.persist();
await persistor.unload(cardPersistResourceRecords, ['c1']);
await persistor.load(cardPersistResourceRecords, ['c1']);
```

Rules a generator must keep:

- Pass both generics of `OIMPersistor<TPersistBackend, TWriteBatch>`: the backend
  class and its write batch class (`OIMPersistMemoryWriteBatch`, `OIMPersistIndexedDbWriteBatch`,
  `OIMPersistKeyValueWriteBatch`; `OIMPersistJsonMemoryBackend` uses `OIMPersistMemoryWriteBatch`,
  `OIMPersistLocalStorageKeyValueBackend` uses `OIMPersistKeyValueWriteBatch`).
- Pass the generics of strategies, codecs and `OIMPersistEntityWriter<TEntity, TKey>`
  explicitly; their options carry no type to infer them from.
- An entity collection persisted through a collection source is built with the
  `OIMPersistEntityWriter` as its `entityWriter`, and the same writer goes into the
  source's `persistEntityWriter`. The source takes the collection service and ONE of its store slots
  (`entityCollectionService`, `entityStoreSlot`). The writer belongs to the content service, not to the store
  slot, and the source keeps only the writes whose `entitySlot.storeSlot` is its own store slot; a write to
  another store slot of the same collection type is ignored by it.
  `new OIMPersistEntityWriter({ entityWriter })` wraps the `IOIMEntityWriter` that
  really writes, and reports the entity slot of every fill, put, patch, column patch,
  column delete and clear that changed something (`subscribeEntitySlotWritten`).
- The entity collection service a source takes is any collection service with `getSlots`, `findSlotByKey`,
  `writeSlotContentByKey`, `writeInBatch` and a `slotContentService` with `clearSlotContent`
  (`TOIMPersistEntityCollectionService`): what `createOIMSlotCollectionService` over an entity content service builds.
- A source refuses, by name, a store slot on another channel slot than the one it was given (the bucket source
  checks both the entity and the bucket store slot).
- Order: `addPersistResource` every resource, `await persistor.hydrate()`, then
  `persistor.start()`.

### Constructors and option keys

| constructor | options |
|---|---|
| `OIMPersistor` | `{ persistBackend, persistScheduler, onPersistError? }` |
| `OIMPersistRecordsResource` | `{ persistRecordSource, persistRecordsService, persistHydrateReconcile? }` |
| `OIMPersistSnapshotResource` | `{ persistSnapshotSource, persistSnapshotService, persistCodec, persistHydrateReconcile? }` |
| `OIMPersistCollectionWriteRecordSource`, `OIMPersistCollectionChangeWriteRecordSource` | `{ entityCollectionService, entityStoreSlot, persistEntityWriter }` (`TOIMPersistRecordSourceCollectionOptions`) |
| `OIMPersistBucketRecordSource` | `{ channelMap, entityCollectionService, entityStoreSlot, slotContentBucketService, bucketSlot }` — `channelMap` is the db, `slotContentBucketService` the bucket collection's `slotContentService` |
| `OIMPersistSingleEntitySnapshotSource` | `{ channelMap, singleSlotService, entityStoreSlot }` — a single entity service (`createOIMSingleSlotService` over an entity content service) and one of its store slots (`TOIMSingleSlotStoreSlot`) |
| `OIMPersistEntityWriter` | `{ entityWriter }` |
| `OIMPersistMicrotaskScheduler` | none |
| `OIMPersistFrameScheduler` | `{ channelSlot }` — `db.defaultChannelSlot` |
| `OIMPersistIdentityCodec` | none |
| `OIMPersistVersionedCodec` | `{ version, migrations, persistCodec }` |
| `OIMPersistMemoryBackend` | none |
| `OIMPersistMemoryRecordsService`, `OIMPersistMemorySnapshotService` | `{ storageKey }` |
| `OIMPersistJsonMemoryBackend` | `{ initialPersistJsonDump? }`, the object itself optional |
| `OIMPersistIndexedDbBackend` | `{ databaseName, databaseVersion?, indexedDb? }` |
| `OIMPersistIndexedDbRecordsService` | `{ tableName }` |
| `OIMPersistIndexedDbSnapshotService` | `{ tableName, primaryKey }` |
| `OIMPersistKeyValueBackend` | `{ persistKeyValueStorage, persistKeyValueSerializer? }` |
| `OIMPersistItemKeyValueStorage` | `{ persistKeyValueItemStorage }` |
| `OIMPersistKeyValueEntrySnapshotService` | `{ storageKey }` |
| `OIMPersistKeyValuePathSnapshotService` | `{ storageKey, path }` |
| `OIMPersistLocalStorageKeyValueBackend` | `{ persistKeyValueItemStorage?, persistKeyValueSerializer? }`, the object itself optional |
| `OIMPersistSlotSourceChangeMark` | `{ channelClock, slots }` |
| `OIMPersistSubscriptionSourceChangeMark` | `{ subscribeSourceChanged }` |
| `OIMPersistAsyncKVStorage` | `{ persistAsyncKVMultiStorage }` |

`onPersistError(error, persistErrorContext)` receives a `TOIMPersistErrorContext`,
`{ persistResource, persistOperation }`. `TOIMPersistOperation` is
`'start' | 'persist' | 'hydrate' | 'clear' | 'quarantine'`. `TOIMPersistErrorReport`
is one failure, `{ error, persistErrorContext }`, as it is handed to `onPersistError`
or collected into the `AggregateError`.

### Two resource kinds, and when to pick each

| | `OIMPersistRecordsResource` | `OIMPersistSnapshotResource` |
|---|---|---|
| source | a record source: entity store slot or bucket | any snapshot source: entity store slot, bucket or single entity |
| strategy | `OIMPersistMemoryRecordsService`, `OIMPersistIndexedDbRecordsService` | `OIMPersistMemorySnapshotService`, `OIMPersistIndexedDbSnapshotService`, `OIMPersistKeyValueEntrySnapshotService`, `OIMPersistKeyValuePathSnapshotService` |
| autosave writes | the delta: one upsert or one deletion per entity slot written since the last drain | the whole snapshot, read from the source and encoded |
| `persist()` writes | every record, replacing what is stored; while any key is unloaded, every in-memory record as an upsert over what is stored, plus the deletions the resource already heard | the whole snapshot |
| codec | none | `persistCodec`, required |
| `unload` | yes | no |
| `load` | yes | no |

Pick records whenever the backend has a records strategy (memory, JSON,
IndexedDB): autosave then costs one entry per written entity slot, independent of
the store slot's size. Pick snapshot for a single entity, for the key-value
backends (localStorage, async KV), which have no records strategy, or when a
versioned codec must migrate what is stored. A record source is also a snapshot
source whose snapshot is `TOIMPersistRecords` (`{ records: { key, entity }[] }`),
so an entity store slot or a bucket goes into either kind.

A records resource keeps its dirty state as a set of entity slots, read through the
slot with no key lookup; a slot written several times between drains is one entry.
At the drain each slot becomes an upsert of `{ key, entity }` when it holds an entity
and is not released, and a deletion of its key otherwise. When a key has both, a
released slot and a live slot minted again for that key inside one batch, the live
slot wins: an upsert, not a deletion.

### The sources, and the scheduler each pairs with

| source | reports | scheduler |
|---|---|---|
| `OIMPersistCollectionWriteRecordSource` | synchronously, at the write, from `OIMPersistEntityWriter` only | `OIMPersistMicrotaskScheduler` |
| `OIMPersistCollectionChangeWriteRecordSource` | synchronously, at the write, from `OIMPersistEntityWriter` and from a content-change listener on the entity store slot | `OIMPersistMicrotaskScheduler` |
| `OIMPersistBucketRecordSource` | from effects (`OIMEffectService`), when the channel runs its frame | `OIMPersistFrameScheduler({ channelSlot })` |
| `OIMPersistSingleEntitySnapshotSource` | from an effect, when the channel runs its frame | `OIMPersistFrameScheduler({ channelSlot })` |

- **Collection** (an entity collection service and one of its store slots): every entity slot of that store slot that holds an entity. Starting
  reports nothing; content present before `start()` is written by `persist()` or by
  its next write. An entity removed for any reason, a slot release policy included,
  goes through the writer's `clearEntity` and reaches the backend as a deletion;
  `unload` is the call that removes from memory and keeps the stored value. The two
  collection sources are one fork, chosen at construction, with the same options:

  | collection source | in-place edit announced with `slotContentService.markEntityChanged(entitySlot, changedColumns?)` | cost while a resource listens | pick it when |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `OIMPersistCollectionWriteRecordSource` | NOT persisted: it hears only the writer | none: every write stays on the core fast path | every change goes through `writeSlotContentByKey`, `writeSlotContent`, `updateEntity` and `clearSlotContent` |
  | `OIMPersistCollectionChangeWriteRecordSource` | persisted: while subscribed it adds a content-change listener of every column to the store slot | EVERY write to that store slot leaves the core fast path, not only `markEntityChanged`: changed-column bookkeeping and the listener loop per write | the app edits entities in place |
- **Bucket**: the entities one bucket slot holds. Get the slot with
  `bucketCollectionService.holdSlotByKey(bucketStoreSlot, key)`. The source watches the
  bucket slot with one effect and each member entity slot with one effect. An entity
  that leaves the bucket is deleted from the backend and stays in the entity
  store slot. The first subscription reports every member, so `start()` writes the
  current members on the first drain, except members still holding the value a
  hydrate restored.
- **Single entity**: the snapshot is the entity itself (a store slot of a single entity service, read through
  `findSingleSlot(entityStoreSlot)`), so it
  goes only into `OIMPersistSnapshotResource`. Its first subscription reports the
  current value unless it is the value a hydrate restored. `readSnapshot` throws when
  the entity slot holds no value.

The bucket and single-entity sources tell their own restored writes apart from user
writes by comparing the entity, column by column with SameValueZero (NaN equals NaN, as core's write guard does), against a copy taken when
it was restored (`OIMPersistRestoredEntities`). A wake is not written while the source
still holds the restored value. The first time a different value is seen, the memo for
that key is gone, so an edit and a later revert to the restored value, in another
frame, are both written.

```ts
import {
    OIMPersistBucketRecordSource, OIMPersistRecordsResource, OIMPersistFrameScheduler, OIMPersistor,
} from '@oimdb/persist';
import { OIMPersistMemoryBackend, OIMPersistMemoryRecordsService, OIMPersistMemoryWriteBatch } from '@oimdb/persist-memory';

type TDeckCardSlot = TOIMEntitySlot<Card, TOIMStoreKey>;
const deckCardCollectionService = createOIMSlotCollectionService(db, { slotContentService: createOIMSlotContentEntityService<Card>(db) });
const deckCardEntityStoreSlot = deckCardCollectionService.createStoreSlot(db);
const deckBucketService = createOIMSlotCollectionService(db, { slotContentService: new OIMSlotContentPositionalArrayBucketService<TDeckCardSlot>({ bucketCommands: new OIMBucketCommands({ maxCommandsPerSlot: undefined }) }) });
const deckBucketStoreSlot = deckBucketService.createStoreSlot(db);
const spadesBucketSlot = deckBucketService.holdSlotByKey(deckBucketStoreSlot, 'spades');

const deckPersistor = new OIMPersistor<OIMPersistMemoryBackend, OIMPersistMemoryWriteBatch>({
    persistBackend: new OIMPersistMemoryBackend(),
    persistScheduler: new OIMPersistFrameScheduler({ channelSlot: db.defaultChannelSlot }),
});
deckPersistor.addPersistResource(new OIMPersistRecordsResource({
    persistRecordSource: new OIMPersistBucketRecordSource({
        channelMap: db,
        entityCollectionService: deckCardCollectionService,
        entityStoreSlot: deckCardEntityStoreSlot,
        slotContentBucketService: deckBucketService.slotContentService,
        bucketSlot: spadesBucketSlot,
    }),
    persistRecordsService: new OIMPersistMemoryRecordsService<TOIMStoreKey, Card>({ storageKey: 'spades' }),
}));
await deckPersistor.hydrate();
deckPersistor.start();

const aceSlot = deckCardCollectionService.writeSlotContentByKey(deckCardEntityStoreSlot, 'c1', { id: 'c1', title: 'Ace', rank: 1, deck: 'spades' });
deckBucketService.slotContentService.writeSlotContent(spadesBucketSlot, [aceSlot]);
db.flush();
await deckPersistor.whenIdle();
```

### Schedulers

`IOIMPersistScheduler` is `attachDrain(drain)`, `start()`, `stop()`, `requestDrain()`.
The persistor calls `attachDrain` from its constructor; both shipped schedulers throw
when a second persistor attaches, so construct one scheduler per persistor.

- `OIMPersistMicrotaskScheduler`: `requestDrain()` queues one microtask; the
  requests that follow before it runs are absorbed by it. `stop()` makes a queued
  microtask do nothing.
- `OIMPersistFrameScheduler({ channelSlot })`: while started it subscribes with
  `OIMChannelService.INSTANCE.subscribeAfterEachFrame(channelSlot, …)` and drains after a frame only when a drain was
  requested since the last one; `stop()` unsubscribes and forgets the request. It
  holds no slot and never asks the channel for a frame: it drains only after a frame
  the channel runs anyway.

**The pairing is a rule.** A write to an entity slot that nobody holds causes no frame
(`OIMChannelService.INSTANCE.writeWithoutFlushCheck` returns at once when `holdCount` is `0`), so a
collection source on the frame scheduler can report changes that no frame ever
drains. Pair `OIMPersistCollectionWriteRecordSource` and
`OIMPersistCollectionChangeWriteRecordSource` with
`OIMPersistMicrotaskScheduler`. The bucket and single-entity sources report from
effects, which cause the frames they run in, so pair them with
`OIMPersistFrameScheduler`. Resources of both groups in one persistor share its
one scheduler; give them two persistors when they need different schedulers.

`whenIdle()` resolves when the work queued at the moment of the call has settled. On
the frame scheduler the drain runs inside `db.flush()`, so `db.flush(); await
persistor.whenIdle()` covers the autosave. On the microtask scheduler the autosave
is queued on the microtask after the write: let one microtask pass before calling
`whenIdle()`, or call `persist()`.

### Persistor methods

| method | what it does |
|---|---|
| `addPersistResource(persistResource)` | registers and returns it; on a started persistor it starts the resource first and registers it only if that start succeeded (a failed start is thrown from `addPersistResource`) |
| `removePersistResource(persistResource)` | stops it and drops its pending write |
| `start()` / `stop()` | subscribe / unsubscribe every resource and the scheduler; `start()` skips quarantined resources; pending writes survive `stop()`. A resource whose subscribe throws does not stop the others: each failure goes to `onPersistError` with `persistOperation: 'start'`, or, without a handler, all are thrown as one `AggregateError`. A resource whose start failed stays registered and unsubscribed, with no autosave, until `stop()` and `start()` again; `addPersistResource` on a started persistor does not register a resource whose start throws. A bucket or single-entity source reports its current value at subscribe time (except a hydrate-restored value), so the first drain after `start()` writes it; a collection source reports nothing then |
| `destroy()` | `stop()`, then forgets every resource |
| `hydrate()` | reads every resource and writes it into its source; ends the upsert-only mode of an unloaded resource |
| `persist()` | writes every resource in full, started or not, in one write batch; a records resource with unloaded keys writes its in-memory records as upserts over the stored table instead of replacing it, plus the deletions it already heard |
| `clearPersisted()` | deletes every resource's stored data in one write batch; memory is untouched; ends the upsert-only mode of an unloaded resource |
| `unload(persistRecordsResource, keys)` | writes the keys' current values plus the resource's pending change in one write batch, repeated until the keys have no unwritten change (unload holds the keys' entity slots while it writes and compares their revision stamps, a slot's stamp moving only on a real write; it also checks the resource's pending set and whether a key's slot was replaced), then removes the keys from memory only |
| `load(persistRecordsResource, keys)` | the pair of `unload`: queued after the pending writes, reads only those keys from the backend (`readRecordsOfKeys`) and puts the stored entities back without writing them back; skips a key that holds a value in memory or has a change the resource has not written yet; the keys stop counting as unloaded |
| `whenIdle()` | resolves when the queued work settles; never rejects |

Every promise-returning call and every autosave runs on one ordered chain, one at a
time, in request order. A snapshot is read when its work runs, not when it was queued.

### The write batch, retry and quarantine

- **One batch per drain.** A drain takes every dirty resource with a pending write,
  calls `persistBackend.createWriteBatch()` once, lets each resource write into it,
  and calls `commit()` once. `persist()` and `clearPersisted()` do the same for every
  registered resource.
- **Whole-batch failure.** Every resource in the batch puts its in-flight change back
  (a records resource returns the failed entity slots to its dirty set; a snapshot
  resource marks itself pending), then the persistor writes each resource again in a
  batch of its own, so the healthy ones commit and the failure is attributed to the
  resource that caused it. A failed batch of N resources costs 1 + N commits.
- **Retry.** A failed autosave leaves the resource dirty; the next drain writes it.
  The next drain comes from the next drain request (a change in any resource), a
  `persist()` or an `unload`. There is no retry timer.
- **Quarantine.** Three consecutive autosave failures of one resource stop it
  listening to its source and drop its pending write; it is reported once with
  `persistOperation: 'quarantine'`, or on `console.error` without `onPersistError`.
  A successful `persist()` of it lifts the quarantine and, on a started persistor,
  starts it again; `start()` skips a quarantined resource. Any successful write
  resets the count, whichever operation committed it (autosave, `persist()`,
  `clearPersisted()`, `unload`); `persist()` failures do not add to it.
- **Errors.** With `onPersistError`, each failure is handed over and the promise
  resolves; a failed autosave below quarantine is reported with `'persist'`, a failed
  resource subscribe in `start()` with `'start'`. Without it, `start()` (throws),
  `hydrate()`, `persist()` and `clearPersisted()` attempt every resource, then
  reject with one `AggregateError` whose `errors` holds every failure; a failed
  autosave below quarantine is silently retained, and the quarantine logs to the
  console. `unload` rejects its own promise when its write fails, and then leaves
  the keys in memory.

### Hydrate: reconcile and refusal

`hydrate()` reads each resource through its strategy. A read that resolves
`undefined` means nothing is stored, and nothing is applied. Anything else, an empty
`{ records: [] }` included, is applied: decoded through `persistCodec` on a snapshot
resource, passed through `persistHydrateReconcile(currentSnapshot, incomingSnapshot)`
when set, then written into the source. Hydrate's own writes are not reported as
changes, so `start()` after `hydrate()` writes nothing back.

What the source does with it:

- collection: upserts every record into the entity store slot, then deletes every entity the records do not
  name; the store slot becomes exactly the stored content;
- bucket: upserts every record into the entity store slot and sets the bucket's
  members to exactly the restored entities;
- single entity: `singleSlotService.writeSingleSlotContent(entityStoreSlot, entity)`.

**Refusal.** If the source changes while the backend read is in flight and the
resource has no `persistHydrateReconcile`, hydrate throws instead of applying, because
applying would revert that change. The source keeps its newer state; the error goes
to `onPersistError` with `'hydrate'`, or into the `AggregateError`. Before the read
the resource calls `persistSnapshotSource.markSourceChanges()`, which returns an
`IOIMPersistSourceChangeMark` (`isSourceChangedSinceMark()`, `dispose()`): the
single-entity and bucket sources return an `OIMPersistSlotSourceChangeMark`
that holds the slots and compares their revision stamps (`changedAtRevision`, `changedAtEpoch`) with the
channel clock reading taken at the mark (`oimIsAnySlotChangedAfter`), the
collection sources an `OIMPersistSubscriptionSourceChangeMark` whose flag their
own report sets. A change made during the read is seen even when no frame runs, and
the guard runs whether or not the persistor is started.

**Reconcile.** `oimReconcileByKey<TKey, TEntity>(resolveEntity)` builds a
`TOIMPersistHydrateReconcile<TOIMPersistRecords<TKey, TEntity>>`.
`resolveEntity(currentEntity, incomingEntity, key)` runs for every stored key, with
`currentEntity` `undefined` when memory lacks the key, and returns the entity to keep
or `undefined` to drop it. Keys only in memory are kept. Order: memory's keys first,
then the stored keys memory lacked. A snapshot resource over a single entity takes any
`(currentSnapshot, incomingSnapshot) => snapshot` function.

```ts
import { oimReconcileByKey } from '@oimdb/persist';

const answerReconcile = oimReconcileByKey<TOIMStoreKey, Card>(
    (currentEntity, incomingEntity) => currentEntity === undefined
        ? incomingEntity
        : { ...currentEntity, rank: incomingEntity.rank },
);
```

### unload, load and clearPersisted

`persistor.unload(persistRecordsResource, keys)` takes an `OIMPersistRecordsResource`
only. It first drains the persistor's dirty resources onto the chain, then, in its
own turn, writes in one write batch that resource's pending change and the current
value of every unloaded key (`persistRecordSource.readRecordsDelta(persistRecordSource.findEntitySlotsByKeys(keys))`), so
an edit no drain had reached, or one made while the persistor was stopped or the
resource quarantined, is saved. unload holds the keys' entity slots while it writes, and after each commit it
compares their revision stamps (a slot's stamp moves only on a real write), checks the
resource's pending set and whether a key's slot was replaced; while any of those moved it
writes another batch of the same shape, so an edit made during any commit
(and, on the bucket source, an edit the channel has not flushed yet) reaches the
backend. Only then does it remove
the keys from the source with this resource's reporting suppressed, so the removal is
not written by it. The backend keeps the keys; `load` brings those keys back and the
next `hydrate()` brings back everything, and a restored entity persists its next edit like any other. A failed write rejects
the unload and leaves the keys in memory. On a collection source and on the bucket source
the keys are deleted from the entity store slot.
Deleting an entity does not take it out of a bucket: the bucket keeps the slot as a
member until it is refiled. The bucket source remembers the deletion as restored for
every key that is a member of the bucket at unload time, whether or not the persistor
is listening.

While any key of a records resource is unloaded, `persist()` writes that resource's
in-memory records as upserts over the stored table instead of replacing it, plus the
deletions the resource already heard (its pending deletions), so the unloaded records
stay on the backend. A deletion it never heard is not written in that mode.
`hydrate()` and `clearPersisted()` end that mode, and so does a `load` of every
unloaded key.

`persistor.load(persistRecordsResource, keys)` is the pair of `unload` and takes an
`OIMPersistRecordsResource` only (a key-value backend has no records strategy, so a
snapshot resource has no `load`). It drains the dirty resources onto the chain and
runs after those writes. In its turn it reads only those keys through
`persistRecordsService.readRecordsOfKeys(persistBackend, keys)`: on IndexedDB one
`readonly` transaction with one `get` per key, on memory a lookup of each key in the
stored map; a key the backend does not hold is left out. It skips every key that holds
a value in memory or has a change the resource has not written yet (pending or in a
commit), so neither a write nor a heard deletion made during the read is overwritten.
The rest goes to `persistRecordSource.loadRecords(persistRecords)` with this
resource's reporting suppressed, so the loaded entities are not written back. A
collection source upserts them into the entity store slot; the bucket source upserts them
into the entity store slot, adds the slots back to the bucket
(`slotContentBucketService.addBucketMemberSlots`) and remembers them as restored. The keys
stop counting as unloaded, so once none is, `persist()` replaces the stored table
again. Another resource over the same entity store slot is not suppressed and hears
the upserts as writes. A failed read rejects the promise `load` returned.

When to unload and when to load (on a screen change, on idle, on a read miss) is the
application's decision, or an orchestrator's; persist offers the two doors and decides
neither.

**Limit:** another resource over the same entity store slot is not suppressed. It
reports the unloaded keys as deletions, and its next autosave deletes them from ITS
storage. Unload only keys no other resource persists.

**Limit:** a deletion made while the persistor is stopped, or the resource is
quarantined, is not heard. While any key of the resource is unloaded, `persist()`
writes no deletion it did not hear, and `unload` writes it only while the entity's slot
still exists (once the slot was released no slot is found for the key); otherwise the
record comes back on the next `hydrate()`. Call `persist()` while started, and with no
key unloaded, to make a deletion the resource never heard durable.

`persistor.clearPersisted()` calls every resource's strategy delete
(`deleteRecords` / `deleteSnapshot`) inside one write batch with one commit, under the
same whole-batch split and error rules as `persist()`. Memory is untouched.

### Codecs

A snapshot resource encodes on every write and decodes on hydrate through its
required `persistCodec`, an `IOIMPersistCodec<TSourceSnapshot, TPersistedSnapshot>`
(`encode`, `decode`). A records resource has no codec: it stores entities as the
source holds them.

- `new OIMPersistIdentityCodec<TSnapshot>()`: passes the snapshot through.
- `new OIMPersistVersionedCodec<TSourceSnapshot, TPersistedSnapshot>({ version, migrations, persistCodec })`:
  stores a `TOIMPersistVersionedShape`, `{ version, data }`, where `data` is the
  inner `persistCodec`'s encoding (required; use `OIMPersistIdentityCodec` when
  nothing transforms). `migrations` is a `Record<number, (data: unknown) => unknown>`
  keyed by the version each migration produces. On decode it runs, ascending, every
  migration whose key is above the stored `version` and at most the current one,
  then decodes with the inner codec. A stored `version` above the codec's own is
  refused: `decode` throws and the hydrate reports it with `'hydrate'`. The strategy
  is typed with `TOIMPersistVersionedShape`.

```ts
import {
    OIMPersistIdentityCodec, OIMPersistVersionedCodec, OIMPersistKeyValueBackend, OIMPersistKeyValueEntrySnapshotService,
    OIMPersistItemKeyValueStorage, OIMPersistKeyValueWriteBatch, OIMPersistSnapshotResource,
    OIMPersistFrameScheduler, OIMPersistSingleEntitySnapshotSource, OIMPersistor,
} from '@oimdb/persist';
import type { TOIMPersistVersionedShape } from '@oimdb/persist';

type TSettings = { theme: 'light' | 'dark'; density: 'compact' | 'comfortable' };

const settingsSingleEntityService = createOIMSingleSlotService(db, { slotContentService: createOIMSlotContentEntityService<TSettings>(db) });
const settingsEntityStoreSlot = settingsSingleEntityService.createStoreSlot(db);
settingsSingleEntityService.writeSingleSlotContent(settingsEntityStoreSlot, { theme: 'light', density: 'compact' });
const itemByStorageKey = new Map<string, string>();
const settingsPersistor = new OIMPersistor<OIMPersistKeyValueBackend, OIMPersistKeyValueWriteBatch>({
    persistBackend: new OIMPersistKeyValueBackend({
        persistKeyValueStorage: new OIMPersistItemKeyValueStorage({
            persistKeyValueItemStorage: {
                getItem: storageKey => itemByStorageKey.get(storageKey) ?? null,
                setItem: (storageKey, item) => { itemByStorageKey.set(storageKey, item); },
                removeItem: storageKey => { itemByStorageKey.delete(storageKey); },
            },
        }),
    }),
    persistScheduler: new OIMPersistFrameScheduler({ channelSlot: db.defaultChannelSlot }),
});
settingsPersistor.addPersistResource(new OIMPersistSnapshotResource({
    persistSnapshotSource: new OIMPersistSingleEntitySnapshotSource({
        channelMap: db, singleSlotService: settingsSingleEntityService, entityStoreSlot: settingsEntityStoreSlot,
    }),
    persistSnapshotService: new OIMPersistKeyValueEntrySnapshotService<TOIMPersistVersionedShape>({ storageKey: 'settings' }),
    persistCodec: new OIMPersistVersionedCodec<TSettings, TSettings>({
        version: 2,
        migrations: { 2: data => ({ density: 'comfortable', ...(data as object) }) },
        persistCodec: new OIMPersistIdentityCodec<TSettings>(),
    }),
}));
await settingsPersistor.hydrate();
settingsPersistor.start();

settingsSingleEntityService.slotContentService.updateEntity(
    settingsSingleEntityService.getSingleSlot(settingsEntityStoreSlot), { theme: 'dark' },
);
db.flush();
await settingsPersistor.whenIdle();
```

### Backends and their strategies

**Memory** (`@oimdb/persist-memory`). `new OIMPersistMemoryBackend()`. Snapshot values
and records live in two separate maps, so a snapshot and a records resource may share
a `storageKey`. `OIMPersistMemoryRecordsService<TKey, TEntity>({ storageKey })` keeps one
`Map` of key to entity per `storageKey`: autosave sets and deletes keys, `persist()`
replaces the map (while the resource has unloaded keys, sets keys and deletes only the deletions the resource already heard), `clearPersisted()` deletes it, and a `load` looks each of its keys up in the map through `readRecordsOfKeys`. `OIMPersistMemorySnapshotService<TSnapshot>({ storageKey })`
keeps one value. `readRecords(storageKey)` and `readSnapshotValue(storageKey)` read
what was committed. `OIMPersistMemoryWriteBatch` queues every change and applies them in
order on `commit()`.

**JSON** (`@oimdb/persist-json`, depends on `@oimdb/persist-memory`).
`OIMPersistJsonMemoryBackend` extends `OIMPersistMemoryBackend` and takes the memory
strategies. `dehydrate()` returns a `TOIMPersistJsonDump`,
`{ snapshotValues: Record<storageKey, value>, recordsByStorageKey: Record<storageKey, { key, entity }[]> }`;
`new OIMPersistJsonMemoryBackend({ initialPersistJsonDump })` writes such a dump straight into
its maps. The SSR flow: on the server, `await persistor.persist()` and then
`JSON.stringify(persistJsonMemoryBackend.dehydrate())`; on the client,
`new OIMPersistJsonMemoryBackend({ initialPersistJsonDump: JSON.parse(jsonText) })`, register
the same resources under the same `storageKey`s, `await persistor.hydrate()`. To merge
a durable cache over the server's content, hydrate the JSON persistor first, then the
durable persistor with `persistHydrateReconcile`, then `start()` the durable one.

**IndexedDB** (`@oimdb/persist-idb`). `new OIMPersistIndexedDbBackend({ databaseName, databaseVersion?, indexedDb? })`;
`indexedDb` defaults to `globalThis.indexedDB` and the constructor throws without
either. `OIMPersistIndexedDbRecordsService<TKey, TEntity>({ tableName })` stores one value
per entity key in an object store: autosave puts and deletes per key, `persist()`
clears the table and puts every entity (while the resource has unloaded keys, only
puts plus a delete per deletion the resource already heard), `clearPersisted()` clears it,
and a `load` reads its keys through `readRecordsOfKeys` in one `readonly` transaction,
one `get` per key.
`OIMPersistIndexedDbSnapshotService<TSnapshot>({ tableName, primaryKey })` stores one value
at `primaryKey`. One commit is one `readwrite` transaction over every table the batch
touches. A commit opens the database and creates missing tables by a version upgrade
(retried when another connection upgrades first, up to five attempts; an upgrade
blocked for five seconds rejects); a read never creates a table, and a missing table
reads as `undefined`. A `TOIMPersistIndexedDbPrimaryKey` is an `IDBValidKey` or a plain
object; a plain object is encoded as the string `oimdb:object:` plus its JSON with
sorted property names, and is read back as that string.

**Key-value** (`@oimdb/persist`). `new OIMPersistKeyValueBackend({ persistKeyValueStorage, persistKeyValueSerializer? })`
stores serialized strings under string keys. `persistKeyValueStorage` is an
`IOIMPersistKeyValueStorage` (`readItems(storageKeys)`, `writeItems(itemByStorageKey)`,
`removeItems(storageKeys)`); `OIMPersistItemKeyValueStorage({ persistKeyValueItemStorage })`
adapts any `TOIMPersistKeyValueItemStorage` (`getItem`, `setItem`, `removeItem`,
synchronous or returning promises) with one call per key. The serializer is a
`TOIMPersistKeyValueSerializer` (`serialize`, `deserialize`) and defaults to
`OIM_PERSIST_KEY_VALUE_JSON_SERIALIZER`. Strategies, both snapshot strategies:

| strategy | stored as |
|---|---|
| `OIMPersistKeyValueEntrySnapshotService<TSnapshot>({ storageKey })` | the whole snapshot under `storageKey` |
| `OIMPersistKeyValuePathSnapshotService<TSnapshot>({ storageKey, path })` | the snapshot at `path` (a `string[]`) inside an object under `storageKey`; several resources may share the key; the constructor throws on an empty `path` |

`OIMPersistKeyValueWriteBatch` commits with at most one `readItems` (keys with path
writes or path deletions and no whole-value write in the batch), one `writeItems` and
one `removeItems`; it serializes every value before writing any. Path segments are
own properties, so a stored `__proto__` is data.

- **localStorage** (`@oimdb/persist-localstorage`): `OIMPersistLocalStorageKeyValueBackend`
  extends `OIMPersistKeyValueBackend` over a `TOIMPersistKeyValueItemStorage`
  (`getItem`, `setItem`, `removeItem`) given as `persistKeyValueItemStorage`, which
  defaults to `globalThis.localStorage`; the constructor throws without either. One `setItem` per written key.
- **async KV** (`@oimdb/persist-async-kv`): no backend class. Use
  `new OIMPersistKeyValueBackend({ persistKeyValueStorage: new OIMPersistAsyncKVStorage({ persistAsyncKVMultiStorage }) })`,
  where `persistAsyncKVMultiStorage` is a `TOIMPersistAsyncKVMultiStorage` (`multiGet`, `multiSet`,
  `multiRemove`, each returning a promise), the shape of React Native's
  `AsyncStorage`. One `multiGet`, one `multiSet` and one `multiRemove` per commit at
  most.

### Writing a backend, a strategy, a source

- Backend: `IOIMPersistBackend<TWriteBatch>` with `createWriteBatch()`; its batch is an
  `IOIMPersistWriteBatch` with `commit(): Promise<void>`, collecting changes and
  applying them in `commit`. `OIMPersistWriteBatchChanges<TWriteBatchTarget>` is the list a
  batch keeps them in: `addWriteBatchChange(change)`, `hasWriteBatchChanges`,
  `applyWriteBatchChanges(target)`. `oimWritePersistRecordsDelta(delta, putRecord, deleteRecord)`
  walks a `TOIMPersistRecordsDelta` in the one order every backend uses: upserts, then deletions.
- Snapshot strategy: `IOIMPersistSnapshotService<TPersistBackend, TWriteBatch, TSnapshot>`
  with `readSnapshot(persistBackend)`, `writeSnapshot(writeBatch, snapshot)`,
  `deleteSnapshot(writeBatch)`. Records strategy:
  `IOIMPersistRecordsService<TPersistBackend, TWriteBatch, TKey, TEntity>` with
  `readRecords(persistBackend)`, `readRecordsOfKeys(persistBackend, keys)`,
  `writeRecords(writeBatch, persistRecords)`,
  `writeRecordsDelta(writeBatch, persistRecordsDelta)` (a `TOIMPersistRecordsDelta`,
  `{ upserts, deletedKeys }`), `deleteRecords(writeBatch)`. A read resolves
  `undefined` only when nothing is stored; `readRecordsOfKeys` resolves the records of
  the keys the backend holds and leaves out the rest.
- Source: `IOIMPersistSnapshotSource<TSnapshot>` (`readSnapshot`, `writeSnapshot`,
  `subscribeSnapshotChanged`, `markSourceChanges`) or
  `IOIMPersistRecordSource<TKey, TEntity>`, which adds `subscribeEntitySlotChanged`,
  `readRecordsDelta(entitySlots)`, `findEntitySlotsByKeys(keys)`, `markEntitySlotChanges(entitySlots)`,
  `loadRecords(persistRecords)`, `unloadKeys(keys)`.
  `markSourceChanges()` is required and returns an `IOIMPersistSourceChangeMark`
  (`isSourceChangedSinceMark()`, `dispose()`); build it with
  `new OIMPersistSlotSourceChangeMark({ channelClock, slots })` or
  `new OIMPersistSubscriptionSourceChangeMark({ subscribeSourceChanged })`.
  It must accept more than one subscription, each with its own `TOIMDisposer`.
- Scheduler: `IOIMPersistScheduler`, above.

### Limits

- **No key-value records strategy.** Over `OIMPersistKeyValueBackend` (localStorage,
  async KV) an entity store slot or a bucket goes through `OIMPersistSnapshotResource`: every
  autosave walks every entity slot of the source and serializes the whole snapshot
  under one key.
- **A bucket membership change walks the bucket.** Each change of the bucket slot
  re-reads every member and every watched slot, and the source keeps one effect per
  member entity slot.
- **The memory and JSON backends keep values by reference.** With
  `createOIMEntityWriterInPlace()` the stored entity is the live entity object, so an
  in-place write moves the stored value before any commit, and `dehydrate()` returns
  the live objects. Use `createOIMEntityWriterReplacing()` with
  `entityInserter: oimInsertEntityWithCopy` where the stored value must stay
  what was committed, and serialize a dump at once.
- **Hydrate without a reconcile replaces.** The collection source deletes every
  entity the stored records do not name, and an existing but empty records table
  (IndexedDB after `clearPersisted()`) reads as an empty list and empties the
  entity store slot.
- **A key-value commit is not atomic across keys**: `writeItems` and `removeItems` are
  separate calls, and the item-driven storage calls `setItem` once per key.
- **One backend and one scheduler per persistor.** Sources needing different
  schedulers, or two backends, take two persistors.

---

## `@oimdb/exodra`

Turns a core read into an Exodra `TExoBindable` or `TExoBindableList`. It depends
only on the type-only `@exodra/reactivity-types`.

### One door: `exoBinding(channelMap, binding)`

A subscription here is one call — `OIMEffectService.INSTANCE.subscribeEffect(channelMap, sourceSlots, sourceComputeds, onChange)` —
and the value is read off the slots afterwards. So one adapter covers an entity, a
column, a bucket's slots and a derivation:

```ts
import { exoBinding } from '@oimdb/exodra';

const rank = rankService.computedCollectionService.holdSlotByKey(ranks, 'c1');

exoBinding(db, { sourceSlots: [slot], derive: () => slot.entity });
exoBinding(db, { sourceSlots: [todo], derive: () => Array.from(pageService.slotContentService.getBucketMemberSlots(todo)) });
exoBinding(db, { sourceComputeds: [rank], derive: () => rank.computedValueService.getValueForSlot(rank) });
```

`TOIMExoBinding<TValue>` is `{ sourceSlots?, sourceComputeds?, derive }`; both source keys are optional and default to none. `sourceSlots` is typed
`readonly TOIMSlot[]` and `sourceComputeds` `readonly TOIMComputedSlot[]`.

What `exoBinding` owns, each failing silently if a caller writes the pair by hand:
it **settles every derivation before the read** (a derivation is asked and never
woken); and it
arms **one effect** however many downstream subscribers there are, and none while
nobody listens.

**There is no observable wrapper on either side of this bridge**, and there must
not be one: the core hands over no object carrying a value and a subscribe, so an
intermediate type would have one producer and one consumer, both inside this
package. Build the binding directly.

### Lifetime is the caller's

`exoBinding` **holds nothing**, and that is deliberate: a bindable is lazy, so it
outlives its own subscriptions, and a hold scoped to one of them buys nothing —
a hold's give-back ends in the owner's release guard, so returning it at teardown
leaves exactly the state the teardown would have left. Whoever resolved the
identity holds it, and says so with `TOIMExoDisposable<TValue>` =
`TExoBindable<TValue> & { readonly dispose: TOIMDisposer }`:

```ts
import { exoBinding } from '@oimdb/exodra';

const rankFor = (id: TOIMStoreKey) => {
    const held = rankService.computedCollectionService.holdSlotByKey(ranks, id);
    return Object.assign(
        exoBinding(db, { sourceComputeds: [held], derive: () => held.computedValueService.getValueForSlot(held) }),
        { dispose: () => { held.owner.unholdSlot(held); } },
    );
};
```

Only a valueless identity is exposed by getting this wrong: an empty bucket, a key
resolved before its entity arrived, an entity since removed.

### The views

- `exoSource(read, subscribe)` — the lazy, ref-counted base. For sources that are
  **not** this engine's.
- `exoCombine(sources, fn)` — fan-in across any `TOIMExoReadable`. Not glitch-free;
  keep heavy fan-in inside one computed.
- `exoFollowKey(key, makeBindable)` — repoints as a selection moves. The factory
  must return a `TOIMExoDisposable`.
- `exoRows(keys, render)` — identity-stable children keyed by primary key. `render`
  returns `TOIMExoRenderedRow<TSchema>` = `{ schema, dispose }`.

### Lists are a fork, and both arms ship

Who decided the order is the difference, and the core already forks on it.

| | `exoDerivedList(channelMap, computedSlot, render, maxCommandsPerSlot?)` | `exoPositionalList(channelMap, slotContentBucketService, bucketSlot, render)` |
|---|---|---|
| takes | a `TOIMComputedSlot<readonly TOIMEntitySlot[]>` | a bucket content service built with an `OIMBucketCommands` and one of its bucket slots, from any of its store slots |
| the script | **derived**, by `oimOrderedListCommandsOfTransition` | **recorded**, by `OIMBucketCommands`, read inside the frame |
| per changed frame | one diff: two passes plus an LIS pass, `common − LIS` moves | one pass over the frame's own script |

Both hand back `TOIMExoList<TSchema>` = `TExoBindableList<TSchema> & { dispose }`,
and both are **attached from construction**, not from their first subscriber —
that is what lets `snapshot()` promise the list every later op is measured
against. Each item's schema is memoised in a `WeakMap` inside the bridge, so a
`reset` hands back the objects the previous snapshot did.

The derived script comes from `oimOrderedListCommandsOfTransition`. Items are
memoised per list, so two lists showing one entity slot render it twice.

### Full export list

`exoBinding`, `exoSource`, `exoCombine`, `exoFollowKey`, `exoRows`,
`exoDerivedList`, `exoPositionalList`; `TOIMExoBinding`, `TOIMExoReadable`,
`TOIMExoDisposable`, `TOIMExoRenderedRow`, `TOIMExoList`.

---

## Performance

**No figure may be quoted for this engine, and none is quoted anywhere in this
file.**

Every artifact under `packages/bench/measurements/` predates the surface
documented in this file, so none of its
figures prices what is described here. Such figures are **struck, not updated** — a
stale number with a real-looking artifact path attached is worse than none.

`packages/bench/results/` holds a timing series
that is still in flight: fifty-five timing artifacts beside one memory artifact,
of which eleven scenarios — `readByKey`, `scrollWindow`, `filterTwoAxes`,
`consumerFloor`, `patchColumn`, `patchOutsideWindow`, `churnChain`,
`churnShared`, `churnSharedDeep`, `churnWide`, `mountFloor` — carry all three
points. Two things bound
what it may be quoted for, and both are recorded in the artifacts themselves:
the series is **incomplete**, and every run in it was taken with the load gate
raised — to **3.5** foreign runnable processes on the 22 `small`/`wide` pieces,
and to **25** on the 34 `default`-point ones — against the harness's own
default of **0.5** (`packages/bench/src/harness/load.ts`,
`DEFAULT_MAX_FOREIGN_LOAD`). Read `packages/bench/measurements/README.md` for what
a raised gate does to a comparison before quoting anything out of that directory.

Everything outside that series has **no number at all**. No strategy of any shipped
fork has a measured price, so no consumer can pick with the numbers in front of
them.

The one quantity that needs no measurement, because it is arithmetic rather than
a reading: emptying a bucket one slot at a time on an array-driven bucket costs
n(n-1)/2 element moves — **499 500** for a thousand — which is why a bucket content service's `writeSlotContent`
and `clearSlotContent` go through one `drainSlots`. Counted, not timed, in
`packages/core/src/engine/bucket/array/tests/everyone-out-at-once-and-not-one-at-a-time.test.ts`, which
also pins `drainSlots` at zero element writes.

Fast properties are checked, not timed. Every slot kind is one object literal with
every field present at birth; per-index state lives in the `indexKeys` array;
nothing adds a field to a slot later or deletes one; neither entity writer
`delete`s a column — it writes `undefined`, in place or into a spread copy. So every slot of a kind keeps one V8
hidden class through holds, effects, moves between buckets, patches and release
deadlines, and an entity keeps its own when a column leaves or arrives —
`packages/core/tests/what-v8-keeps-on-fast-properties.test.ts` asks V8 directly
through its own natives for fast properties and a shared map, and
`packages/core/tests/how-many-shapes-reach-the-write-door.test.ts` pins three slot
shapes at the write door, one below V8's polymorphic ceiling, and four at `holdSlot`,
at it, a computed column slot among them as a computed slot. What that saves per read is not measured. An
entity handed in with a few hundred fields is in dictionary mode before it
arrives.

The goal the measurement work serves: prove that **for every typical task there
is a combination of shipped strategies whose cost is at or below the hand-written
floor**, on the same tasks every framework in `packages/bench` is measured on. A
ratio above 1.00 is a loss only when no strategy combination reaches the floor.
